A320 SIM syllabus

MFTD/FBS
FFS

Course overview

18 sessions · MFTD/FBS 2–9 and FFS 1–10. Choose a session to compare exercises, flight setup and the session schedule for both trainees.

Trainee A emphasis

Managed climb and FMGC work, APU MEL and crossbleed starts, fuel-feed and IDG faults, ADR/IR faults, dual-engine failure, overweight approaches, and severe engine damage.

Trainee B emphasis

Ground-speed mini and braking, start-valve and smoke events, FMGC resets, sidestick priority, emergency electrical configuration, contaminated-runway and gear work, and gravity gear extension.

Common ground

Both cover takeoffs, approaches, landings, stalls, UPRT and one-engine-inoperative handling. FFS 8 has the same UPRT exercise sequence; FFS 10 has the same skill-test exercise sequence, with different weather.

Failure procedures

Engine failure · MFTD/FBS 8

2 procedures in this group — choose one

ENG 1(2) FAIL

Amber cautionLAND ASAP (amber) Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

An engine fails after V1 (or at go-around). Below 400 ft the PF only flies: rudder to centre the beta target, 12.5° then SRS, gear up. At 400 ft the PF orders ECAM ACTIONS until the engine is secured, then calls STOP ECAM to level off at EO acceleration altitude, clean up and set MCT at green dot. CONTINUE ECAM takes the PM to the STATUS page, where the PF stops the ECAM again for the after-takeoff flow and a relight decision.

In MFTD/FBS 8 Trainee A: after V2 on takeoff. Trainee B: at go-around.

Rotation
≈3°/s to 12.5° pitch
Minimum speed
V2 (SRS: V2 to V2 +15 kt)
READ & DO from
400 ft AGL
Relight wait
30 s after ENG FAIL
Takeoff thrust
10 min max
Final takeoff segment

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Engine core speed below idle with the ENG MASTER lever ON and the ENG FIRE pb not pushed.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Flameout causes include fuel starvation, volcanic ash/sand, heavy rain/hail/icing, bird strike, engine stall, control malfunction.
  • Suspect damage with two or more of: EGT above red line, rotor speed mismatch or no rotation, vibration/buffet, abnormal oil pressure/temperature, hydraulic loss, repeated stalls.
  • Takeoff with an engine failure: the blue beta target replaces the sideslip index; lateral normal law gives some rudder, the pilot completes it to centre the target.
  • When an engine failure is detected the FMGS gives engine-out predictions and deletes pre-selected speeds.
FCTM technique
  • Aircraft handling first: stabilise pitch, speed and path before the ECAM.
  • Failure above V2: keep the SRS attitude; minimum speed V2.
  • "Secure the engine" = ENG MASTER OFF (no damage), AGENT 1 DISCH (damage), fire out or AGENT 2 DISCH (fire).
  • With AP engaged the rudder trim is managed by the AP; release rudder pedal pressure.
  • Do not exceed the EO maximum acceleration altitude if acceleration is delayed.
  • In cruise: MCT, A/THR off, set heading, standard strategy M.78/300 kt, descend to EO recovery altitude, never below green dot.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT — No damage, relight considered. See the ENG RELIGHT brief.
  • ONE ENGINE INOPERATIVE — GO-AROUND — Engine failure at go-around. TOGA + prompt rudder; SRS or 12.5°; GA TRK — terrain.
Gaps and omissions
  • Thrust-malfunction and on-ground branches of ENG FAIL are not shown in the flow; this brief covers the in-flight case.
  • Callout wording differs slightly between sources: FCOM "ECAM ACTION" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETE" vs PDP and FCTM "ECAM ACTIONS" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETED". The PDP is a generic Airbus tutorial; FCOM wording is shown where both exist.
  • HS-TO-only versions omitted (FCOM P 87–89 and P 174–183/226).

ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A

A QRH (paper) procedure for restarting an engine that failed without damage. Check the relight envelope, set the failed engine to IDLE/IGN with crossbleed open, then ENG MASTER ON and watch N2/EGT — there is no automatic start abort in flight.

Light-up
within 30 s of fuel flow
Failed attempt
N2 < 50 % within 70 s
Before retry
wait 30 s (drain)
Windmill relight
≥ 270 kt

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Decide
  1. 1.1 PF
    • Only with no engine damage, no fire shutdown and no risk of fire
    • Choose relight type from the envelope (starter-assisted / windmill)
  2. 1.2 PM

2Order the QRH procedure

    • PF orders “(name) PROCEDURE”, then flies and communicates
  2. 2.2 PM

3Set up
  1. 3.1 PM
    • ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFF
    • THR LEVER (affected engine)Check IDLE
  2. 3.2 PF
    • Thrust lever of the affected engine: confirm IDLE
  3. 3.3 PM
    • ENG MODE selIGN
    • X BLEEDOPEN
    • WING ANTI ICE (for starter assist)OFF
4Start
  1. 4.1 PM
    • ENG MASTER (affected engine)ON

  2. 4.2 PF

      • X BLEEDAUTO

      • ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFF
      • Wait 30 s before a new start (drain)
    • ENG RELIGHT PROCEDURE COMPLETED
From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

ENG RELIGHT — IN FLIGHT
  1. No attempt if engine damage, if shut down for fire, or if a relight may cause fire.
  2. ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFF
  3. THR LEVER (affected engine)Check IDLE
  4. ENG MODE selIGN
  5. X BLEEDOPENOutside the windmilling envelope the FADEC opens the starter valve.
  6. WING ANTI ICE (for starter assist)OFF
  7. ENG MASTER (affected engine)ON
  8. ENG PARAMETERS (N2, EGT)MONITOR
  9. AUTOMATIC START ABORT NOT AVAIL
  10. When idle reached (ENG AVAIL):
  11. ENG MODE selNORM
  12. TCAS MODE selTA/RA
  13. X BLEEDAUTO
  14. Affected SYSRESTORE
  15. If no relight:
  16. ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFFWait 30 s before attempting a new start.
  17. If N2 does not increase above 50 % within 70 s, consider the relight unsuccessful; consider a windmill relight at minimum 270 kt.

ZoneRelight type

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. QRH procedure, considered from ENG 1(2) FAIL (no damage) or STATUS "CONSIDER ENG RELIGHT".

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The relight can be a windmilling start or a starter-assisted relight using bleed from the other engine.
  • Unlike a ground auto start, the crew must act on an abnormal start.
FCTM technique
  • The crew may stop the relight procedure at any time if the situation requires (time, distance to fly).
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FAIL — Calls for ENG RELIGHT CONSIDER if no damage. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • Envelope boundaries are graphical — use the QRH chart; values are not transcribed.
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM P 1–3/226, QRH 19.06A).

ANTI ICE STBY PITOT or L(R) STAT or AOA · MFTD/FBS 8

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A

An amber caution: one standby probe (pitot, left or right static, or AOA) has lost its heating. There is no action line — it is crew awareness. If the standby instruments are being used, monitor the air data closely, because an unheated probe can ice up.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. The heating system of the corresponding standby probe has failed.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • Electrical heating protects pitot probes, static ports, AOA probes and TAT probes. Three independent Probe Heat Computers control the Captain, F/O and STBY probes.
  • Probes are heated automatically in flight or with one engine running, or manually with PROBE/WINDOW HEAT ON.
  • ADR 3 and the standby speed use the same probe; STBY SPD UNCERTAIN appears when ADR 3 speed is declared faulty.
Related procedures
  • [MEM] UNRELIABLE SPEED INDICATION — If standby/ADR 3 speed becomes erroneous. See the Unreliable speed brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • No FCTM technique for this caution in the supplied FCTM.
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM P 40/42).

ENG 1(2) FIRE (ON GROUND) · RTO

Red warning Practised by Trainee A

An engine fire warning below V1: the Captain calls STOP and rejects the takeoff. Once stopped, the crew secures the aircraft, discharges both agents and — if the fire is not extinguished — goes to the QRH EMER EVAC procedure.

In MFTD/FBS 8 Engine fire below V1, not extinguishable — leads to the evacuation.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Fire detected by both loops, or by one loop with the other faulty, or both loops ruptured within 5 s.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • ECAM inhibits non-essential alerts from 80 kt to 1 500 ft (or 2 min after lift-off): any alert in this period is significant.
  • Above 100 kt and below V1 the Captain is go-minded; a fire alert or severe damage is one of the few reasons to reject.
FCTM technique
  • The Captain keeps a hand on the thrust levers until V1, whether PF or PM.
  • "STOP" both confirms the decision and states the Captain has control — the only handover without "I have control".
  • Rejected before 72 kt or autobrake inoperative: reduce thrust and apply full pedal braking until stopped.
  • After an A/BRK MAX stop, disarm ground spoilers before taxiing; do not vacate until it is clear no evacuation is needed.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] EMER EVAC — Fire not extinguishable. See the EMER EVAC brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • Company (THAI) phraseology is used instead of the generic Airbus wording: PA “CABIN CREW, AT YOUR STATIONS” (PDP: “ATTENTION! CREW AT STATIONS”) and ATC call sign “THA ___” (PDP: “AIRBUS ___”).

ENG 1(2) FIRE (IN FLIGHT)

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee B

A red engine-fire warning in flight. Once the path is safe the crew applies the fire procedure without delay: idle, master off, fire pb, agent 1 after 10 s, and agent 2 if the fire is still there 30 s later. When the fire is out, ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN follows; LAND ASAP. In cruise, the engine-out drift-down strategy is flown around the drill.

In MFTD/FBS 8 Fire extinguished after the second agent.

  1. LAND ASAP (red)
  2. THR LEVER (AFFECTED)IDLE
  3. ENG MASTER (AFFECTED)OFFLP and HP valves close.
  4. ENG FIRE P/B (AFFECTED)PUSHAural stops; light stays on until the fire is out; FADEC no longer supplied.
  5. AGENT 1 AFTER 10 SDISCHDelay lets N1 decrease; automatic countdown on ECAM.
  6. ATCNOTIFY
  7. IF FIRE AFTER 30 S:
  8. AGENT 2DISCH
  9. Associated: ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN — do not attempt to restart the engine.

FCOM PRO-ABN-ENG P 91/226 · PDF 3338

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Fire detected by both loops, or by one loop with the other faulty, or both loops ruptured within 5 s.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Thrust and engine parameters can stay normal early in a fire — not a reason to delay the procedure.
  • Discharge agents while the alert and a local warning remain. The FIRE light stays on until the fire is out, even after agent 2.
FCTM technique
  • If the alert and local warnings disappear after agent 1 (or 1+2), the fire procedure can be stopped and the remaining ECAM done as usual.
  • Consider LAND ASAP: land at the nearest airport where a safe landing can be performed.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN — Associated procedure. X BLEED SHUT, WING ANTI ICE OFF, avoid icing (fire pb pushed); TCAS TA; STATUS: CAT 3 SINGLE.
  • ENGINE FAILURE IN CRUISE — drift-down strategy — Fire (or any engine failure) at cruise level. MCT, A/THR off; Standard strategy M.78/300 kt to the EO LRC ceiling; Never below green dot.
Gaps and omissions
  • STATUS of the fire case is that of ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN (see the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief).

A QRH procedure. The F/O runs the actions up to the decision point while the Captain decides. The decision to evacuate is irreversible once ordered; until then it can be deferred or cancelled.

FCOM PRO-ABN-MISC P 16/30 · PDF 3811 · QRH C2 · PDF 294

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Applied when considering an emergency evacuation, or when required by the ECAM (e.g. ENG FIRE on ground: EMER EVAC PROC APPLY).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Typical causes: uncontrollable fire, smoke/fumes — during taxi, after a rejected takeoff or after landing.
  • With engines stopped only the right dome light works; on batteries the crew seats must be moved mechanically.
FCTM technique
  • "CABIN CREW (PA)…ALERT" tells the cabin the flight crew still controls the situation and prevents an unwanted cabin-initiated evacuation (done in the RTO flow).
  • ΔP check does not apply after an RTO: at least one automatic pressure system is required for departure.
  • "EVACUATION…INITIATE" = notify cabin crew, press EVAC COMMAND, advise ATC — preferably in this order.
  • Until the order is given the evacuation can be deferred or cancelled; once ordered it is irreversible.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FIRE (ON GROUND) · RTO — Engine fire on ground not extinguished. AGENT 1+2 DISCH → EMER EVAC PROC APPLY.
Gaps and omissions
  • Company (THAI) phraseology is used instead of the generic Airbus/FCOM wording: “CABIN CREW, AT YOUR STATIONS” (PDP/FCOM: “ATTENTION CREW AT STATIONS”) and “REMAIN SEATED, RESUME NORMAL DUTIES” (PDP/FCOM: “CABIN CREW and PASSENGERS REMAIN SEATED”).
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM PRO-ABN-MISC P 15/30).

FMGC 1(2) FAULT · FMGC 1+2 FAULT · MFTD/FBS 8

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee B

One FMGC failing leaves the other running everything (single mode): recover the AP on the other side, put both NDs on the same range and mode, and reset the failed FMGC from the QRH. Both FMGCs failing drops AP/FD and A/THR: try to re-engage them, otherwise fly manual thrust with FDs off and TRK/FPA, tune navaids on the RMPs, reset per QRH, and use MCDU BACK UP NAV.

In MFTD/FBS 8 Demo FMGC 1 and FMGC 2 failure, then FMGC 1+2 fault reset with the QRH System Reset table.

C/B pull
10 s, then push
Re-engage AP/FD
1 min after PLEASE WAIT clears
Resets
only per QRH table

Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Single FMGC failure (demo FMGC 1 / FMGC 2)
  1. 1.1 PF
    • Golden rules: fly, navigate, communicate; appropriate level of automation
    • AP1 and FD1 lost (affected side) → engage AP2; A/THR stays
    • Do not use the MCDU until PLEASE WAIT clears
  2. 1.2 PM
    • Select the same range and mode on both NDs (SET OFFSIDE RNG/MODE → OFFSIDE FM CONTROL)
    • Failed-side MCDU reverts to MCDU MENU; exit by selecting any MCDU page (healthy FM in force)
    • Both FDs now driven by the operative FMGC; any MCDU entry goes to it
2Reset the failed FMGC (QRH 02.12)
  1. 2.1 PM
    • CONFIRM?
    • Before each C/B action: PM points to the C/B, PF answers “CONFIRMED”
  2. 2.2 PF
    • CONFIRMED
  3. 2.3 PM
    • If FMGC 1 is affected
      • AP 2 pbON
      • FD 1 pbOFF
      • C/B B02 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 1) on 49VUPULL — wait 10 s — PUSH
    • If FMGC 2 is affected
      • AP 1 pbON
      • FD 2 pbOFF
      • C/B M17 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 2) on 121VUPULL — wait 10 s — PUSH
  4. 2.4 PF
    • Wait 1 min after PLEASE WAIT disappears before re-engaging FD/AP of the reset FMGC
3Dual FMGC failure
  1. 3.1 PF
    • FMGC auto-reset may occur; when the ECAM is confirmed apply ECAM/OEB actions and the abnormal task sharing
    • AP/FD and A/THR disconnect — try to re-engage both
    • Not recovered: move thrust levers for manual thrust; FDs OFF; TRK/FPA (bird)
  2. 3.2 PM
    • Tune navaids on the RMPs
    • Check the QRH system reset table, then reset per QRH 02.12
    • Not recovered: MCDU MENU → BACK UP NAV (simplified IRS/GPS navigation)

AUTO FLT — BOTH MCDU LOCKED OR BLANK OR FMGC MALFUNCTION (in flight)
  1. If FMGC 1 is affected:
  2. AP 2 pbON
  3. FD 1 pbOFF
  4. C/B B02 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 1) — on 49VUPULL
  5. Wait 10 s

  8. If FMGC 2 is affected:

  10. FD 2 pbOFF
  11. C/B M17 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 2) — on 121VUPULL
  12. Wait 10 s
  13. C/B M17 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 2)PUSH
  14. Caution Wait 1 min after the PLEASE WAIT message disappears from the MCDU, before engaging or re-engaging the FD and the AP of reset FMGC.
  15. If the FMGC reset is not successful, consider FMGC reset with engines not running.

QRH 02.12A · PDF 65 · QRH 02.12B · PDF 66

System reset — general
In flight
  • Reset authorized only if an ECAM/OEB/FCOM/QRH procedure requests it, or the alert/malfunction is listed and authorized in the system reset table.
  • Only one reset at a time unless the procedure says otherwise.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Single or dual FMGC failure. Handled from the FCTM technique, the FMGS degraded modes and the QRH system reset table (AUTO FLT — BOTH MCDU LOCKED OR BLANK OR FMGC MALFUNCTION).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Single mode: the failed FMGC shows OPP FMGC IN PROCESS; its ND shows MAP NOT AVAIL / SET OFFSIDE RNG/MODE, or OFFSIDE FM CONTROL when ranges match.
  • If one FMGC fails, the remaining FMGC controls the radio receivers on both sides; if both fail, use the RMPs.
  • BACK UP NAV gives flight planning, position from IRS/GPIRS, F-PLN on ND and sequencing — no AP/FD NAV mode.
FCTM technique
  • Single failure: recover flight-plan display on the affected ND by using the same range as the opposite ND; consider a reset per QRH.
  • Dual failure: if the FG part is still available, the AP may remain engaged and revert to HDG-V/S or TRK-FPA (FG standard dependent).
Gaps and omissions
  • No ECAM procedure titled FMGC 1(2) FAULT exists in the supplied FCOM; the brief uses FCTM, FCOM DSC and QRH reset content.
  • FCOM DSC-22_20-40-10 manual FMGC reset / resynchronisation not expanded here.

SDAC/FWC faults · MFTD/FBS 8

2 procedures in this group — choose one

FWS SDAC 1 + 2 FAULT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee B

Both system data acquisition concentrators are lost, so some amber cautions will not appear. Red warnings, engine and fuel parameters and slat/flap positions stay on the upper ECAM. Watch the overhead panel for local fault lights; only the ENG, FUEL, F/CTL and WHEEL (gear position) SD pages remain. SDAC is not in the QRH system reset table: no reset in flight; on ground, the standard reset procedure may be used.

In MFTD/FBS 8 Demonstration with reset. The QRH allows no SDAC reset in flight, only the standard reset on ground (see Reset rule).

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Both SDAC 1 and SDAC 2 have failed.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • QRH system reset rule: in flight, a reset is authorized only if the ECAM/OEB/FCOM/QRH procedure requests it, or if the alert is listed and authorized in the system reset table; on ground, also if the affected system is NOT listed in the table. In all other cases: RESET NOT AUTHORIZED. Only one reset at a time.

Gaps and omissions
  • SDAC is not in the QRH system reset table, so the general rule (QRH 02.01A) applies: no reset in flight, standard reset on ground. The SDAC C/B identities are not given in the supplied QRH. No FCTM technique for this alert in the supplied manuals.

FWS FWC 1 + 2 FAULT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee B

Both flight warning computers are lost: no ECAM cautions or warnings, no aural warnings, no master lights, no altitude alert, STATUS, auto callouts or memos. ECAM system pages remain, so the crew checks the overhead panel and SD pages more often than usual. The procedure requests no reset, and the QRH reset table lists only a single FWC fault (FWS FWC 1(2) FAULT), so resetting FWC 1 + 2 is not authorized in flight.

In MFTD/FBS 8 Demonstration with reset. The QRH authorizes no reset for FWC 1 + 2; its FWC 1(2) reset is for a single FWC only (see No reset).

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Both FWC 1 and FWC 2 have failed, or communication between the FWC and the EIS is lost.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • QRH system reset rule: in flight, a reset is authorized only if the ECAM/OEB/FCOM/QRH procedure requests it, or if the alert is listed and authorized in the system reset table; on ground, also if the affected system is NOT listed in the table. In all other cases: RESET NOT AUTHORIZED. Only one reset at a time.
Related procedures
  • FWS SDAC 1 + 2 FAULT — Related FWS failure. See the SDAC brief.
  • FWS FWC 1(2) FAULT (single FWC) — A different alert. Only this single-FWC fault is in the QRH system reset table; it does not apply to FWC 1 + 2.. If FWS FWC 1 FAULT: C/B F01 (FWS / FWC1 / SPLY) on 49VU PULL, wait 5 s, PUSH; If FWS FWC 2 FAULT: C/B Q07 (EIS / FWC2 / SPLY) on 121VU PULL, wait 5 s, PUSH; On ground, wait 50 s after pushing the C/Bs; STATUS: CAT 3 SINGLE ONLY.
Gaps and omissions
  • No FCTM technique for this alert in the supplied FCTM.
  • On ground, QRH 02.01A also authorizes a reset when the affected system is not listed in the reset table. The FWC is listed (as FWS FWC 1(2) FAULT), so the supplied manuals give no reset for FWC 1 + 2 on ground either.

UNRELIABLE SPEED INDICATION · SEVERE TURBULENCE · MFTD/FBS 8

Memory items Practised by Trainee B

If the safe conduct of the flight is affected, fly the memory pitch/thrust, then level off and stabilise using the QRH pitch/thrust tables while the PM identifies and isolates the faulty ADR. This brief also compares the QRH table with the Severe Turbulence table: unreliable speed gives pitch and thrust to fly without trusting speed, while severe turbulence keeps the AP on and sets a target speed/Mach with a reference N1.

In MFTD/FBS 8 Compare the QRH Unreliable Speed tables with the QRH Severe Turbulence table.

Below THR RED ALT
15° / TOGA
THR RED ALT – FL 100
10° / CLB
Above FL 100
5° / CLB
Level-off pitch, clean
4° (≤ FL 250) · 3° (above)
Severe turbulence target
275 kt · M.76 at FL 330+

Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Memory items (if safe flight is affected)
  1. 1.1 PF + PM
    • UNRELIABLE SPEED
  2. 1.2 PF
    • AP / A/THR / FDOFF
    • PITCH/THRUST15°/TOGA · 10°/CLB · 5°/CLB
    • FLAPSMAINTAIN (CONF FULL → CONF 3)
    • SPEEDBRAKESCHECK RETRACTED
    • L/GUP
    • Once pitch/thrust are stable, go to the QRH without delay — memory values held too long can exceed speed limits
  3. 1.3 PM
    • Confirm discrepancies: STBY vs own PFD, own PFD vs PF PFD
    • Rely on the STALL warning (AOA-based)
2Level off (QRH procedure)
  1. 2.1 PF
    • At or above MSA / circuit altitude: level off for troubleshooting
    • APOFF
    • FDs OFF
  2. 2.2 PM
    • FDsOFF
  3. 2.3 PF
    • A/THROFF
    • SPEEDBRAKESCHECK RETRACTED
    • PITCH/THRUSTAPPLY
  4. 2.4 PM
    • PITCH/THRUSTDETERMINE FROM QRH TABLE
  5. 2.5 PF
    • LEVEL OFFPERFORM
    • Pitch above target → more thrust; below → less thrust. Altitude unreliable → GPS altitude (MCDU GPS MONITOR)
    • Below FL 250: BUSS (activation not reversible)
    • If needed and reliable (bird reliable if baro altitude reliable)
      • BIRD ON
  6. 2.6 PM
    • After “BIRD ON”
      • TRK/FPA (BIRD)SELECT
  7. 2.7 PF + PM
    • RESPECT STALL WARNING
3Flight path stabilised
  1. 3.1 PF
    • AP / A/THROFF
  2. 3.2 PM
    • FDsOFF
  3. 3.3 PF
    • SPEEDBRAKESCHECK RETRACTED
    • FLIGHT PATHKEEP STABILIZED
4Identify the faulty ADR
  1. 4.1 PF
    • Advise ATC without delay (altitude may be wrong)
  2. 4.2 PM
    • PROBE/WINDOW HEATON
    • ALL SPEED INDICATIONSCROSSCHECK
    • ADR3 and STBY speed use the same probe
    • At least one ADR confirmed reliable
      • RELIABLE AIR DATAUSE
      • UNRELIABLE ADR pb(s)OFF
    • Cannot identify / all affected — above FL 250
      • KEEP ONE ADR ON
      • TWO ADR pbsOFF
      • ATC/XPDRALT RPTG OFF
      • Flight continuation: pitch/thrust tables
    • Below FL 250, speed still unreliable
      • ALL ADR pbsOFF
      • SPEEDFLY THE GREEN (BUSS)
      • NAV ADR 1+2+3 FAULT ECAMAPPLY
    • ADR pbs are switched off with the pb — not the rotary selector
5Continue the flight
  1. 5.1 PF
    • Fly pitch/thrust by phase — climb, cruise, descent, approach — early stabilised approach
  2. 5.2 PM
    • Read the table for each phase; radome damage → +5 % N1, fuel flow +27 %
6Compare: Severe turbulence (QRH 25.08)
  1. 6.1 PF
    • SEAT BELTSON
    • KEEP AUTO PILOT ON; excessive thrust variations → disconnect A/THR
    • Target 275 kt (FL 200–310) / M.76 (FL 330+), 250 kt at FL 150 and below
    • Consider descending to or below OPT FL for buffet margin
  2. 6.2 PM
    • SPEED AND THRUSTADJUST (table N1 by FL / weight)
    • For approach
      • A/THRON
      • USE MANAGED SPEED

  4. If excessive thrust variations:

  6. DESCENT TO OR BELOW OPT FLCONSIDERIncreases the margin to buffet.
  7. For approach:
  8. A/THRON
  9. USE MANAGED SPEED

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. ADR CHECK PROC APPLY on ECAM (e.g. NAV ADR DISAGREE), or crew suspicion: speed discrepancies, fluctuating IAS/altitude, abnormal pitch/thrust/speed correlation, abnormal AP/FD/A/THR behaviour, stall/overspeed warning contradicting IAS.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Most likely cause: obstruction of pitot and/or static probes; probes rarely clog identically, so the first sign is usually a discrepancy between CAPT PFD, F/O PFD and STBY.
  • Systems vote across three ADRs; two consistent but wrong ADRs can out-vote the correct one (e.g. two pitots blocked the same way).
  • Above FL 250 unreliable speed is mostly temporary (water/ice) and clears in minutes; at low altitude it is mostly permanent.
  • Erroneous barometric altitude affects FPV, V/S and the transponder — advise ATC.
FCTM technique
  • Two objectives: fly the aircraft, then identify and isolate the affected ADR(s).
  • Apply the memory items when in doubt about flying safely in the short term with current parameters.
  • Rely on the STALL warning — it is AOA-based and not affected by erroneous airspeed.
  • Do not instinctively reject an outlier ADR: two or even three ADRs can give identical but erroneous data.
  • Change one parameter at a time (speed, altitude or configuration); GPS altitude is on the MCDU GPS MONITOR page.
  • Approach: early stabilised approach; configure wings level using back-up speeds (VMAX = VFE/VMO, VMIN = VSW).
Related procedures
  • NAV ADR 1+2+3 FAULT — All ADRs switched off below FL 250. Apply the ECAM procedure.

ELEC EMER CONFIG · MFTD/FBS 8

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee B

Both AC main buses are lost. The RAT drives the emergency generator, leaving essentially CM1 instruments, VHF1/HF1/ATC1 and alternate law (direct law with gear down). CM1 flies manually as PF while the PM works the ECAM; after STATUS the crew uses the QRH summary to decide, prepare and fly the approach at no less than 140 kt.

SYS REMAINING — highlights
On EMER GEN / on batteries
  • ND1 lost on batteries; PFD1, upper ECAM, DMC 1/3, SDAC 1/FWC 1 normal (lost below 50 kt on ground).
  • IR, ADR, VOR, MMR, DME, ATC N°1 only (DME, ATC, ADF lost on batteries). IR2/IR3 lost 5 min after main generators fail unless IR3 replaces IR1.
  • FMGC, MCDU, FAC N°1 only (lost on batteries); FCU ch 1 only.
  • ELAC, SEC, FCDC, SFCC N°1 only.
  • HF1 and CVR lost on batteries; VHF1, RMP1, ACPs, interphone normal.
  • ENG FIRE EXT bottle 1 only; IGNITION A only; MAN PRESS CTL inop.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2 are not supplied.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 8.

  • RAT extends automatically when AC BUS 1 and 2 are lost above 100 kt; blue hydraulics drive the EMER GEN, which supplies AC ESS and (via ESS TR) DC ESS.
  • If the RAT stalls, the network transfers to the batteries and static inverter, and AC/DC SHED ESS are shed. On ground: DC BAT BUS connected below 100 kt; AC ESS shed below 50 kt (all displays lost).
  • EMER ELEC PWR MAN ON (guarded): manual RAT extension; EMER GEN couples 3 s after the RAT supplies it. Red FAULT light: EMER GEN not supplying power.
  • Remaining: FLY — PFD1, alternate law; NAVIGATE — ND1, FMGC1, RMP1, VOR1/ILS1, DME1; COMMUNICATE — VHF1, HF1, ATC1. On batteries FAC1 and FMGC1 are also lost.
  • Secondary failures are inhibited on the ECAM in ELEC EMER CONFIG.
FCTM technique
  • Red LAND ASAP, but approaching a poorly equipped airfield in marginal weather is unwise; prolonged flight is not recommended.
  • A clear reading of STATUS is essential to sequence actions during the approach.
  • Complex procedure: use the QRH summary after the ECAM procedure.
  • BSCUs lost: no NWS or anti-skid; alternate braking with yellow hydraulics up to 1 000 PSI; no reversers.
  • RA 1+2 lost with their automatic callouts — the PM makes the callouts.
  • Approaching 50 kt on the landing roll, all display units are lost.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] GRAVITY FUEL FEEDING — ECAM line PROC : GRVTY FUEL FEEDING. ENG MODE SEL IGN; avoid negative G; Gravity feed ceiling (HS-TXA..TXT): current FL if > 30 min above FL 300; FL 300 if < 30 min; FL 150 or 7 000 ft above departure if FL 300 never exceeded; FL 100 for JET B; Gravity feed ceiling (HS-TXU): FL 360 / FL 260 / FL 150 or 7 000 ft; At the ceiling: FUEL X FEED OFF.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Associated procedure. Protections lost except manoeuvre protection; MAX SPEED 320 KT; Respect stall warning in TAWS manoeuvres.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — At landing gear extension. MAN PITCH TRIM USE; MAX SPEED 320/.77; Manoeuvre with care; manual thrust recommended.

Failure procedures

ENG 1(2) START FAULT · MFTD/FBS 9

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A

A hot start shows as ENG 1(2) START FAULT with EGT OVERLIMIT: EGT goes above 635 °C during the start. In an automatic start on ground the FADEC aborts the start and dry-cranks the engine by itself; the crew waits for the dry crank to finish, sets the ENG MASTER to OFF and, after the starter cools, does a manual start or reports a no-start to maintenance.

In MFTD/FBS 9 Followed by a manual engine start.

EGT limit · starting
635 °C
Pause between start cycles (ground)
15 s
Starter cooling
30 min after 3 failed cycles, 4 min continuous or 5 min cumulated crank
Dry crank (to clear fuel vapours)
30 s minimum
Manual start: ENG MASTER ON
N2 ≥ 16 % (max motoring) and 30 s after MAN START ON
Manual start max cycle
2 min

Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Automatic start (normal SOP)
  1. 1.1 PF
    • ENGINE 1 START
    • THRUST leversIDLE
    • ENG MODE selectorIGN/START
    • ENG 1 MASTER leverON
    • Master ON only after the amber crosses (except N1 and N2) and messages have gone
  2. 1.2 PF + PM
    • Watch the start: FF increases 30 s after master ON; EGT rises and N1 rises before 34 % N2 within 20 s of fuel on; igniters off at 43 % N2
    • An impending hot or hung start may be recovered by the FADEC without ECAM: dual ignition and fuel off then on within 0.5 s — no need to shut down
2Detection
  1. 2.1 PF + PM
    • First to notice: MASTER CAUTION reset
  2. 2.2 PM
    • ENG 1 START FAULT
    • Confirm on the EWD and ENG SD page: EGT OVERLIMIT is the hot-start case (EGT above 635 °C during start)
  3. 2.3 PF
    • ECAM ACTIONS
3ECAM actions — on ground, auto start
  1. 3.1 PF + PM
    • The FADEC has already shut off fuel and ignition and starts an automatic dry crank; ECAM shows AUTO CRANK IN PROGRESS
  2. 3.2 PM
    • AUTO CRANK IN PROGRESS(wait)
    • When dry crank process is completed
      • ENG MASTER (AFFECTED)OFF
      • Setting the master OFF confirms the automatic start abort
    • On ground the ENG MASTER crosscheck (CONFIRM?/CONFIRMED) is not required
  3. 3.3 PM
    • CLEAR ENG ?
  4. 3.4 PF
    • CLEAR ENG
  5. 3.5 PM
    • ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETE
4Decide
  1. 4.1 PF
    • After the starter cools, either do a manual start or report the “no start condition” to maintenance
    • Manual start is recommended after a start aborted for stall, EGT overlimit, LO START AIR PRESS, no N1 rotation or hung start
    • Respect the starter limits: 15 s between cycles; 30 min cooling after 3 failed cycles
5Manual start (SUP) — next attempt
  1. 5.1 PF + PM
    • Read the whole procedure first; then the PM reads and the PF acts on the controls
  2. 5.2 PF
    • THR LEVERSIDLE
    • ENG MODE selNORM THEN IGN/START
    • When all engine parameters (except N1 and N2) are available
      • ENG MAN START pb-swON
      • START VALVECHECK IN-LINE
      • N2 INCREASECHECK
      • OIL PRESS INCREASECHECK
    • When N2 reaches max motoring (16 % minimum) and 30 s after MAN START ON
      • ENG MASTERON

    • CHRONOSTART
    • Times the light-up
    • IGNITERS A AND BCHECK ON
    • FUEL FLOW INCREASECHECK
  4. 5.4 PF + PM
    • 20 s maximum after fuel flow increase
      • EGT INCREASECHECK
      • N1 INCREASE (before 34 % N2)CHECK
    • When N2 reaches 43 %
      • IGNITERS A AND B (at 43 % N2)CHECK OFF
      • START VALVE (slightly above 43 % N2)CHECK CROSS LINE
      • MAIN / SECONDARY ENG PARAMETERSCHECK NORMAL
  5. 5.5 PF
    • ENG MAN START pb-swOFF
    • ENG MODE selNORM
    • If a start malfunction is suspected or an engine ECAM alert triggers
      • Before master ON: ENG MAN START pb-sw OFF
      • After master ON: ENG MASTER OFF, then ENG MAN START pb-sw OFF; consider a dry crank before another attempt
      • ECAM ACTIONS

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

ECAM procedure
  1. ENG 1(2) IGNITION FAULT:
  2. The engine does not start within the 20 s (30 s in flight) that follow the ignition start.
  3. NO N1 ROTATION: or STALL or EGT OVERLIMIT or HUNG START:
  4. In flight:
  5. ENG MASTER (AFFECTED)OFFWait 30 s before attempting a new start (to drain the engine).
  6. On ground (auto start):
  7. If the engine does not start or in case of detected stall, potential EGT overheat or hung start, the FADEC will immediately shut off fuel and turn off ignition. After any start attempt that is not successful, a dry crank automatically occurs. At the end of the dry crank sequence, the start valve is closed.
  8. AUTO CRANK IN PROGRESS.
  9. When dry crank process is completed:
  10. ENG MASTER (AFFECTED)OFFConfirms automatic start abort. After the starter cools, for any subsequent attempt the crew must perform a manual start, or must report the “no start condition” to maintenance.
  11. With engine above idle, if EGT limit is exceeded ECAM requires to set engine master lever at OFF.
  12. On ground (manual start):
  13. ENG MASTER (AFFECTED)OFF
  14. MAN START (AFFECTED)OFF
  15. MODE SELCRANK
  16. MAN START (AFFECTED)ON
  17. ECAM does not display the last two lines. Dry crank the engine for 30 s. The start valve automatically reopens when N2 is below 10 %. After the starter cools: manual start, or report the “no start condition” to maintenance.
  18. LO START AIR PRESS:
  19. BLEED AIR SUPPLYCHECK
  20. THR LEVER NOT AT IDLE:
  21. THR LEVERIDLE

ENGINE VENTILATION (DRY CRANKING)
  1. On ground, after an unsuccessful manual start, or an unsuccessful automatic start not followed by an automatic dry crank.
  2. Before dry crank:
  3. ENG MASTER (affected engine)CHECK OFF
  4. ENG MODE selCHECK NORM
  5. ENG MAN START pb-sw (affected engine)CHECK OFF
  6. Dry crank:

FCOM PRO-NOR-SUP-ENG P 17/18 · PDF 4402

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Start fault due to no light up, engine stall, engine overtemperature, hung start, no N1 rotation, low start air pressure, or thrust lever not at idle.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

  • During engine start the ENG EGT OVER LIMIT alert is inhibited; if EGT goes above 635 °C the ENG 1(2) START FAULT [EGT OVERLIMIT] alert triggers instead.
  • The FADEC detects hot start, hung start, stall, failed light-up, low start air pressure and thrust lever not at idle; on ground with N2 below 50 % it closes the HP valve and start valve, turns off ignition and runs a 30 s dry crank to remove fuel vapours.
  • With residual EGT above 250 °C at start, an auto-crank function motors the engine until EGT is below 250 °C, with no crew message (very hot conditions or turn-arounds under 20 min).
  • Alert partly inhibited: phase 3 for no light-up, stall, overtemperature, hung start or low air pressure; phase 6 for thrust lever not at idle; phase 9 for no N1 rotation; fully inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7 and 8.
FCTM technique
  • Engine-start supplementary procedures: read the entire procedure first, then the PM reads the actions and the PF acts on the controls.
  • Manual start is recommended after a start aborted for stall, EGT overlimit, LO START AIR PRESS, no N1 rotation or hung start, and when an abort is expected (hot or high airfields, reduced EGT margin, weak ground air, tailwind above 10 kt).
  • In hot weather (OAT ≥ 40 °C) with residual EGT above 100 °C, dry crank 2 min before a manual start; starting with residual EGT above 250 °C is not recommended.
Related procedures
  • MANUAL ENGINE START (SUP) — Next start attempt after the auto start abort. THR LEVERS IDLE; MODE IGN/START, MAN START ON; ENG MASTER ON at N2 ≥ 16 % and 30 s; CHRONO, check light-up within 20 s; At 43 % N2: MAN START OFF, MODE NORM.
  • [QRH] ENGINE TAILPIPE FIRE — Internal fire can occur at start; EGT does not decrease after master OFF, or ground crew reports it. ENG MASTER OFF; Do not press the ENG FIRE pb (FADEC power needed for motoring); Air bleed press established, BEACON ON; MODE CRANK, MAN START ON until fire stopped.
Gaps and omissions
  • The HS-TX procedure has no separate HOT START heading (it exists only in the HS-TO variant, not used); a hot start appears as EGT OVERLIMIT.
  • No FCTM technique or PDP slide covers the start-fault handling itself; the PF/PM split for the ECAM part follows the general AOP-20/AOP-30-30 rules.
  • The SOP says “ENGINE 1 START” for engine 1; use the engine being started.

Engine fire · MFTD/FBS 9

ENG 1(2) FIRE (IN FLIGHT)

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee A

A red engine-fire warning in flight. Once the path is safe the crew applies the fire procedure without delay: idle, master off, fire pb, agent 1 after 10 s, and agent 2 if the fire is still there 30 s later. When the fire is out, ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN follows; LAND ASAP. In cruise, the engine-out drift-down strategy is flown around the drill.

In MFTD/FBS 9 Fire in cruise (FL 290): after the fire drill, drift down using the standard strategy (see Drift down).

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Fire detected by both loops, or by one loop with the other faulty, or both loops ruptured within 5 s.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Thrust and engine parameters can stay normal early in a fire — not a reason to delay the procedure.
  • Discharge agents while the alert and a local warning remain. The FIRE light stays on until the fire is out, even after agent 2.
FCTM technique
  • If the alert and local warnings disappear after agent 1 (or 1+2), the fire procedure can be stopped and the remaining ECAM done as usual.
  • Consider LAND ASAP: land at the nearest airport where a safe landing can be performed.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN — Associated procedure. X BLEED SHUT, WING ANTI ICE OFF, avoid icing (fire pb pushed); TCAS TA; STATUS: CAT 3 SINGLE.
  • ENGINE FAILURE IN CRUISE — drift-down strategy — Fire (or any engine failure) at cruise level. MCT, A/THR off; Standard strategy M.78/300 kt to the EO LRC ceiling; Never below green dot.
Gaps and omissions
  • STATUS of the fire case is that of ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN (see the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief).

ENGINE FAILURE IN CRUISE · drift-down strategy

Technique Practised by Trainee A

After an engine failure at cruise level the aircraft cannot hold its altitude. The PF sets MCT with A/THR off, sets a heading and determines the engine-out recovery altitude, then drifts down at M.78/300 kt (standard strategy) to the EO LRC ceiling, never below green dot. After an engine fire, the fire drill is done first and without delay.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Engine failure or engine shutdown (including after an engine fire) at cruise level.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Three strategies exist: standard, obstacle and fixed speed. Unless a specific procedure was set at dispatch (ETOPS, mountainous areas), the standard strategy is used.
FCTM technique
  • Engine failure in cruise: unless a dispatch procedure exists, use the standard strategy, M 0.78/300 kt to the REC MAX EO (LRC engine-out ceiling). Obstacle strategy: green dot to the drift-down ceiling, then standard when clear.
  • Do not hurry the ECAM actions in cruise — complete the drill correctly.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FIRE (IN FLIGHT) — When the engine failure is a fire. Fire drill first, without delay.
Gaps and omissions
  • No source puts the fire drill and the cruise strategy in one sequence. The fire procedure is applied without delay (FCTM), while the cruise flow sets MCT and A/THR off first and starts ECAM “when appropriate” (PDP). The brief keeps the fire drill first.

OVERWEIGHT LANDING

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A

An in-flight turn back or diversion may need a landing above the maximum landing weight. This is permitted only with the QRH OVERWEIGHT LANDING procedure. Plan a long, early-stabilised approach and use flaps FULL unless performance limits it. Turn the packs OFF (or supply them from the APU) for go-around thrust. Cross the threshold at VLS and touch down below 360 ft/min, then use max reverse early.

In MFTD/FBS 9 Overweight landing with LOC/DME vectors after the engine fire.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Immediate landing above maximum landing weight (in-flight turn back or diversion).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • In exceptional cases (in-flight turn back or diversion), an immediate landing above maximum landing weight is permitted, provided the pilot follows the overweight landing procedure.
  • Above MLW, structural considerations require the ability to touch down at 360 ft/min without damage.
FCTM technique
  • Fly a long straight-in approach or a wide visual pattern to configure early; VAPP at the FAF, VLS at the threshold.
  • VLS CONF 1+F may be higher than VLS CONF 3 + 5 kt in a CONF 1+F go-around: follow SRS, which accelerates to the displayed VLS.
  • Modulate braking with the runway available to avoid very hot brakes and tire deflation.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Fire detected by both loops, or by one loop with the other faulty, or both loops ruptured within 5 s.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • ECAM inhibits non-essential alerts from 80 kt to 1 500 ft (or 2 min after lift-off): any alert in this period is significant.
  • Above 100 kt and below V1 the Captain is go-minded; a fire alert or severe damage is one of the few reasons to reject.
FCTM technique
  • The Captain keeps a hand on the thrust levers until V1, whether PF or PM.
  • "STOP" both confirms the decision and states the Captain has control — the only handover without "I have control".
  • Rejected before 72 kt or autobrake inoperative: reduce thrust and apply full pedal braking until stopped.
  • After an A/BRK MAX stop, disarm ground spoilers before taxiing; do not vacate until it is clear no evacuation is needed.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] EMER EVAC — Fire not extinguishable. See the EMER EVAC brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • Company (THAI) phraseology is used instead of the generic Airbus wording: PA “CABIN CREW, AT YOUR STATIONS” (PDP: “ATTENTION! CREW AT STATIONS”) and ATC call sign “THA ___” (PDP: “AIRBUS ___”).

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Applied when considering an emergency evacuation, or when required by the ECAM (e.g. ENG FIRE on ground: EMER EVAC PROC APPLY).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Typical causes: uncontrollable fire, smoke/fumes — during taxi, after a rejected takeoff or after landing.
  • With engines stopped only the right dome light works; on batteries the crew seats must be moved mechanically.
FCTM technique
  • "CABIN CREW (PA)…ALERT" tells the cabin the flight crew still controls the situation and prevents an unwanted cabin-initiated evacuation (done in the RTO flow).
  • ΔP check does not apply after an RTO: at least one automatic pressure system is required for departure.
  • "EVACUATION…INITIATE" = notify cabin crew, press EVAC COMMAND, advise ATC — preferably in this order.
  • Until the order is given the evacuation can be deferred or cancelled; once ordered it is irreversible.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FIRE (ON GROUND) · RTO — Engine fire on ground not extinguished. AGENT 1+2 DISCH → EMER EVAC PROC APPLY.
Gaps and omissions
  • Company (THAI) phraseology is used instead of the generic Airbus/FCOM wording: “CABIN CREW, AT YOUR STATIONS” (PDP/FCOM: “ATTENTION CREW AT STATIONS”) and “REMAIN SEATED, RESUME NORMAL DUTIES” (PDP/FCOM: “CABIN CREW and PASSENGERS REMAIN SEATED”).
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM PRO-ABN-MISC P 15/30).

CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT · EMER DESCENT · MFTD/FBS 9

Memory items Practised by Trainee B

A red warning that the cabin altitude is too high. Above FL 160 the crew first does the EMER DESCENT memory items: oxygen masks, signs, descent with AP and A/THR, speed brakes. Then they do the ECAM read-and-do. Without structural damage they descend at maximum speed to FL 100 or MEA/MORA. Below FL 160 they apply the ECAM and start a normal descent.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Climb or descent: cabin altitude above the higher of 9 550 ft or airfield pressure altitude + 1 000 ft. Cruise: cabin altitude above 9 550 ft.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10.

  • Depressurization is identified by excessive and uncontrollable cabin altitude and rate of climb, the CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT alert, or all cabin oxygen masks dropping (independent pressure switch).
  • At idle, high speed and speed brakes out, the descent rate is about 7 000 ft/min: FL 390 to FL 100 takes about 4 min and 40 NM.
  • Suspect structural damage after a loud bang or a high cabin V/S.
  • HS-TXA..TXFOEB 61 root cause: the active CPC can show a wrong but normal-looking cabin altitude; the standby CPC triggers the alert. The crew may wrongly disregard the alert or delay the descent.
FCTM technique
  • Above FL 160: EMER DESCENT memory items first, then the ECAM. Below FL 160: ECAM procedure and a normal descent.
  • Two steps: memory items (PM monitors the FMA), then read & do (PF adjusts the settings).
  • At high levels, extend speed brakes while monitoring VLS so AoA protection does not retract them or disconnect the AP.
  • Structural damage suspected: SPEED/MACH pb to SPEED to stop the IAS increasing or to reduce speed; use speed brakes carefully.
  • Below FL 100 limit the descent rate to about 1 000 ft/min (PDP adds 500 ft/min for passenger comfort), except on approach.
Related procedures
  • CAB PR SYS 1+2 FAULT — Both CPCs failed — a common lead-in to the excess cabin altitude. MODE SEL MAN; MAN V/S CTL AS RQRD; keep aircraft altitude at or above cabin altitude; Final approach: V/S CTL FULL UP; ΔP zero before opening doors.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXFHS-TXG..TXU
OEB 61 (CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT)Applies: do the ECAM even if the CAB PRESS SD page looks normalNot applicable

The ECAM, memory items and QRH are the same for every HS-TX (Applicable to ALL). Only OEB 61 differs: it applies to HS-TXA..TXF.

Gaps and omissions
  • The ECAM has no explicit LAND ASAP for this alert; the diversion decision follows the general assess/decide step.
  • Callout wording comes from the PDP; the FCOM memory-item callout is “EMERGENCY DESCENT”.
  • The PDP says the EMER DESCENT (PA) line may not show on the ECAM on some aircraft; it is in the HS-TX FCOM procedure.

L/G GEAR NOT DOWNLOCKED · MFTD/FBS 9

Red warning Practised by Trainee B

A red warning on approach: one gear did not lock down 30 s after the lever went down. Fly first (the approach may be discontinued). Then the PM recycles the gear (lever up, wait for uplock and doors closed, lever down). If it is still not locked after 120 s, do the QRH L/G GRAVITY EXTENSION. If that fails, do LANDING WITH ABNORMAL L/G. One green triangle on each gear is enough to confirm the gear is down.

In MFTD/FBS 9 The approach is discontinued; the gear malfunction is removed after the go-around.

Information
  • If gravity extension unsuccessful, refer to [QRH] Landing with Abnormal L/G.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. One gear is not downlocked and L/G is selected down (landing gear sequence not completed after 30 s).

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 8.

  • Lever DOWN after gravity extension extinguishes the UNLK lights, avoids the L/G CTL message and minimises the risk of gear retraction on the ground.
  • If both LGCIUs failed, ECAM gear indications are lost; the LDG GEAR panel lights stay if LGCIU 1 is powered. No three green arrows may mean the handcrank is not at its stop.
  • Do not reset the free-fall system after a successful gravity extension (fluid loss, possible gear unlock); it may be reset on training flights.
FCTM technique
  • Check the WHEEL SD page and the LDG GEAR DN memo before any gravity extension or abnormal-gear landing: one green triangle on each gear is enough.
  • Landing with abnormal gear: land on any available gear rather than none; reduce weight; no ground spoilers or autobrake with a main gear abnormal; anti-skid off.
  • ENG masters OFF: nose gear abnormal — before nose impact; one main — at touchdown; both mains — in the flare. Fire pbs pushed when the aircraft has stopped.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] LANDING WITH ABNORMAL L/G — Gravity extension unsuccessful. Cabin crew, ATC NOTIFY; consider fuel reduction; LDG DIST up to +70 %; For approach: GPWS SYS OFF, handcrank back to normal, no autobrake, A/SKID & N/W STRG OFF, MAX BRAKE PR 1 000 PSI; At 500 ft AGL: BRACE FOR IMPACT ORDER; no reverse; ENG masters OFF per gear case; stopped: PARK BRK ON, all FIRE pb PUSH, AGENTS DISCH, evacuation as required.
Gaps and omissions
  • The ECAM says apply gravity extension if unsuccessful after 120 s; the QRH first allows up to 4 recycles (60 s each) if time permits, then 120 s. They are consistent — the QRH is the detailed version.
  • No PDP module and no FCTM text covers this warning or who turns the gravity handcrank; PF/PM split follows the general AOP-20/AOP-30 rules.
  • Discontinued approach technique is outside this brief (recovery manoeuvre).

ENG 1(2) FAIL · MFTD/FBS 9

Amber cautionLAND ASAP (amber) Practised by Trainee B

An engine fails after V1 (or at go-around). Below 400 ft the PF only flies: rudder to centre the beta target, 12.5° then SRS, gear up. At 400 ft the PF orders ECAM ACTIONS until the engine is secured, then calls STOP ECAM to level off at EO acceleration altitude, clean up and set MCT at green dot. CONTINUE ECAM takes the PM to the STATUS page, where the PF stops the ECAM again for the after-takeoff flow and a relight decision.

In MFTD/FBS 9 Engine failure with damage, after the discontinued approach.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Engine core speed below idle with the ENG MASTER lever ON and the ENG FIRE pb not pushed.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Flameout causes include fuel starvation, volcanic ash/sand, heavy rain/hail/icing, bird strike, engine stall, control malfunction.
  • Suspect damage with two or more of: EGT above red line, rotor speed mismatch or no rotation, vibration/buffet, abnormal oil pressure/temperature, hydraulic loss, repeated stalls.
  • Takeoff with an engine failure: the blue beta target replaces the sideslip index; lateral normal law gives some rudder, the pilot completes it to centre the target.
  • When an engine failure is detected the FMGS gives engine-out predictions and deletes pre-selected speeds.
FCTM technique
  • Aircraft handling first: stabilise pitch, speed and path before the ECAM.
  • Failure above V2: keep the SRS attitude; minimum speed V2.
  • "Secure the engine" = ENG MASTER OFF (no damage), AGENT 1 DISCH (damage), fire out or AGENT 2 DISCH (fire).
  • With AP engaged the rudder trim is managed by the AP; release rudder pedal pressure.
  • Do not exceed the EO maximum acceleration altitude if acceleration is delayed.
  • In cruise: MCT, A/THR off, set heading, standard strategy M.78/300 kt, descend to EO recovery altitude, never below green dot.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT — No damage, relight considered. See the ENG RELIGHT brief.
  • ONE ENGINE INOPERATIVE — GO-AROUND — Engine failure at go-around. TOGA + prompt rudder; SRS or 12.5°; GA TRK — terrain.
Gaps and omissions
  • Thrust-malfunction and on-ground branches of ENG FAIL are not shown in the flow; this brief covers the in-flight case.
  • Callout wording differs slightly between sources: FCOM "ECAM ACTION" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETE" vs PDP and FCTM "ECAM ACTIONS" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETED". The PDP is a generic Airbus tutorial; FCOM wording is shown where both exist.
  • HS-TO-only versions omitted (FCOM P 87–89 and P 174–183/226).

Failure procedures

ANTI ICE L(R) WINDOW · FFS 3

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A

An amber caution: the heating of the left or right cockpit side window has failed. There is no action line, only crew awareness, and STATUS shows L(R) WNDW HEAT as INOP SYS. A reset is allowed only on the ground, from the QRH reset table, when a spurious alert is likely (packs OFF with the OAT above 40 °C, or the windshield in direct sunlight). It is not authorized in flight.

In FFS 3 At preflight on EXT PWR; probe/window heat ON for cold weather.

Action
Crew awareness
Inhibited
phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8
Reset in flight
Not authorized
Ground reset
PACK 1+2 ON, wait 5 min, then C/B pull · 5 s · push

QRH 02.09A · PDF 62

STATUS
INOP SYS
  • L(R) WNDW HEAT

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when the heating system of the left(right) cockpit window is failed.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • Electrical heating protects the flight compartment windows (hot air protects slats and engine intakes).
  • Electrical heating anti-ices each windshield and defogs the cockpit side windows. Two independent WHCs, one on each side, regulate the system, protect it against overheating and indicate faults.
  • Window heating comes ON automatically when at least one engine is running or in flight, and manually before engine start when PROBE/WINDOW HEAT is switched ON.
  • The windshield heats at low power on ground and normal power in flight; the windows have only one heating level.
  • PROBE/WINDOW HEAT pb: AUTO = heated in flight, or on ground with one engine running (except TAT probes). ON = blue light, probes and windows heated permanently. Ensure the probe covers are removed before selecting ON.
  • Two different C/B sets: the reset uses the WHC C/Bs X13 / W13 (ANTI ICE / WHC / 1 / 2); the arcing procedure pulls the heating C/Bs ANTI ICE/WINDOWS L X14 / R W14 (122VU) or L/R WSHLD AF10 / AF03 (123VU).
Related procedures
  • Ground operations in cold weather (FCOM supplementary) — Cold-weather preflight selects PROBE/WINDOW HEAT ON, so window heat runs before engine start; this alert is not inhibited in that phase. WINDSHIELD AND UPPER COCKPIT FUSELAGE — ICE/SNOW REMOVED (caution: melted ice or snow could re-freeze on the forward fuselage near the probes); PROBE COVERS — CHECK REMOVED; PROBE/WINDOW HEAT — ON; After first engine start: PROBE/WINDOW HEAT — AUTO.
  • COCKPIT WINDSHIELD / WINDOW ARCING — Electrical arcing of a windshield/window, or burning smell or smoke from the bottom corner of a windshield. Affected WINDOW/WINDSHIELD ANTI ICE C/B — PULL; ANTI ICE/WINDOWS L C/B X14 · R C/B W14 [122VU]; ANTI ICE L WSHLD C/B AF10 · R WSHLD C/B AF03 [123VU].
Gaps and omissions
  • No FCTM technique and no PDP module for this caution; the flow uses the generic ECAM and QRH task sharing (FCTM AOP-30-30, PDP abnormal operations).
  • The QRH reset title covers WINDSHIELD (WINDOW), but its steps name only “If ANTI ICE L WINDSHIELD” / “If ANTI ICE R WINDSHIELD”. No separate step is given for the L(R) WINDOW alert.
  • Dispatch with window heat inoperative (MEL) is not covered by the supplied manuals.
  • HS-TO cold-weather AFTER START version omitted.

Failure procedures

IR faults · FFS 4

2 procedures in this group — choose one

NAV IR 1(2)(3) FAULT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A

An amber caution: one inertial reference has failed, so one side loses attitude and heading (red ATT flag on the PFD, red HDG flag on the ND). The only ECAM action is on the pedestal switching panel: ATT HDG to CAPT 3 for IR 1, F/O 3 for IR 2, plus the transponder system. If the IR FAULT light flashes, the IR may give attitude again in ATT mode through the QRH IR ALIGNMENT IN ATT MODE procedure.

In FFS 4 IR 1(2)(3) FAULT on the PM side, no ECAM.

IR 1 FAULT
ATT HDG CAPT 3 · XPDR SYS 2
IR 2 FAULT
ATT HDG F/O 3 · XPDR SYS 1
Approach capability
CAT 3 SINGLE ONLY
ATT mode heading
Reset about every 10 min

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when the IR 1(2)(3) is failed. Inhibited in flight phases 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 — not inhibited in phase 3 for NAV IR 1(2) FAULT, or for NAV IR 3 FAULT while the ADR 3 is in use.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • Each ADIRS has two parts (ADR and IRS) that may fail independently. The IRS part may fail totally or may be available in ATT mode.
  • A single NAV ADR FAULT or NAV IRS FAULT is a simple procedure: only action on the switching panel as indicated by the ECAM.
  • ATT HDG selector: NORM — ADIRU 1 supplies PFD 1/ND 1, ADIRU 2 supplies PFD 2/ND 2. CAPT 3 — IR 3 replaces IR 1. F/O 3 — IR 3 replaces IR 2.
  • If ADIRU 2 fails, the ATT HDG selector has to be set to F/O 3 to maintain side 1 / side 2 segregation; ADIRU 3 is then supplied by GPS receiver 2.
  • IR FAULT light flashing: attitude and heading may be recovered in ATT mode. Steady: the IR is lost.
  • In ATT mode the IR gives only attitude and heading (heading entered on the MCDU, reset about every 10 min). Once an IR is set from NAV to ATT or OFF in flight, NAV mode is lost for the rest of the flight; it is recovered only on ground by a complete alignment.
FCTM technique
  • The PF usually remains PF for the entire flight, unless the captain re-allocates tasks or a failure impacts the PF's FLY task.
  • IR MODE selector actions are crosschecked by both pilots before acting in flight.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] IR ALIGNMENT IN ATT MODE — STATUS shows IR MAY BE AVAIL IN ATT; apply when the IR FAULT light flashes.. IR (affected) MODE SEL ATT (crosscheck first); Keep speed, heading and FL constant for 30 s; MCDU DATA → IRS MONITOR → SET HDG: enter A/C HDG; Crosscheck heading with STBY compass; update about every 10 min.
  • NAV ADR 1(2)(3) FAULT — If the ADR of the same ADIRU has also failed, apply the ADR FAULT procedure first.. AIR DATA SWTG to the side of the failed ADR (CAPT 3 / F/O 3); ADR (affected) P/B OFF.
Gaps and omissions
  • No IR-specific FCTM or PDP module exists; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling (FCTM AOP-30-30, PDP Management of abnormal operations). No callout is given for the ATT HDG switching itself.
  • The alert is inhibited in flight phases 4, 5, 7 and 8 (and partly 3). The manuals give no separate crew procedure for an IR loss with no ECAM alert; detection then relies on the PFD/ND flags and the overhead FAULT light.
  • GPWS TERR, ROW/ROP and TCAS INOP lines are equipment-dependent (option marks and footnotes on the FCOM page).
  • The HS-TO version of IR ALIGNMENT IN ATT MODE (extra "On ground: T.O SURV pb OFF" line) is not used.

NAV IR 1+2(1+3)(2+3) FAULT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A

An amber caution: two inertial references have failed. AP, FD and A/THR are lost, the flight controls revert to alternate law (protections lost) and one PFD loses attitude unless IR 3 can replace it. With IR 1+2 failed, set ATT HDG to CAPT 3: the captain keeps attitude and the F/O PFD has none. Land in CONF 3 at VREF + 10 kt; the law becomes DIRECT when the gear goes down.

In FFS 4 IR 1+2 (1+3) (2+3) FAULT, no ECAM.

Law reconfiguration — dual IR

FCOM flight controls law reconfiguration table (NAV rows), same values for HS-TXA..TXF and HS-TXG..TXU.

FailurePitch lawProtectionRollYaw
2 ADR or 2 IR (2nd self detected failed)ALTNREDUCEDDIRECTALTN

3 IRDIRECTNODIRECTMECH
More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when IR 1+2(1+3)(2+3) are failed. Inhibited in flight phases 4 and 8.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 8.

  • Dual NAV IRS failures cause the loss of AP, FD and A/THR, and the flight controls revert to ALTN law.
  • (3) in the table: after the faulty IR is set to OFF and ELAC 1 and 2 are reset.
  • There is no procedure for IRS 1 + 2 + 3 failure; the ECAM STATUS shows the approach procedure and INOP systems, and the standby instruments are the only attitude, altitude, speed and heading references.
  • ATT HDG selector: CAPT 3 — IR 3 replaces IR 1; F/O 3 — IR 3 replaces IR 2.
  • IR FAULT light flashing: attitude and heading may be recovered in ATT mode. Steady: the IR is lost.
  • In ATT mode the IR gives only attitude and heading (heading entered on the MCDU, reset about every 10 min). Once an IR is set from NAV to ATT or OFF in flight, NAV mode is lost for the rest of the flight; it is recovered only on ground by a complete alignment.
FCTM technique
  • The PF usually remains PF, unless the captain re-allocates tasks or a failure impacts the PF's FLY task (e.g. loss of attitude on the PF side).
  • To take control, the pilot clearly announces "I have control" and presses and holds the sidestick pb.
  • Reconfiguration law: at high altitude descend to increase the buffet margin (about 4 000 ft below REC MAX ALT); at high speed maneuver with care using small inputs.
Related procedures
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Associated procedure of the dual IR fault.. MAX SPEED 320 KT; MANEUVER WITH CARE (if displayed); Respect stall warnings with TAWS alerts.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — Active once the landing gear is down.. MAN PITCH TRIM USE; MAX SPEED 320/.77; Maneuver and use speed brakes with care.
  • [QRH] IR ALIGNMENT IN ATT MODE — STATUS shows IR MAY BE AVAIL IN ATT; apply when the IR FAULT light flashes.. IR (affected) MODE SEL ATT (crosscheck first); Keep speed, heading and FL constant for 30 s; MCDU DATA → IRS MONITOR → SET HDG: enter A/C HDG; Crosscheck heading with STBY compass; update about every 10 min.
Gaps and omissions
  • FD loss is stated by the FCTM; the FCOM STATUS INOP SYS lists AP 1+2 and A/THR but not FD.
  • No IR-specific PDP module or callouts; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling. The F/CTL ALTN LAW callout is the ECAM title announced by the PM.
  • GLS AUTOLAND, STEEP APPR, ROW/ROP and FLS items carry option marks (equipment-dependent).
  • The HS-TO version of IR ALIGNMENT IN ATT MODE (extra "On ground: T.O SURV pb OFF" line) is not used.

Alternate/direct law · FFS 4

2 procedures in this group — choose one

F/CTL ALTN LAW

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

An amber caution: the flight controls are in alternate law (PROT LOST). Pitch handling stays like normal law, but all protections except the maneuver (load factor) protection are lost. Respect MAX SPEED 320 kt and maneuver with care; if an elevator has failed, do not use the speed brakes. Land in CONF 3 at VREF + 10 kt; when the gear goes down (and the AP is off) the law becomes DIRECT, so trim manually.

In FFS 4 ALTN LAW and DIR LAW handling, then tuck under and Mach buffet in Normal and Alternate law.

Alternate law — what remains

FCOM DSC-27 alternate law with reduced protections.

FunctionIn alternate law
Pitch (flight mode)Load factor demand, like normal law
Load factor limitationAvailable (as normal law)
Pitch attitude protectionNone — amber X on PFD
Low speedLow speed stability (nose-down demand) replaces AoA protection; stall warning; α floor inoperative

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when alternate laws are active. Inhibited in flight phases 4, 5, 7 and 8.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • Three levels of reconfiguration: alternate law (with or without reduced protections), direct law, mechanical. The ECAM and PFD indicate any control law degradation.
  • In flight, pitch alternate law is based on load factor demand; the basic high speed protection, pitch attitude protection and angle-of-attack protection are not available.
  • Alternate law without reduced protection: identical to alternate law but without the low-speed or high-speed stability — only the load factor limitation remains.
  • Low energy aural alert is lost in alternate law.
  • The AP disconnects if the speed exceeds VMO/MMO or the bank angle exceeds 45°.
  • If the aircraft goes far outside the normal envelope, the abnormal attitude law engages (F/CTL DIRECT LAW on ECAM); after recovery, alternate law without reduced protection remains for the rest of the flight (F/CTL ALTN LAW on ECAM).
FCTM technique
  • Within the normal flight envelope, alternate-law handling in pitch is identical to normal law. Outside it, the PF must take appropriate preventive actions to avoid losing control or high speed excursions.
  • At high altitude, descend about 4 000 ft below REC MAX ALT to reduce stall warnings in turbulence. At high speed, maneuver with care using small inputs.
  • Protections are not structural limits; the PF must not deliberately exceed the normal flight envelope.
  • Direct law: be careful with large thrust changes or sudden speedbrake movements, particularly with an aft CG. Retract speedbrakes gently to give time to re-trim. At go-around, TOGA thrust gives a large pitch-up moment — apply nose-down trim to avoid excessive pitch-up or a transient stall warning.
Related procedures
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — Active from landing gear extension (with AP: when L/G down and AP off).. MAN PITCH TRIM USE; MAX SPEED 320/.77; Maneuver and use speed brakes with care.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXFHS-TXG..TXU
2 FAC, yaw damper, FAC 1 + HYD Y or FAC 2 + HYD G failurePitch ALTN (reduced protection), roll DIRECT, yaw MECHPitch and roll stay NORM, yaw MECH; ALTN LAW is indicated; no reversion to DIRECT LAW at L/G extension
Bank angle above 45° in alternate lawBANK BANK message on both PFDs and "BANK BANK" aural alertHS-TXN..TXU: as HS-TXA..TXF. HS-TXG..TXM: bank angle protection not provided (no BANK BANK alert described)

Two FCOM units (HS-TXA..TXF, HS-TXG..TXU) with identical procedure and STATUS. The law reconfiguration after FAC / yaw damper failures differs (see HS-TX differences).

Gaps and omissions
  • The two FCOM procedure units differ only by effectivity; their visible content (lines, STATUS, inhibition) is identical.
  • The bank-angle alert splits the fleet differently (HS-TXA..TXF, HS-TXN..TXU vs HS-TXG..TXM) from the procedure units.
  • No FCTM abnormal-procedure chapter or PDP task-sharing module is specific to F/CTL ALTN LAW; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling, the FCTM reconfiguration-law technique and the PDP law slides.

F/CTL DIRECT LAW

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

An amber caution: the flight controls are in direct law. Sidestick deflection moves the surfaces directly, there is no automatic trim (USE MAN PITCH TRIM on the PFD) and no protection. Overspeed and stall warnings remain. Keep below 320 kt / M .77, trim manually, use small inputs at high speed, prefer manual thrust and avoid large thrust changes. Land in CONF 3 at VREF + 10 kt.

In FFS 4 Later, the crosswind landing is flown in DIR LAW.

Direct law — handling

FCOM DSC-27 direct law.

AxisIn direct law
PitchDirect stick-to-elevator; max elevator deflection varies with CG; no automatic trim

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when direct law is active. Inhibited in flight phases 4, 5, 7 and 8.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • The pitch direct law is a direct stick-to-elevator relationship. Maximum elevator deflection is a compromise between controllability with a forward CG and a not-too-sensitive control with an aft CG.
  • The roll direct law uses only the ailerons and spoilers 4 and 5 to limit roll rate (spoiler 3 replaces a failed spoiler 4; all roll spoilers if the ailerons have failed).
  • Both pitch trim wheels give mechanical control of the THS and have priority over electrical control. A pilot action on the pitch trim wheel disconnects the autopilot.
  • The abnormal attitude law also shows F/CTL DIRECT LAW on the ECAM and USE MAN PITCH TRIM on the PFDs.
FCTM technique
  • Direct law: be careful with large thrust changes or sudden speedbrake movements, particularly with an aft CG. Retract speedbrakes gently to give time to re-trim. At go-around, TOGA thrust gives a large pitch-up moment — apply nose-down trim to avoid excessive pitch-up or a transient stall warning.
Related procedures
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW — Alternate law reverts to direct law at landing gear extension.. MAX SPEED 320 KT; FOR LDG FLAP LVR 3, VREF + 10 KT.
Gaps and omissions
  • Conflict on yaw in direct law: FCOM DSC-27 says yaw damping and turn coordination are lost (mechanical yaw); the PDP slide says "Turn coordination reduced". FCOM is followed.
  • The HS-TO version (FCOM P 21–24/132) is not used.
  • No PDP task-sharing module is specific to F/CTL DIRECT LAW; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling, the FCTM reconfiguration-law technique and the PDP law slides.

MECHANICAL BACKUP · FFS 4

Technique Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

When the fly-by-wire control is lost, the aircraft is flown mechanically: pitch with the pitch trim wheel (THS), lateral with the rudder pedals. The aim is not accurate flying but a safe, stabilized attitude while the lost systems are restored. Move the trim wheel smoothly, because the THS is very powerful. Rudder makes the aircraft roll after a short delay, so apply some rudder, wait, and release early to level the wings.

In FFS 4 Demonstration.

Lateral
Rudder pedals

G or Y hydraulic

MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY (red)

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Recognise
  1. 1.1 PF + PM
    • PFDs show MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY in red
    • Objective: keep the aircraft attitude safe and stabilized, not accurate flying, to allow restoration of the lost systems
  2. 1.2 PF
    • Fly the aircraft: pitch trim wheel for pitch, rudder pedals for lateral control
2Pitch control
  1. 2.1 PF
    • Use the pitch trim wheel to control pitch; apply any action smoothly — the THS effect is significant due to its large size
    • Mechanical THS control is available at any time if the green or yellow hydraulic system works; the trim wheel has priority over electrical control
3Lateral control
  1. 3.1 PF
    • Apply some rudder to turn and wait for the aircraft reaction — rudder induces a significant roll with a slight delay
    • To stabilize and level the wings, anticipate by releasing the rudder pedals
4Restore
  1. 4.1 PM
    • Restore the lost systems with the ECAM / QRH procedures of the failure that caused the mechanical backup
  2. 4.2 PF
    • Fly, navigate, communicate in this order

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. No ECAM alert of its own. The last level of flight control reconfiguration: it covers a temporary total electrical loss, the temporary loss of the five fly-by-wire computers, the loss of both elevators, or the total loss of ailerons and spoilers. The PFDs show MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY in red.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Three levels of reconfiguration: alternate law, direct law, mechanical.
  • The purpose of the mechanical backup is to achieve all safety objectives in MMEL dispatch condition: to manage a temporary and total electrical loss, the temporary loss of five fly-by-wire computers, the loss of both elevators, or the total loss of ailerons and spoilers.
  • Pitch: the pilot manually applies trim to the THS; the PFDs display MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY in red. Lateral: the pilot uses the rudder pedals.
  • MAN PITCH TRIM ONLY is displayed on the FMA (line 3) in case of loss of L + R elevators.
  • The pilots can use conventional rudder pedals to control the rudder mechanically.
  • Pitch trim wheels: mechanical control of the THS, priority over electrical control; an action on the wheel disconnects the AP.
FCTM technique
  • The objective is not to fly the aircraft accurately, but to maintain the aircraft attitude safe and stabilized, in order to allow the restoration of lost systems.
  • Pitch: pitch trim wheel, applied smoothly — the THS effect is significant due to its large size.
  • Lateral: rudder gives a significant roll with a slight delay. Apply some rudder to turn and wait; release the pedals early to stabilize and level the wings.
Gaps and omissions
  • There is no ECAM or QRH procedure titled mechanical backup in the supplied manuals; the brief uses FCOM DSC-27 and FCTM AOP-10-30-20 only.
  • No PDP slide covers mechanical-backup handling, and no callouts or thrust technique are given for it.
  • Which ECAM alerts accompany the mechanical backup depends on the causing failure (electrical, fly-by-wire computers, elevators); those procedures are not reproduced here.

CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT · EMER DESCENT · FFS 4

Memory items Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

A red warning that the cabin altitude is too high. Above FL 160 the crew first does the EMER DESCENT memory items: oxygen masks, signs, descent with AP and A/THR, speed brakes. Then they do the ECAM read-and-do. Without structural damage they descend at maximum speed to FL 100 or MEA/MORA. Below FL 160 they apply the ECAM and start a normal descent.

In FFS 4 Trainee A: structural damage suspected. Trainee B: no structural damage suspected.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Climb or descent: cabin altitude above the higher of 9 550 ft or airfield pressure altitude + 1 000 ft. Cruise: cabin altitude above 9 550 ft.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10.

  • Depressurization is identified by excessive and uncontrollable cabin altitude and rate of climb, the CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT alert, or all cabin oxygen masks dropping (independent pressure switch).
  • At idle, high speed and speed brakes out, the descent rate is about 7 000 ft/min: FL 390 to FL 100 takes about 4 min and 40 NM.
  • Suspect structural damage after a loud bang or a high cabin V/S.
  • HS-TXA..TXFOEB 61 root cause: the active CPC can show a wrong but normal-looking cabin altitude; the standby CPC triggers the alert. The crew may wrongly disregard the alert or delay the descent.
FCTM technique
  • Above FL 160: EMER DESCENT memory items first, then the ECAM. Below FL 160: ECAM procedure and a normal descent.
  • Two steps: memory items (PM monitors the FMA), then read & do (PF adjusts the settings).
  • At high levels, extend speed brakes while monitoring VLS so AoA protection does not retract them or disconnect the AP.
  • Structural damage suspected: SPEED/MACH pb to SPEED to stop the IAS increasing or to reduce speed; use speed brakes carefully.
  • Below FL 100 limit the descent rate to about 1 000 ft/min (PDP adds 500 ft/min for passenger comfort), except on approach.
Related procedures
  • CAB PR SYS 1+2 FAULT — Both CPCs failed — a common lead-in to the excess cabin altitude. MODE SEL MAN; MAN V/S CTL AS RQRD; keep aircraft altitude at or above cabin altitude; Final approach: V/S CTL FULL UP; ΔP zero before opening doors.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXFHS-TXG..TXU
OEB 61 (CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT)Applies: do the ECAM even if the CAB PRESS SD page looks normalNot applicable

The ECAM, memory items and QRH are the same for every HS-TX (Applicable to ALL). Only OEB 61 differs: it applies to HS-TXA..TXF.

Gaps and omissions
  • The ECAM has no explicit LAND ASAP for this alert; the diversion decision follows the general assess/decide step.
  • Callout wording comes from the PDP; the FCOM memory-item callout is “EMERGENCY DESCENT”.
  • The PDP says the EMER DESCENT (PA) line may not show on the ECAM on some aircraft; it is in the HS-TX FCOM procedure.

NAV RA 1 AND 2 FAULT · FFS 4

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

An amber caution with no action line, crew awareness only. The effects matter for the approach: no G/S capture with the APPR pb (LOC is available with the LOC pb), CAT 1 limits only, no auto callouts or RETARD, no GPWS, reactive windshear detection or SPEED SPEED SPEED. When the gear goes down the flight controls revert to DIRECT LAW, the AP disconnects and USE MAN PITCH TRIM appears. Land in CONF 3 at VREF + 10 kt.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when both RAs are failed (dual RA failure). Inhibited in flight phases 3, 4, 5 and 8.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 8.

  • The radio altimeters feed the GPWS and the FWC (auto callouts), the AP and A/THR modes, and the flight control law switching. With both RAs failed, the flight control system uses the LGCIU inputs instead for mode switching.
  • Law reconfiguration table: 2 radio altimeters at L/G extension (or CONF 2 if both LGCIUs faulty) — pitch DIRECT, no protection, roll DIRECT, yaw ALTN.
FCTM technique
  • Although the ECAM procedure is straightforward, the effects of the failure on the aircraft operation require consideration.
  • Fly the final phases of the approach on raw data, to avoid possible excessive roll rates if LOC is still engaged.
  • Direct law: be careful with large thrust changes or sudden speedbrake movements; at go-around, TOGA thrust gives a large pitch-up moment — apply nose-down trim.
Related procedures
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — Active from landing gear extension.. MAN PITCH TRIM USE; MAX SPEED 320/.77; Maneuver and use speed brakes with care.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCOM procedure is titled NAV RA 1 AND 2 FAULT (DUAL RA FAILURE); the FCTM calls it dual radio altimeter failure. No PDP module covers it; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling.
  • The manuals give no standard callouts to replace the missing auto callouts; none are invented here.
  • The HS-TO version (FCOM P 115–116/124) is not used.

Cargo smoke · FFS 4

2 procedures in this group — choose one

SMOKE AFT CARGO SMOKE

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

A red warning with red LAND ASAP. Smoke is detected in the aft cargo hold, which is built to contain a fire, so the smoke is not felt in the cockpit; only the SMOKE light on the CARGO SMOKE panel confirms it. Close the aft isolation valve if it did not close by itself, cabin fans OFF, discharge AGENT 1 (guarded pb, crosscheck first) and AGENT 2 after 60 min, and divert. Expect the warning to stay after discharge. On the ground, the passengers disembark before any cargo door is opened.

In FFS 4 Listed in the syllabus as AFT/BULK CRG SMOKE.

LAND ASAP
Red — nearest airport with a safe landing
AGENT 1
DISCH (bottle 1 empties in about 60 s)
AGENT 2
DISCH after 60 min
Cargo doors
Not opened before PAX DISEMBARK
