More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when smoke in the AFT cargo compartment is detected. Inhibited in flight phases 4, 5, 7 and 8.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • The cargo compartments are designed to be air-tight and fireproof to contain a fire, and the cargo ventilation prevents cargo smoke from reaching the cockpit/cabin. The crew can only confirm the alert with the SMOKE light on the CARGO SMOKE panel.
  • The aft compartment has four smoke detectors on two loops. The warning needs both detectors of a cavity (or one, if the other is inoperative). The isolation valves close and the extraction fan stops automatically.
  • The DISCH pb fires the squibs of the fire bottles: bottle 1 discharges in about 60 s; a flow metering system controls bottle 2 for at least 135 min. BTL 1(2) light amber when empty.
  • The DISCH sw is guarded. The DISCH AGENT 2 light comes on amber 60 min after AGENT 1 and goes off when the AGENT 2 squib is ignited.
FCTM technique
  • An immediate diversion should be considered as soon as smoke/fumes are detected. If the source is not immediately obvious, accessible and extinguishable, divert without delay.
  • Guarded controls are crosschecked by both pilots before acting in flight.
  • If smoke/fumes become perceptible in the cockpit or cabin, or any doubt exists about the smoke origin, apply the [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE — If any doubt exists about the smoke origin, or smoke/fumes are perceptible.. LAND ASAP; immediate actions; Diversion and descent to FL 100 / MEA-MORA if the source is not isolated; Boxed items at any time: REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, ELEC EMER CONFIG, immediate landing.
  • SMOKE DISCH AGENT 2 — Reminder 60 min after AGENT 1 when the cargo smoke alert has stopped.. AGENT 2 DISCH.
Gaps and omissions
  • "AFT/BULK CRG SMOKE" is not an HS-TX alert title; the THA FCOM gives SMOKE AFT CARGO SMOKE for all HS-TX.
  • The procedure does not call for an evacuation; it requires PAX DISEMBARK before opening the cargo doors.
  • FCOM note 1 (recovering aft cargo ventilation for livestock) applies only to aircraft with the AFT cargo ventilation option and is not used here.
  • No PDP module covers cargo smoke; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling.
  • The HS-TO version (FCOM P 34–36/50) is not used.

REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

Used when dense smoke or fumes become the greatest threat. Keep the air flowing (CAB FANS OFF and PACK FLOW HI, unless there are fuel vapours), raise the landing elevation to 10 000 ft / MEA-MORA and start a descent to FL 100 / MEA-MORA. Then go back to the SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure during the descent. At FL 100 the cabin is depressurised and RAM AIR is used. If smoke persists: max 200 kt, cockpit door open, and open the PM sliding window.

QRH 27.02A · PDF 249 · QRH 27.02B · PDF 250

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. QRH procedure. Apply it if smoke/fumes become the greatest threat when applying the [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure — a boxed item that may be applied at any time of that procedure, but not before its immediate actions.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The most effective means of smoke/fumes removal is ram air: descend to FL 100 or MEA-MORA while the cabin altitude is raised to 10 000 ft or MEA-MORA. The higher cabin altitude also reduces, at least temporarily, the smoke/fumes concentration.
  • With fuel vapours, CAB FANS ON: recirculated air ventilates the air mixer bay and other fuselage areas, preventing fuel vapour accumulation and the risk of explosion; passenger health is not affected.
  • Without fuel vapours, CAB FANS OFF prevents smoke/fumes from entering the cockpit and cabin; PACK FLOW HI gives maximum airflow. Do not shut down the packs or reduce ventilation to smother the fire. Do not deploy oxygen masks if fire is suspected in the cabin.
  • In ELEC EMER CONFIG, APU MASTER ON closes the battery contactors for a maximum of 3 min, so the crew can manually control the outflow valve powered by the DC BAT BUS.
  • If there is smoke/fumes in the cockpit, open the cockpit window to evacuate it. Due to the increased noise level, pay particular attention to visual warnings.
FCTM technique
  • The [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure: diversion anticipated (LAND ASAP), immediate actions, then — if the source is not immediately isolated — diversion and descent, origin identification and fighting. Boxed items (REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, ELEC EMER CONFIG, immediate landing) may be applied at any time, but not before the immediate actions.
  • Once the first steps of REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES are applied, return to the SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure for the steps for the suspected source while descending to FL 100; reaching FL 100, complete REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES.
  • QRH procedures: read the notes before performing the action they relate to.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE — Parent procedure: REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES is one of its boxed items.. LAND ASAP; immediate actions (crew protection, avoid further contamination, cabin crew communication); If source not immediately isolated: DIVERSION and DESCENT TO FL 100 / MEA-MORA INITIATE; Identify and fight: AIR COND, CAB EQPT, or AVNCS/ELECTRICAL (or source unknown and persisting).
  • ELEC EMER CONFIG (as a smoke boxed item) — Dense smoke still the greatest threat, or all specific actions unsuccessful.. Shed as much electrical equipment as possible to isolate the source; Remain in ELEC EMER CONFIG until a late stage; restore generation a few minutes before landing.
Gaps and omissions
  • The parent [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure (two HS-TX FCOM variants, HS-TXA..TXO and HS-TXP..TXU) is summarised only, not reproduced.
  • The PDP gives only the order callout ("REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES PROCEDURE"); the split of the QRH lines between PF and PM is not given beyond read & do by the PM. The PF descent, ATC and speed items follow the FCTM task sharing.

NAV ADR 1(2)(3) FAULT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee B

An amber caution: one air data reference has failed, so one side loses speed and altitude data. Switch AIR DATA to CAPT 3 (ADR 1) or F/O 3 (ADR 2) and turn the failed ADR pb OFF; for ADR 2 also check the baro reference. Approach capability drops to CAT 3 SINGLE.

NAV ADR 1(2)(3) FAULT

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when the ADR 1(2)(3) is failed. Inhibited in flight phases 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 10 — NAV ADR 1(2) FAULT is not inhibited in phases 3, 5 and 7; NAV ADR 3 FAULT is not inhibited in phase 3 while the ADR 3 is in use.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10.

  • Each ADIRS has two parts (ADR and IRS) that may fail independently. A single NAV ADR FAULT only requires action on the switching panel as indicated by the ECAM.
  • AIR DATA selector: NORM — ADIRU 1 to the captain side, ADIRU 2 to the F/O side. CAPT 3 — ADR 3 replaces ADR 1. F/O 3 — ADR 3 replaces ADR 2.
  • ADR pb-sw FAULT light: ADR failed (NAV ADR FAULT alert). Pressing it turns the ADR off and the FAULT light goes off.
FCTM technique
  • Overhead actions: the PM points to the control and announces system – control – action, then checks the result.
Related procedures
  • NAV IR 1(2)(3) FAULT — If the IR of the same ADIRU has also failed, apply it after this ADR procedure.. ATT HDG SWTG to the side of the failed IR; ATC/XPDR to the other system.
Gaps and omissions
  • No ADR-specific FCTM technique beyond the ADR/IRS FAULT paragraph, and no PDP module; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling. No callout is given for the switching itself.
  • The HS-TO version of the procedure (FCOM P 23–25/124) is not used.

NAV ADR 1+2(1+3)(2+3) FAULT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee B

An amber caution: two air data references have failed. Normal law is lost (alternate law, protections lost), AP, FD and A/THR are lost, and one side loses air data unless ADR 3 can replace it. With ADR 1+2 failed, set AIR DATA to CAPT 3, turn the failed ADRs OFF and select FLAPS 1 only below the VFE of CONF 1+F. With ADR 1+3 failed, the gear cannot retract and must be extended by gravity. Land in CONF 3 at VREF + 10 kt; the law becomes DIRECT when the gear goes down.

ADR 1+3 · L/G
No retraction · GRVTY EXTN
FOR LDG
FLAP LVR 3
APPR SPD
VREF + 10 KT

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure, STATUS

NAV ADR 1+2(1+3)(2+3) FAULT
  1. Flight control normal laws are lost. Pitch alternate law preserves the neutral static stability. All protections, except maneuver protections are lost.
  2. In the case of a simultaneous ADR and IR (same ADIRU) failure, apply the ADR FAULT procedure prior to the IR FAULT procedure.
  3. If NAV ADR 1+2 FAULT:
  4. AIR DATA SWTGCAPT 3Set ADR 3 (if available) to the captain's side.
  5. ADR (AFFECTED) P/BOFF
  6. The GPWS TERR FAULT and GPWS SYS FAULT lights illuminate (enhanced/predictive GPWS functions inhibited). If this occurs, switch off the GPWS TERR pb-sw and the GPWS SYS pb-sw.
  7. In the case of NAV ADR 1+2 FAULT, check speed is below VFE of CONF 1+F before selecting FLAPS 1. Because ADR 1+2 parameters are lost, the SFCCs will set CONF 1+F instead of CONF 1.
  8. ASSOCIATED PROCEDURES: F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Refer to PRO-ABN-F_CTL F/CTL ALTN LAW
  9. If NAV ADR 1+3(2+3) FAULT:
  10. Air data information is lost on one PFD.
  11. In the case of NAV ADR 1+3 FAULT, the landing gear safety valve is controlled closed: landing gear retraction is inoperative; landing gear extension must be performed by gravity.
  12. AIR DATA SWTGNORM
  13. ATC/XPDR (IF ADR 1 FAILED)SYS 2
  14. ATC/XPDR (IF ADR 2 FAILED)SYS 1
  15. ADR (AFFECTED) P/BOFF
  16. In the case of NAV ADR 1+3 FAULT: The GPWS TERR FAULT and GPWS SYS FAULT lights illuminate (enhanced/predictive GPWS functions inhibited). If this occurs, switch off the GPWS TERR pb-sw and the GPWS SYS pb-sw.
  17. If NAV ADR 2+3 FAULT and ANTI ICE CAPT AOA:
  18. AVOID ICING CONDITIONS—
  19. ASSOCIATED PROCEDURES: F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Refer to PRO-ABN-F_CTL F/CTL ALTN LAW

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when two ADRs are failed. Inhibited in flight phases 1, 4, 8 and 10.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 1, 4, 8, 10.

  • Dual NAV ADR failures cause the loss of AP, FD and A/THR, and the flight controls revert to ALTN law.
  • With a triple ADR failure, the NAV ADR 1+2+3 FAULT procedure has all three ADRs switched OFF, to replace the PFD speed scale and altitude by the BUSS and GPS altitude.
  • AIR DATA selector: CAPT 3 — ADR 3 replaces ADR 1; F/O 3 — ADR 3 replaces ADR 2.
FCTM technique
  • Reconfiguration law: at high altitude descend to increase the buffet margin (about 4 000 ft below REC MAX ALT); at high speed maneuver with care using small inputs.
  • The PF usually remains PF, unless the captain re-allocates tasks or a failure impacts the PF's FLY task.
Related procedures
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Associated procedure of the dual ADR fault.. MAX SPEED 320 KT; MANEUVER WITH CARE (if displayed); Respect stall warnings with TAWS alerts.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — Active once the landing gear is down.. MAN PITCH TRIM USE; MAX SPEED 320/.77; Maneuver and use speed brakes with care.
  • [QRH] L/G GRAVITY EXTENSION — NAV ADR 1+3 FAULT: the gear can only be extended by gravity.. Do not apply if at least one green triangle on each gear on the WHEEL SD page; GRAVITY GEAR EXTN handcrank PULL AND TURN (3 turns clockwise to the mechanical stop); L/G lever DOWN; GEAR DOWN indications CHECK; If successful: do not reset the handcrank; if unsuccessful: LDG WITH ABNORMAL L/G PROC APPLY.
Gaps and omissions
  • FD loss is stated by the FCTM; the FCOM STATUS INOP SYS lists AP 1+2 and A/THR but not FD.
  • VFE of CONF 1+F is in FCOM LIM-AG-SPD, not reproduced here.
  • No ADR-specific PDP module or callouts; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling.
  • The HS-TO versions of the procedure (FCOM P 30–37/124) are not used.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Applied when considering an emergency evacuation, or when required by the ECAM (e.g. ENG FIRE on ground: EMER EVAC PROC APPLY).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Typical causes: uncontrollable fire, smoke/fumes — during taxi, after a rejected takeoff or after landing.
  • With engines stopped only the right dome light works; on batteries the crew seats must be moved mechanically.
FCTM technique
  • "CABIN CREW (PA)…ALERT" tells the cabin the flight crew still controls the situation and prevents an unwanted cabin-initiated evacuation (done in the RTO flow).
  • ΔP check does not apply after an RTO: at least one automatic pressure system is required for departure.
  • "EVACUATION…INITIATE" = notify cabin crew, press EVAC COMMAND, advise ATC — preferably in this order.
  • Until the order is given the evacuation can be deferred or cancelled; once ordered it is irreversible.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FIRE (ON GROUND) · RTO — Engine fire on ground not extinguished. AGENT 1+2 DISCH → EMER EVAC PROC APPLY.
Gaps and omissions
  • Company (THAI) phraseology is used instead of the generic Airbus/FCOM wording: “CABIN CREW, AT YOUR STATIONS” (PDP/FCOM: “ATTENTION CREW AT STATIONS”) and “REMAIN SEATED, RESUME NORMAL DUTIES” (PDP/FCOM: “CABIN CREW and PASSENGERS REMAIN SEATED”).
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM PRO-ABN-MISC P 15/30).

Failure procedures

Engine failure · FFS 5

3 procedures in this group — choose one

ENG 1(2) FAIL

Amber cautionLAND ASAP (amber) Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

An engine fails after V1 (or at go-around). Below 400 ft the PF only flies: rudder to centre the beta target, 12.5° then SRS, gear up. At 400 ft the PF orders ECAM ACTIONS until the engine is secured, then calls STOP ECAM to level off at EO acceleration altitude, clean up and set MCT at green dot. CONTINUE ECAM takes the PM to the STATUS page, where the PF stops the ECAM again for the after-takeoff flow and a relight decision.

In FFS 5 Trainee A: after V2 (familiarization), between V1 and V2 (repeat to proficiency), after V2, and at go-around from minima. Trainee B: between V1 and V2 (repeat to proficiency), after V2, and during go-around.

Rotation
≈3°/s to 12.5° pitch
Minimum speed
V2 (SRS: V2 to V2 +15 kt)
READ & DO from
400 ft AGL
Relight wait
30 s after ENG FAIL
Takeoff thrust
10 min max
Final takeoff segment
Green dot · MCT

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Engine core speed below idle with the ENG MASTER lever ON and the ENG FIRE pb not pushed.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Flameout causes include fuel starvation, volcanic ash/sand, heavy rain/hail/icing, bird strike, engine stall, control malfunction.
  • Suspect damage with two or more of: EGT above red line, rotor speed mismatch or no rotation, vibration/buffet, abnormal oil pressure/temperature, hydraulic loss, repeated stalls.
  • Takeoff with an engine failure: the blue beta target replaces the sideslip index; lateral normal law gives some rudder, the pilot completes it to centre the target.
  • When an engine failure is detected the FMGS gives engine-out predictions and deletes pre-selected speeds.
FCTM technique
  • Aircraft handling first: stabilise pitch, speed and path before the ECAM.
  • Failure above V2: keep the SRS attitude; minimum speed V2.
  • "Secure the engine" = ENG MASTER OFF (no damage), AGENT 1 DISCH (damage), fire out or AGENT 2 DISCH (fire).
  • With AP engaged the rudder trim is managed by the AP; release rudder pedal pressure.
  • Do not exceed the EO maximum acceleration altitude if acceleration is delayed.
  • In cruise: MCT, A/THR off, set heading, standard strategy M.78/300 kt, descend to EO recovery altitude, never below green dot.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT — No damage, relight considered. See the ENG RELIGHT brief.
  • ONE ENGINE INOPERATIVE — GO-AROUND — Engine failure at go-around. TOGA + prompt rudder; SRS or 12.5°; GA TRK — terrain.
Gaps and omissions
  • Thrust-malfunction and on-ground branches of ENG FAIL are not shown in the flow; this brief covers the in-flight case.
  • Callout wording differs slightly between sources: FCOM "ECAM ACTION" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETE" vs PDP and FCTM "ECAM ACTIONS" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETED". The PDP is a generic Airbus tutorial; FCOM wording is shown where both exist.
  • HS-TO-only versions omitted (FCOM P 87–89 and P 174–183/226).

ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

A QRH (paper) procedure for restarting an engine that failed without damage. Check the relight envelope, set the failed engine to IDLE/IGN with crossbleed open, then ENG MASTER ON and watch N2/EGT — there is no automatic start abort in flight.

In FFS 5 Trainee A repositions to FL 350 after the restart.

Light-up
within 30 s of fuel flow
Failed attempt
N2 < 50 % within 70 s
Before retry
wait 30 s (drain)
Windmill relight
≥ 270 kt
Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Decide
  1. 1.1 PF
    • Only with no engine damage, no fire shutdown and no risk of fire
    • Choose relight type from the envelope (starter-assisted / windmill)
  2. 1.2 PM
    • Open QRH ENG RELIGHT — IN FLIGHT (keep the ECAM displayed)
    • From ENG 1(2) FAIL: recommended at the STATUS page once all ECAM actions are done
2Order the QRH procedure
  1. 2.1 PF
    • ENG RELIGHT PROCEDURE
    • PF orders “(name) PROCEDURE”, then flies and communicates
  2. 2.2 PM
    • READ AND DO the QRH lines aloud
3Set up
  1. 3.1 PM
    • ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFF
    • THR LEVER (affected engine)Check IDLE
  2. 3.2 PF
    • Thrust lever of the affected engine: confirm IDLE
  3. 3.3 PM
    • ENG MODE selIGN
    • X BLEEDOPEN
    • WING ANTI ICE (for starter assist)OFF
4Start
  1. 4.1 PM
    • ENG MASTER (affected engine)ON
    • ENG PARAMETERS (N2, EGT)MONITOR
    • Light-up within 30 s after fuel flow increases — AUTOMATIC START ABORT NOT AVAIL
  2. 4.2 PF
    • Unsure of the relight? Move the thrust lever forward and check the response
5Result
  1. 5.1 PM
    • When idle reached (ENG AVAIL)
      • ENG MODE selNORM
      • TCAS MODE selTA/RA
      • X BLEEDAUTO
      • Affected SYSRESTORE
    • If no relight
      • ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFF
      • Wait 30 s before a new start (drain)
    • ENG RELIGHT PROCEDURE COMPLETED
From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

ENG RELIGHT — IN FLIGHT
  1. No attempt if engine damage, if shut down for fire, or if a relight may cause fire.
  2. ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFF
  3. THR LEVER (affected engine)Check IDLE
  4. ENG MODE selIGN
  5. X BLEEDOPENOutside the windmilling envelope the FADEC opens the starter valve.
  6. WING ANTI ICE (for starter assist)OFF
  7. ENG MASTER (affected engine)ON
  8. ENG PARAMETERS (N2, EGT)MONITOR
  9. AUTOMATIC START ABORT NOT AVAIL
  10. When idle reached (ENG AVAIL):
  11. ENG MODE selNORM
  12. TCAS MODE selTA/RA
  13. X BLEEDAUTO
  14. Affected SYSRESTORE
  15. If no relight:
  16. ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFFWait 30 s before attempting a new start.
  17. If N2 does not increase above 50 % within 70 s, consider the relight unsuccessful; consider a windmill relight at minimum 270 kt.

Engine relight envelope (QRH 19.06B)

Read the chart in the QRH; zones summarised.

ZoneRelight type
1Starter-assisted relight (N2 ≤ 18 %), lower speeds
2Windmill quick relight if N2 > 18 %

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. QRH procedure, considered from ENG 1(2) FAIL (no damage) or STATUS "CONSIDER ENG RELIGHT".

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The relight can be a windmilling start or a starter-assisted relight using bleed from the other engine.
  • Unlike a ground auto start, the crew must act on an abnormal start.
FCTM technique
  • The crew may stop the relight procedure at any time if the situation requires (time, distance to fly).
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FAIL — Calls for ENG RELIGHT CONSIDER if no damage. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • Envelope boundaries are graphical — use the QRH chart; values are not transcribed.
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM P 1–3/226, QRH 19.06A).

ENGINE FAILURE IN CRUISE · drift-down strategy

Technique Practised by Trainee A

After an engine failure at cruise level the aircraft cannot hold its altitude. The PF sets MCT with A/THR off, sets a heading and determines the engine-out recovery altitude, then drifts down at M.78/300 kt (standard strategy) to the EO LRC ceiling, never below green dot. After an engine fire, the fire drill is done first and without delay.

In FFS 5 ENG 1(2) FAIL with the drift-down procedure.

Thrust
MCT · A/THR off
Standard strategy
M.78 / 300 kt
Minimum speed
Green dot
Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Drift down (standard strategy)
  1. 1.1 PF + PM
    • After an engine fire, the fire drill comes first and without delay; the PF flies the strategy around it. No obstacle constraint → standard strategy
  2. 1.2 PF
    • ALL THRUST LEVERSMCT
    • A/THROFF
    • A/THR off so thrust is not reduced when selecting speed or OPEN DES; MCT is frozen
    • Never decelerate below green dot; at high levels and weights do not delay the descent
    • If the failure occurs below the EO LRC ceiling
      • Keep A/THR on
  3. 1.3 PF + PM
    • STRATEGYDETERMINE
  4. 1.4 PM
    • ATCNOTIFY
    • After an engine fire this is already done in the ECAM actions
  5. 1.5 PF
    • HDGSET AS APPROPRIATE AND PULL
    • ENGINE OUT RECOVERY ALTITUDEDETERMINE
    • MCDU PROG page REC MAX = EO LRC ceiling; do not press EO CLR
    • When ready for descent
      • M.78 / 300 KTSET AND PULL

    • When V/S < 500 ft/min in descent
      • V/S − 500 FT/MINSET AND PULL

    • When reaching the EO LRC ceiling (ALT CRZ)
      • SPEEDMANAGE

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Engine failure or engine shutdown (including after an engine fire) at cruise level.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Three strategies exist: standard, obstacle and fixed speed. Unless a specific procedure was set at dispatch (ETOPS, mountainous areas), the standard strategy is used.
FCTM technique
  • Engine failure in cruise: unless a dispatch procedure exists, use the standard strategy, M 0.78/300 kt to the REC MAX EO (LRC engine-out ceiling). Obstacle strategy: green dot to the drift-down ceiling, then standard when clear.
  • Do not hurry the ECAM actions in cruise — complete the drill correctly.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FIRE (IN FLIGHT) — When the engine failure is a fire. Fire drill first, without delay.
Gaps and omissions
  • No source puts the fire drill and the cruise strategy in one sequence. The fire procedure is applied without delay (FCTM), while the cruise flow sets MCT and A/THR off first and starts ECAM “when appropriate” (PDP). The brief keeps the fire drill first.

ENG ALL ENGINES FAILURE · FFS 5

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee A

All engines fail: the captain side keeps PFD 1 and the left-seat pilot flies, in alternate law with no AP, FD or A/THR. The PM runs a short ECAM (RAT and emergency generator, 280/0.77, APU, idle, FAC 1 reset, glide range), then goes straight to the QRH ALL ENG FAIL. If fuel remains and the engines are not damaged, try windmill relights on both engines, then starter-assisted relights below FL 200. If nothing relights, the QRH continues to a forced landing or ditching: those sections are under From the manuals, not in the flow.

In FFS 5 Listed in the syllabus as ENG DUAL FAILURE - FUEL REMAINING, followed by the windmill relight.

Optimum relight speed
280/0.77
Windmill relight
Approaching or below FL 300
Starter-assisted relight
Below FL 200 · APU bleed · green dot · one engine at a time
Glide
2 NM / 1000 FT at 280 kt · 2.5 NM / 1000 FT at green dot
Minimum RAT speed
140 kt
Max speed · max brake pressure
320/0.77 · 1000 PSI

Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Detection — fly first
  1. 1.1 PF + PM
    • Golden rule 1: fly, navigate, communicate
  2. 1.2 PF
    • CM1 (left seat) is PF: only PFD 1 is available. Take over and establish a safe flight path
    • AP, FD and A/THR are lost; alternate law, protections lost. Remove the FD flag, consider FPV
  3. 1.3 PF + PM
    • First to notice: MASTER WARNING / CAUTION reset
  4. 1.4 PM
    • ENG ALL ENGINES FAILURE
    • Confirm the failure on the SD page and overhead panel before acting
  5. 1.5 PF
    • ECAM ACTIONS
    • PF now flies, navigates and communicates
2ECAM actions
  1. 2.1 PM
    • EMER ELEC PWR MAN ON PBPRESS
    • OPT RELIGHT SPD280/0.77
  2. 2.2 PF
    • Fly at or above the optimum relight speed: mandatory after a failure in climb or cruise, to prevent engine core lock
    • In alternate law the overspeed protection is lost and the upper speed limits are reduced
    • Speed indication failure (volcanic ash)
      • Fly the pitch target from the QRH table
  3. 2.3 PM
    • APU (BELOW FL 250)START
    • THR LEVERSIDLE
  4. 2.4 PF
    • Set the thrust levers to idle, after the PM confirms: no thrust surge at relight
  5. 2.5 PM
    • FAC 1OFF THEN ON
    • Recovers the characteristic speeds on the PFD and rudder trim
    • Read GLDG DIST: 2NM/1000FT
  6. 2.6 PF
    • DIVERSION INITIATE: an accessible runway, or the best area for a forced landing or ditching
  7. 2.7 PM
    • ALL ENG FAIL PROCAPPLY
    • Go to the QRH ALL ENG FAIL at once and keep the ECAM procedure displayed
3QRH ALL ENG FAIL — notify, then check fuel
  1. 3.1 PF
    • Emergency message on VHF 1 (MAYDAY) when time permits
    • PF communicates once the ECAM actions are started
  2. 3.2 PM
    • VHF1/HF1/ATC1USE
    • ATCNOTIFY
    • CABIN CREWNOTIFY
    • SIGNSON
    • CREW OXY MASK (FL > 100)USE
    • FUEL QUANTITYCHECK
  3. 3.3 PF + PM
    • Decide: can a relight be attempted? Fuel starvation is one of the most probable causes; engine damage or fuel starvation means no relight
    • Relight cannot be attempted
      • Go to QRH 19.03A: green dot, then ditching or forced landing (see From the manuals)
4Fuel remains — windmill relight
  1. 4.1 PM
    • ENG MODE selIGN
    • Indicate the ENG MASTER levers
    • CONFIRM?
  2. 4.2 PF
    • CONFIRMED
    • After verifying the control the PM points to
  3. 4.3 PM
    • Approaching or below FL 300
      • ALL ENG MASTERSOFF 30 S THEN ON
      • ENGs RELIGHTTRY REGULARLY
    • Masters OFF, start the chrono; at 30 s masters ON; check N2 and EGT; at 1 min, if no relight, masters OFF; repeat
    • Both engines at the same time. The 30 s off ventilates the combustion chamber
    • APU (below FL 250)START
  4. 4.4 PF
    • Hold the optimum relight speed for the windmill relight
5If one engine relights
  1. 5.1 PF + PM
    • ENG ALL ENGINES FAILURE disappears and ENG 1(2) FAIL appears for the other engine: apply that ECAM procedure instead
    • After a successful start, use the restored engine as soon as possible
    • Normal electrical configuration returns, except AC ESS and DC ESS stay on the emergency generator; green, yellow and blue hydraulics return
  2. 5.2 PM
    • ENG 1(2) FAIL asks to consider the QRH ENG RELIGHT for the other engine; it may be stopped at any time if time or distance requires
6Windmill unsuccessful — starter-assisted relight
  1. 6.1 PM
    • APU available and windmill relight not successful, below FL 200
      • ALL ENG MASTERSOFF
      • OPTIMUM SPEED: GREEN DOT (table)
  2. 6.2 PF
    • Reduce to all-engines-inoperative green dot: displayed on PFD 1, also in the QRH table

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. All engines are failed in flight.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10.

  • Thrust is lost so that level flight cannot be held. The alert may not trigger on a partial loss of thrust: the crew then decides between ALL ENG FAIL (time for a relight) and EMER LANDING (no time).
  • This alert inhibits ELEC EMER CONFIG. Its purpose is to secure RAT extension and emergency generator connection, then send the crew to the QRH.
  • All AC busbars are lost; the RAT supplies the emergency generator, which feeds AC ESS and DC ESS. Green and yellow hydraulics are lost; the RAT pressurizes blue.
  • Each APU start attempt takes about 3.5 min off the battery time; total battery time is more than 30 min.
  • The right aileron is lost and floats; the PF may use rudder trim to balance it instead of holding a stick input. It returns when the APU generator connects (ELAC 2).
  • Windmill relight is preferred: it works over a wide altitude range, tries all engines at once and does not depend on aircraft systems.
FCTM technique
  • The ECAM glide distance is an envelope value for a rough range estimate; the actual distance may differ.
  • Going faster than the optimum speed keeps relight conditions, but in alternate law there is no overspeed protection.
  • Prepare for a ditching or forced landing even if a runway can be reached, if no engine relights.
  • Forced landing: gear down by gravity even off a runway, to absorb energy. The brake accumulator allows a limited number of applications, and there is no anti-skid.
  • Ditching: DITCHING pb just before touchdown closes the valves under the aircraft; hold the pitch and keep the wings level until impact.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FAIL — Appears for the remaining engine once one engine relights. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief.
  • [QRH] ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT — Requested from ENG 1(2) FAIL for the remaining engine. See the ENG RELIGHT brief.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Associated procedure. See the F/CTL ALTN LAW brief.
  • [QRH] EMER LANDING — ALL ENG FAILURE — Loss of thrust near the ground, not enough time for a relight. APU START, FLAPS LEVER 2, VAPP, gear per ditching or forced landing, BRACE FOR IMPACT, EMER EVAC PROC.
  • EMER EVAC — After a ditching or forced landing. See the EMER EVAC brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The title "ENG DUAL FAILURE - FUEL REMAINING" is not used in the supplied HS-TX manuals. They use ENG ALL ENGINES FAILURE (ECAM) and ALL ENG FAIL (QRH); the PDP shows a "FUEL REMAINING" title for the A330 only. Fuel remaining corresponds to the "relight can be attempted" branch here.
  • No source gives PF/PM turns for the QRH part. The order follows the QRH lines, with the FCTM and PDP notes; the 30 s masters timing is from the PDP slide.
  • The QRH lists CABIN CREW and PASSENGERS (PA) NOTIFY when no evacuation is needed; the company wording "REMAIN SEATED, RESUME NORMAL DUTIES" is noted on that line.
  • The handling flow stops at relight and STATUS. The no-relight, ditching and forced landing sections of the QRH are given only as verbatim procedures, without PF/PM turns.
  • HS-TO versions omitted (QRH 19.01A–B, 19.02B–19.03B and 19.05A blocks, FCOM P 41–43/226). The QRH points to 19.05A for a forced landing, but the HS-TX block starts on 19.05B.

RNP APPROACH · DEGRADED NAVIGATION · FFS 5

Technique Practised by Trainee A

There is no single procedure: the FCOM SOP lists what to do under Management of Degraded Navigation, and the crew reviews it in the arrival briefing. This brief leads with RNAV(GNSS) approaches with LNAV/VNAV minima; RNAV(RNP) rules are kept for reference under From the manuals. A loss on one side only: continue on the remaining AP/FD. A loss on both sides, XTK above 0.3 NM or 75 ft below the path: discontinue unless visual references are enough to proceed visually. Hand-flying needs the FD: in approach, AP and FD both off is not authorized without F-LOC deviation.

In FFS 5 3D RNP approach, RNAV(GNSS) with LNAV/VNAV minima, flown manually with FD. The syllabus says "degradation or system failure" without naming it.

Discontinue, vertical
75 ft below the path (V/DEV > ¾ dot)

0.3 NM with AP ON, or AP OFF with FD ON

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

Management of degraded navigation — RNAV(GNSS)
  1. Use the appropriate remaining AP/FD in the following cases:
  2. GPS PRIMARY LOST on one ND
  3. NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on one ND
  4. Discontinue the approach in the following cases, if external visual references are not sufficient to proceed visually:
  5. GPS PRIMARY LOST on both NDs
  6. XTK > 0.3 NM
  7. NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE
  8. NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on both NDs
  9. LNAV minima: be prepared to continue the approach by reverting to NAV-FPA, if the vertical guidance is not satisfactory.
  10. LNAV/VNAV minima: discontinue the approach in the case of deviation of 75 ft below the vertical path (V/DEV > ¾ dot).

FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-18-C P 16/36 · PDF 4251

For reference — RNAV(RNP) differs
  1. GPS PRIMARY must be available on both FMS, with both GPS in NAV or SBAS. If one FMS is inoperative or one GPS is not in NAV or SBAS before the IAF, RNAV(RNP) is not permitted.
  2. The approach may be continued in the case of single failure of:
  3. GPS (MMR) · FMGC · EFIS DU · MCDU · AP
  4. Discontinue the approach in the following cases:
  5. FINAL APP does not engage
  6. GPS PRIMARY LOST on both NDs
  7. Dual NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD
  8. FM/GPS POSITION DISAGREE
  9. FMS1/FMS2 POS DIFF
  10. Dual loss of FMGC or dual loss of FINAL APP mode
  11. Loss of GPWS TERRAIN function in case of inconsistencies affecting obstacles or terrain computation
  12. NAV ALT DISCREPANCY
  13. Go-around must be initiated if XTK reaches 1 RNP or V/DEV reaches ¾ dot below the vertical profile.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. During an RNAV(GNSS) or RNAV(RNP) approach: GPS PRIMARY LOST, NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD, NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE, excessive XTK or V/DEV, FINAL APP not engaging, or a failure of a guidance system.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • "RNP APCH" corresponds to RNAV(GNSS) approaches and "RNP AR" to RNAV(RNP). Both use FINAL APP with V/DEV and XTK deviations.
  • Minimum equipment to start RNP APCH: one FMGC, one GPS, two IRS, one MCDU, one FD, one PFD on the PF side, two NDs, two FCU channels.
  • If GPS PRIMARY LOST is displayed, navigation accuracy stays sufficient for RNP operations provided the RNP value is checked or entered and HIGH accuracy is displayed. An RNAV(GNSS) approach, however, requires GPS PRIMARY.
  • GPS jamming or spoofing can cause NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD, GPS PRIMARY LOST and NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE.
FCTM technique
  • If NAV accuracy is LOW before the approach, use TRK FPA, and establish on the final course against navaid raw data.
  • Monitor the final approach with the blue start-of-descent symbol, FMA, V/DEV, XTK and F-PLN, confirmed by needles and distance/altitude.
  • With one engine inoperative, the bank limit can be below 30° when IAS is below manoeuvring speed; retracting flaps at the usual speeds may affect the turn radius.
Related procedures
  • FMGC faults — FMGC failure as the system failure. See the FMGC faults brief.
  • GPS interference (FCOM supplementary) — Expected spoofing during approach. GLS, RNAV(GNSS) or RNAV(RNP) approaches should not be considered; GPS DESELECT.
  • Go-around, one engine inoperative — Engine failure during the go-around. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals have no ECAM or QRH procedure for "RNP degradation": this brief is built from the FCOM SOP lists. The PF/PM turns are arranged from the SOP role labels, not from a PDP slide.
  • The SOP does not list NAV ALT DISCREPANCY as a reason to discontinue an RNAV(GNSS) approach; it does for RNAV(RNP).
  • The manuals do not say how to continue by hand when the PF-side FD is the one lost; they say only to use the appropriate remaining AP/FD.
  • RNP AR contingency detail is in the Airbus ACD and airline procedures, which are not in the supplied books.

ELEC EMER CONFIG · FFS 5

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee A

Both AC main buses are lost. The RAT drives the emergency generator, leaving essentially CM1 instruments, VHF1/HF1/ATC1 and alternate law (direct law with gear down). CM1 flies manually as PF while the PM works the ECAM; after STATUS the crew uses the QRH summary to decide, prepare and fly the approach at no less than 140 kt.

In FFS 5 Trainee A performs it in either branch; if both trainees are co-pilots, the malfunction is removed after the procedures. Trainee B performs it only if both trainees are captains.

    • FAC 1OFF THEN ON
    • BUS TIEAUTO
    • APU (IF AVAIL)START
    • Not before 45 s after the generators were lost; below FL 250
    • BLOWER + EXTRACTOVRD

  1. 5.1 PM

  2. 5.2 PF

  1. 6.1 PF

  1. 7.1 PF

  1. 8.1 PF

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure, STATUS and QRH

ECAM procedure
  1. LAND ASAP (red)
  2. MIN RAT SPEED140 KT
  3. Caution The RAT is able to supply the EMER GEN down to 125 kt, however it may not be able to supply the EMER GEN during flare at these speeds.
  4. GEN 1 + 2OFF THEN ONTurn off then on all generators one after the other.
  5. IF UNSUCCESSFUL:
  6. BUS TIEOFF
  7. GEN 1 + 2OFF THEN ONIf any generator reset is successful, reset both FACs.
  8. EMER ELEC PWRMAN ONDisplayed if the emergency generator is not in line.
  9. ENG MODE SELIGNEngines are fed by gravity only.
  10. VHF1/HF1/ATC1USEBoth ACP remain available; reselect the transmission key to transmit.
  11. The flight crew can recover FMGC 1, which is lost temporarily, through the MCDU MENU page.
  12. FUEL GRVTY FEED — avoid negative G

  14. FAC 1OFF THEN ONRudder trim recovered, no indication.
  15. BUS TIEAUTO

  17. BLOWER + EXTRACTOVRD
  18. FUEL CONSUMPT INCRSD · FMS PRED UNRELIABLE

SYS REMAINING — highlights
On EMER GEN / on batteries
  • ND1 lost on batteries; PFD1, upper ECAM, DMC 1/3, SDAC 1/FWC 1 normal (lost below 50 kt on ground).
  • IR, ADR, VOR, MMR, DME, ATC N°1 only (DME, ATC, ADF lost on batteries). IR2/IR3 lost 5 min after main generators fail unless IR3 replaces IR1.
  • FMGC, MCDU, FAC N°1 only (lost on batteries); FCU ch 1 only.
  • ELAC, SEC, FCDC, SFCC N°1 only.
  • HF1 and CVR lost on batteries; VHF1, RMP1, ACPs, interphone normal.
  • ENG FIRE EXT bottle 1 only; IGNITION A only; MAN PRESS CTL inop.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2 are not supplied.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 8.

  • RAT extends automatically when AC BUS 1 and 2 are lost above 100 kt; blue hydraulics drive the EMER GEN, which supplies AC ESS and (via ESS TR) DC ESS.
  • If the RAT stalls, the network transfers to the batteries and static inverter, and AC/DC SHED ESS are shed. On ground: DC BAT BUS connected below 100 kt; AC ESS shed below 50 kt (all displays lost).
  • EMER ELEC PWR MAN ON (guarded): manual RAT extension; EMER GEN couples 3 s after the RAT supplies it. Red FAULT light: EMER GEN not supplying power.
  • Remaining: FLY — PFD1, alternate law; NAVIGATE — ND1, FMGC1, RMP1, VOR1/ILS1, DME1; COMMUNICATE — VHF1, HF1, ATC1. On batteries FAC1 and FMGC1 are also lost.
  • Secondary failures are inhibited on the ECAM in ELEC EMER CONFIG.
FCTM technique
  • Red LAND ASAP, but approaching a poorly equipped airfield in marginal weather is unwise; prolonged flight is not recommended.
  • A clear reading of STATUS is essential to sequence actions during the approach.
  • Complex procedure: use the QRH summary after the ECAM procedure.
  • BSCUs lost: no NWS or anti-skid; alternate braking with yellow hydraulics up to 1 000 PSI; no reversers.
  • RA 1+2 lost with their automatic callouts — the PM makes the callouts.
  • Approaching 50 kt on the landing roll, all display units are lost.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] GRAVITY FUEL FEEDING — ECAM line PROC : GRVTY FUEL FEEDING. ENG MODE SEL IGN; avoid negative G; Gravity feed ceiling (HS-TXA..TXT): current FL if > 30 min above FL 300; FL 300 if < 30 min; FL 150 or 7 000 ft above departure if FL 300 never exceeded; FL 100 for JET B; Gravity feed ceiling (HS-TXU): FL 360 / FL 260 / FL 150 or 7 000 ft; At the ceiling: FUEL X FEED OFF.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Associated procedure. Protections lost except manoeuvre protection; MAX SPEED 320 KT; Respect stall warning in TAWS manoeuvres.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — At landing gear extension. MAN PITCH TRIM USE; MAX SPEED 320/.77; Manoeuvre with care; manual thrust recommended.

Unreliable speed · FFS 5

2 procedures in this group — choose one

UNRELIABLE SPEED INDICATION · SEVERE TURBULENCE

Memory items Practised by Trainee B

If the safe conduct of the flight is affected, fly the memory pitch/thrust, then level off and stabilise using the QRH pitch/thrust tables while the PM identifies and isolates the faulty ADR. This brief also compares the QRH table with the Severe Turbulence table: unreliable speed gives pitch and thrust to fly without trusting speed, while severe turbulence keeps the AP on and sets a target speed/Mach with a reference N1.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. ADR CHECK PROC APPLY on ECAM (e.g. NAV ADR DISAGREE), or crew suspicion: speed discrepancies, fluctuating IAS/altitude, abnormal pitch/thrust/speed correlation, abnormal AP/FD/A/THR behaviour, stall/overspeed warning contradicting IAS.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Most likely cause: obstruction of pitot and/or static probes; probes rarely clog identically, so the first sign is usually a discrepancy between CAPT PFD, F/O PFD and STBY.
  • Systems vote across three ADRs; two consistent but wrong ADRs can out-vote the correct one (e.g. two pitots blocked the same way).
  • Above FL 250 unreliable speed is mostly temporary (water/ice) and clears in minutes; at low altitude it is mostly permanent.
  • Erroneous barometric altitude affects FPV, V/S and the transponder — advise ATC.
FCTM technique
  • Two objectives: fly the aircraft, then identify and isolate the affected ADR(s).
  • Apply the memory items when in doubt about flying safely in the short term with current parameters.
  • Rely on the STALL warning — it is AOA-based and not affected by erroneous airspeed.
  • Do not instinctively reject an outlier ADR: two or even three ADRs can give identical but erroneous data.
  • Change one parameter at a time (speed, altitude or configuration); GPS altitude is on the MCDU GPS MONITOR page.
  • Approach: early stabilised approach; configure wings level using back-up speeds (VMAX = VFE/VMO, VMIN = VSW).
Related procedures
  • NAV ADR 1+2+3 FAULT — All ADRs switched off below FL 250. Apply the ECAM procedure.

  • PDP mentions a "reversible BUSS (if installed)". The FCOM states activation is not reversible for all HS-TX; the reversible modification is listed for HS-TO only. This brief follows the FCOM.

NAV ADR 1+2+3 FAULT · BUSS

Red warning Practised by Trainee B

Below FL 250, if the speed stays unreliable, the crew turns off all three ADRs. Both PFDs then show the Backup Speed Scale (BUSS) based on angle of attack and the backup altitude scale, GPS altitude. Fly the green band with pitch and thrust. The BUSS cannot be switched back. Do not use speed brakes, and control the cabin pressure manually.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. The three ADRs are failed. Also triggers when the crew turns off all ADRs below FL 250 because speed stays unreliable.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 1, 4, 8, 10.

  • When activated, the BUSS replaces the normal speed and GPS altitude replaces the barometric altitude scale, on both PFDs, once the crew turns off all ADRs.
  • The BUSS comes from the angle of attack and depends on the slat/flap configuration.
  • Backup altitude scale: current GPS altitude with two amber dashes over the last two digits, a GPS ALT flag, and no vertical speed indication.
  • Speed brakes change the speed-to-AOA relationship, so the BUSS may then give erroneous data.
FCTM technique
  • Before retracting the next flap setting fly the upper part of the green band; before extending it, the lower part. This limits excursions into the amber zones.
  • Any longitudinal stick input changes the AOA, so the BUSS must move. If it does not, disregard it.
  • While the BUSS is active: cabin pressure controlled manually, HUD not used if installed, FPV available on one or both PFDs depending on the ADIRS standard.
Related procedures
  • UNRELIABLE SPEED INDICATION — Leads here below FL 250 when speed stays unreliable. See the Unreliable speed brief.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Associated procedure. See the F/CTL ALTN LAW brief.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — Control reverts to direct law at gear extension. See the F/CTL DIRECT LAW brief.

ECAM procedure and STATUS: one version for all HS-TX. QRH ALL ADR OFF differs: HS-TXA..TXO also lose both FMS.

Gaps and omissions
  • "BAS" is not an abbreviation in the supplied manuals: the FCOM says Backup Altitude Scale and the PDP says Back-Up Altitude Scale.
  • PDP mentions a "reversible BUSS (if installed)". The FCOM states activation is not reversible for all HS-TX; the reversible modification is listed for HS-TO only. This brief follows the FCOM.
  • The flow order and PF/PM split of the QRH part are arranged from the QRH lines and AOP-30-30; no PDP slide gives the turns.
  • HS-TO versions omitted (FCOM P 41–42/124, QRH 26.01C).

RNP degradation · FFS 6

2 procedures in this group — choose one

RNAV DEPARTURE · DEGRADED NAVIGATION

Technique Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

There is no single procedure: the FCOM PBN chapter says what to do for RNAV 1(2) and RNP 1 airspace, and both lists are the same. A message on one side: continue on the FMGC that provides the correct position. A message on both sides or a position disagreement: find the correct FMGC on the MCDU PROG page and continue on it. NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on both sides: tell ATC the capability is lost.

In FFS 6 While following the RNAV SID. The syllabus says "RNP degradation or failure" (Trainee B: "or system failure") without naming it.

RNP accuracy, terminal area
0.5 NM with AP ON; 0.51 NM with AP OFF
RNP accuracy, en route
1 NM (AP OFF, FD OFF: 1.1 NM)
NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on both sides
Inform ATC that the capability is lost

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

Management of degraded navigation, RNAV 1(2)
  1. If one of the following messages is displayed, the flight crew should resume navigation with the FMGC that provides the correct position:
  2. GPS PRIMARY LOST on one ND/MCDU
  3. NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on one ND/MCDU
  4. If one of the following MCDU or ECAM messages is displayed, the flight crew should check the position data via the MCDU PROG page in order to identify which FMGC position is correct:
  5. GPS PRIMARY LOST on both NDs/MCDUs
  6. FMS1/FMS2 POS DIFF
  7. CHECK IRS 1(2)(3)/FM POSITION
  8. CHECK A/C POSITION
  9. NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE
  10. The flight crew should resume navigation with the FMGC that provides the correct position.
  11. If NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD is displayed on both sides:
  12. The flight crew should inform the ATC that the RNAV 1(2) capability is lost.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. On an RNAV SID in RNAV 1(2) or RNP 1 airspace: GPS PRIMARY LOST, NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD, FMS1/FMS2 POS DIFF, CHECK IRS 1(2)(3)/FM POSITION, CHECK A/C POSITION or NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • RNAV 1(2) operations correspond to P-RNAV terminal RNAV; the AIP may specify that GPS is required. RNP 1 operations correspond to RNP 1 terminal operations.
  • For RNP 1, RAIM/AIME availability should be confirmed during flight preparation.
  • If GPS PRIMARY LOST is displayed, navigation accuracy stays sufficient for RNP operations provided the RNP value is checked or entered and HIGH accuracy is displayed.
  • GPS jamming or spoofing can cause NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD, GPS PRIMARY LOST and NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE.
FCTM technique
  • Fly, navigate, communicate in that order: keep a safe flight path first, and start READ & DO actions no lower than 400 ft AGL unless the path is safe.
Related procedures
  • FMGC faults — An FMGC failure as the system failure on the SID. See the FMGC faults brief.
  • RNP approach · degraded navigation — Different limits apply once on an RNAV(GNSS) or RNAV(RNP) approach. See the RNP approach brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals have no ECAM or QRH procedure for degraded navigation on a SID: this brief is built from the FCOM PBN lists. The PF/PM turns are arranged from the general task sharing, not from a PDP slide.
  • The manuals do not say how to continue the SID once the capability is lost (for example conventional navigation or vectors); they say only to inform ATC.
  • The syllabus does not name the failure, so the brief covers the listed messages. The required specification (RNAV 1 or RNP 1) comes from the departure chart, which is not in the supplied books.

RNP APPROACH · DEGRADED NAVIGATION

Technique Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

There is no single procedure: the FCOM SOP lists what to do under Management of Degraded Navigation, and the crew reviews it in the arrival briefing. This brief leads with RNAV(GNSS) approaches with LNAV/VNAV minima; RNAV(RNP) rules are kept for reference under From the manuals. A loss on one side only: continue on the remaining AP/FD. A loss on both sides, XTK above 0.3 NM or 75 ft below the path: discontinue unless visual references are enough to proceed visually. Hand-flying needs the FD: in approach, AP and FD both off is not authorized without F-LOC deviation.

In FFS 6 Trainee A only: the later 3D RNP approach with AP, LNAV/VNAV minima and FINAL APP, after the flaps fault. The syllabus names no degradation on this approach; shown for reference.

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

Management of degraded navigation — RNAV(GNSS)
  1. Use the appropriate remaining AP/FD in the following cases:
  2. GPS PRIMARY LOST on one ND
  3. NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on one ND
  4. Discontinue the approach in the following cases, if external visual references are not sufficient to proceed visually:
  5. GPS PRIMARY LOST on both NDs
  6. XTK > 0.3 NM
  7. NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE
  8. NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on both NDs
  9. LNAV minima: be prepared to continue the approach by reverting to NAV-FPA, if the vertical guidance is not satisfactory.
  10. LNAV/VNAV minima: discontinue the approach in the case of deviation of 75 ft below the vertical path (V/DEV > ¾ dot).

FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-18-C P 16/36 · PDF 4251

For reference — RNAV(RNP) differs
  1. GPS PRIMARY must be available on both FMS, with both GPS in NAV or SBAS. If one FMS is inoperative or one GPS is not in NAV or SBAS before the IAF, RNAV(RNP) is not permitted.
  2. The approach may be continued in the case of single failure of:
  3. GPS (MMR) · FMGC · EFIS DU · MCDU · AP
  4. Discontinue the approach in the following cases:
  5. FINAL APP does not engage
  6. GPS PRIMARY LOST on both NDs
  7. Dual NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD
  8. FM/GPS POSITION DISAGREE
  9. FMS1/FMS2 POS DIFF
  10. Dual loss of FMGC or dual loss of FINAL APP mode
  11. Loss of GPWS TERRAIN function in case of inconsistencies affecting obstacles or terrain computation
  12. NAV ALT DISCREPANCY
  13. Go-around must be initiated if XTK reaches 1 RNP or V/DEV reaches ¾ dot below the vertical profile.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. During an RNAV(GNSS) or RNAV(RNP) approach: GPS PRIMARY LOST, NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD, NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE, excessive XTK or V/DEV, FINAL APP not engaging, or a failure of a guidance system.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • "RNP APCH" corresponds to RNAV(GNSS) approaches and "RNP AR" to RNAV(RNP). Both use FINAL APP with V/DEV and XTK deviations.
  • Minimum equipment to start RNP APCH: one FMGC, one GPS, two IRS, one MCDU, one FD, one PFD on the PF side, two NDs, two FCU channels.
  • If GPS PRIMARY LOST is displayed, navigation accuracy stays sufficient for RNP operations provided the RNP value is checked or entered and HIGH accuracy is displayed. An RNAV(GNSS) approach, however, requires GPS PRIMARY.
  • GPS jamming or spoofing can cause NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD, GPS PRIMARY LOST and NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE.
FCTM technique
  • If NAV accuracy is LOW before the approach, use TRK FPA, and establish on the final course against navaid raw data.
  • Monitor the final approach with the blue start-of-descent symbol, FMA, V/DEV, XTK and F-PLN, confirmed by needles and distance/altitude.
  • With one engine inoperative, the bank limit can be below 30° when IAS is below manoeuvring speed; retracting flaps at the usual speeds may affect the turn radius.
Related procedures
  • FMGC faults — FMGC failure as the system failure. See the FMGC faults brief.
  • GPS interference (FCOM supplementary) — Expected spoofing during approach. GLS, RNAV(GNSS) or RNAV(RNP) approaches should not be considered; GPS DESELECT.
  • Go-around, one engine inoperative — Engine failure during the go-around. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals have no ECAM or QRH procedure for "RNP degradation": this brief is built from the FCOM SOP lists. The PF/PM turns are arranged from the SOP role labels, not from a PDP slide.
  • The SOP does not list NAV ALT DISCREPANCY as a reason to discontinue an RNAV(GNSS) approach; it does for RNAV(RNP).
  • The manuals do not say how to continue by hand when the PF-side FD is the one lost; they say only to use the appropriate remaining AP/FD.
  • RNP AR contingency detail is in the Airbus ACD and airline procedures, which are not in the supplied books.

ANTI ICE CAPT PROBES · FFS 6

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

An amber caution: the captain probe heat computer has failed, so the captain probes are no longer heated. ADIRU 1 takes its air data from those probes. The one action is AIR DATA SWTG to CAPT 3, which replaces ADR 1 with ADR 3, unless ADR 3 is not available.

In FFS 6 A TCAS event is inserted as the failure appears.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when the captain probe heat computer is failed.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • Three independent Probe Heat Computers automatically control and monitor the captain, F/O and standby probes. They protect against overheating and indicate faults.
  • Heating protects the pitot probes, static ports, AOA probes and TAT probes.
  • ADIRU 1 is supplied by the CAPT probes, ADIRU 2 by the F/O probes, and ADIRU 3 by the STBY probes and CAPT TAT.
  • With the selector in NORM, ADIRU 1 supplies PFD 1 and ND 1. CAPT 3 replaces ADR 1 with ADR 3.
Related procedures
  • ANTI ICE STBY PITOT or L(R) STAT or AOA — ADIRU 3, which replaces ADIRU 1 here, uses the standby probes. See the standby probe heat brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • ANTI ICE CAPT PROBES is not in the QRH reset table, so a reset is not authorized in flight; on ground the standard reset rule for unlisted systems applies.
  • The manuals give no limitation or icing advice on the ANTI ICE CAPT PROBES STATUS page beyond the INOP SYS line.

Hydraulic system low pressure · FFS 6

3 procedures in this group — choose one

HYD G+B SYS LO PR

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee A

A red warning with red LAND ASAP: green and blue hydraulics are lost. The FCTM says a MAYDAY should be declared, and the ECAM actions should be completed before the approach. No AP, alternate law with protections lost, no slats and no ailerons, only the right elevator. It is a hand-flown approach with selected speed and A/THR off, flap lever 3, and a gravity gear extension at 200 kt, which gives direct law. Use the QRH summary after the ECAM.

In FFS 6 Trainee A only: followed by the ILS flown manually with FD and the landing with partial/no flaps or slats.

Go-around

4Assess and decide
  1. 4.1 PM
    • After ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETE, refer to the HYD G + B SYS LO PR summary: read the CRUISE section
  2. 4.2 PF + PM
    • Assess the situation; select a runway. Fuel: QRH OPS fuel penalty factors, since FMS predictions are unreliable. Landing performance: EFB application
  3. 4.3 PF
    • Decide; inform ATC, cabin crew, passengers and airline operations as required
5Approach preparation and briefing
  1. 5.1 PM
    • Review the STATUS page, then use the APPROACH, LANDING and GO-AROUND sections to prepare the approach and the FMS
  2. 5.2 PF
    • Brief with the APPROACH, LANDING and GO-AROUND sections, crosschecking STATUS
    • Selected speed, gravity gear, flap lever, VAPP, an early stabilized approach, tail strike awareness, braking and steering, go-around callout, configuration and speed
6Approach
  1. 6.1 PM
    • Before the approach: DUAL HYD LO PR
      • If system lost by RSVR LO AIR PR
        • RELATED PUMPSON
      • If system lost by RSVR OVHT
        • IF BLUE OVHT OUT
          • BLUE ELEC PUMPAUTO
        • IF GREEN OVHT OUT
          • GREEN ENG 1 PUMPON
  2. 6.2 PF
    • A/THROFF
    • Select the target speed on the FCU: the A/THR may not satisfactorily maintain speed
    • For flaps extension
      • SPD SELVFE NEXT - 5 kt
  3. 6.3 PM
    • GPWS LDG FLAP 3ON
    • FOR LDG: FLAP LVR 3
    • When SPD 200 KT, if L/G is not downlocked
      • GRVTY GEAR EXTN handcrankPULL AND TURN
      • Rotate the handle clockwise 3 turns until mechanical stop
      • L/G LEVERDOWN
      • GEAR DOWNCHECK
  4. 6.4 PF
    • When L/G down
      • USE MAN PITCH TRIM: control is in direct law
    • When in landing CONF and in final approach
      • DECELERATE TO CALCULATED VAPP
  5. 6.5 PM
    • Before the final approach: check the STATUS page and that all APPR PROC have been completed
7Landing
  1. 7.1 PF
    • Flare: only one elevator and two spoilers per wing, no ailerons; slightly sluggish in direct law
    • Reverser: only N°2. Spoilers: only 2 per wing. Braking: ALTERNATE
8Go-around
  1. 8.1 PF
    • MAX PITCH 15 DEG · THR LVR TOGA THEN MCT
  2. 8.2 PF + PM
    • NO GEAR RETRACTION. Increased fuel consumption
    • For circuit
      • MAINTAIN SLATS/FLAPS CONFIGURATION; recommended speed MAX SPD - 10 kt
    • For diversion
      • SELECT CLEAN CONFIGURATION
      • Slats jammed at zero: normal operating speeds. Slats jammed above zero: recommended speed MAX SPD - 10 kt

GO-AROUND

  • THR LVR : TOGA THEN MCT

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when the green and blue systems pressure ≤1 450 PSI (the alert resets if pressure ≥1 750 PSI).

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5.

  • Dual hydraulic failures bring loss of the AP, flight control law degradation, landing in an abnormal configuration, extensive ECAM procedures and significant considerations for approach and landing.
  • Pitch: with HYD G+B, alternate law has no protections; direct law applies in roll.
  • The RAT can be extended at any time with the RAT MAN ON pushbutton.
FCTM technique
  • A double hydraulic failure is an emergency, with red LAND ASAP displayed; a MAYDAY should be declared. Land as soon as possible, but complete the ECAM actions before the approach.
  • It is a "complex procedure": refer to the QRH summary when the ECAM procedure is complete. A clear reading of STATUS is essential to sequence the actions during the approach.
  • The PF is very busy flying and communicating in alternate law. Handling may differ because some control surfaces are lost, so maneuver with care.
  • The G+B approach extends the gear at 200 kt: below 200 kt direct law gives better pitch control than alternate law with one elevator and all slats lost.
Related procedures
  • LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED — APPR PROC: S/F JAMMED PROC APPLY. SPD SEL VFE NEXT - 5 kt; AT VFE NEXT: SELECT FLAPS LEVER ONE STEP DOWN; See the QRH brief.
  • L/G GRAVITY EXTENSION — APPR PROC: L/G GRVTY PROC APPLY at 200 kt. See the QRH brief; the summary includes the lines.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW — Associated procedure (PROT LOST). See the ALTN LAW brief.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — Control reverts to direct law at landing gear extension. See the DIRECT LAW brief.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXFHS-TXG..TXU
QRH fuel penalty factor, G+B SYS LO PR (L+R AIL, SPLR 1+3+5, L ELEV, RAT extended)10 % to 15 %15 % to 20 %

One FCOM procedure for all HS-TX. Only the QRH fuel penalty factor differs (see HS-TX differences).

Gaps and omissions
  • The FCTM and PDP give the sequence but no PF/PM slide for this failure: the turns come from the AOP-20 task sharing, FCTM AOP-30-60 and the QRH summary. The manuals do not say who turns the handcrank; the PM is shown from instructor practice.
  • The DSC does not label the RAT MAN ON pushbutton as guarded, so no crosscheck is shown for it; the BLUE ELEC PUMP pb is labelled guarded.
  • The MAYDAY wording is not given in the supplied manuals.

HYD G+Y SYS LO PR

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

A red warning with red LAND ASAP: green and yellow hydraulics are lost. The FCTM says a MAYDAY should be declared, and the ECAM actions should be completed before the approach. No AP, alternate law with protections lost, no flaps and no stabilizer. The key point: stabilize at VAPP in CONF 3 before the gravity gear extension, because direct law then freezes the pitch trim reference and the manual trim is unusable. No reversers, no nosewheel steering, and braking on the yellow accumulator only.

In FFS 6 Trainee A: after repositioning, followed by the landing with partial/no flaps or slats. Trainee B: followed by the L/G gravity extension, the ILS flown manually with FD and the landing with the jammed horizontal stabilizer.

FLAP LVR 3 · VREF + 25 KT · GPWS FLAP MODE OFF
L/G gravity extension
When CONF 3 and VAPP
Braking
BRK Y ACCU PR ONLY: 7 applications · MAX BRK PR 1 000 PSI

  • GPWS FLAP MODE : OFF
  • For Flaps extension: SPD SEL : VFE NEXT - 5 kt
  • When in CONF 3: DECELERATE TO CALCULATED VAPP
  • When in CONF 3 and VAPP: Stabilize at VAPP before L/G down, to be trimmed for approach.
  • L/G gravity extension: GRVTY GEAR EXTN handcrank : PULL AND TURN (Rotate the handle clockwise 3 turns until mechanical stop); L/G LEVER : DOWN; GEAR DOWN : CHECK
  • Disregard "USE MANUAL PITCH TRIM". MAN TRIM Unusable

LANDING

  • FLARE: PITCH AUTHORITY REDUCED (No stabilizer). MAN TRIM Unusable. When Flaps jammed close to zero, consider tailstrike clearance. Only 1 spoiler per wing – Direct law
  • SPOILERS: Only 1 per wing
  • NO REVERSER
  • BRAKING: BRK Y ACCU PR ONLY (7 applications)
  • MAX BRK PR : 1 000 PSI
  • NO NOSEWHEEL STEERING

GO-AROUND

  • MAX PITCH 15 DEG
  • THR LVR : TOGA THEN MCT
  • NO GEAR RETRACTION
  • FUEL: Increased fuel consumption (Refer to OPS Use of Fuel Penalty Factor Tables)
  • For circuit: MAINTAIN SLATS/FLAPS CONFIGURATION; Maintain speed close to VAPP (due to pitch trim unusable)
  • For diversion: If Flaps jammed at zero: SELECT CLEAN CONFIGURATION; Maintain at least the higher of VAPP or VLS (due to pitch trim unusable). If Flaps jammed above zero: MAINTAIN SLATS/FLAPS CONFIGURATION; Maintain speed close to VAPP (due to pitch trim unusable)

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when the green and yellow systems pressure ≤1 450 PSI (the alert resets if pressure ≥1 750 PSI).

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5.

  • The stabilizer is lost. In alternate law, the auto trim function is provided through the elevators. At landing gear extension, switching to direct law, the auto trim is lost, and the mean elevator position at that time is memorized and becomes the reference for the centered sidestick position.
  • The PTU must be switched off without delay when required by the ECAM for reservoir low level, low air pressure (only if pressure fluctuates) or overheat, to avoid a PTU overheat that may lead to the loss of the second circuit.
  • Pitch: with HYD G+Y, alternate law has reduced protections; direct law applies in roll; yaw is mechanical.
FCTM technique
  • A double hydraulic failure is an emergency, with red LAND ASAP displayed; a MAYDAY should be declared. Land as soon as possible, but complete the ECAM actions before the approach.
  • It is a "complex procedure": refer to the QRH summary when the ECAM procedure is complete. A clear reading of STATUS is essential to sequence the actions during the approach.
  • Wait for stabilization at VAPP before the gear extension, to ensure a proper centered sidestick position for approach and landing. If this is missed, the flare and pitch control in a go-around may be difficult. Disregard the PFD message USE MAN PITCH TRIM after gear extension.
  • High pitch during the approach should be expected: outline it in the arrival briefing for tail strike awareness, and monitor pitch attitude during the flare.
Related procedures
  • LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED — APPR PROC: S/F JAMMED PROC APPLY. SPD SEL VFE NEXT - 5 kt; AT VFE NEXT: SELECT FLAPS LEVER ONE STEP DOWN; See the QRH brief.
  • L/G GRAVITY EXTENSION — APPR PROC: L/G GRVTY PROC APPLY when CONF 3 and VAPP. See the QRH brief; the summary includes the lines.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW — Associated procedure (PROT LOST). See the ALTN LAW brief.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — Control reverts to direct law at landing gear extension. See the DIRECT LAW brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCTM and PDP give the sequence but no PF/PM slide for this failure: the turns come from the AOP-20 task sharing, FCTM AOP-30-60 and the QRH summary. The manuals do not say who turns the handcrank; the PM is shown from instructor practice.
  • The MAYDAY wording is not given in the supplied manuals.
  • QRH fuel penalty factor for G+Y SYS LO PR is 0 % to 10 % for all HS-TX (stabilizer jammed, spoilers 1, 2, 4 and 5); the FMS predictions are unreliable.

L/G GRAVITY EXTENSION

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee B

The gear free-falls when the handcrank is pulled and turned 3 turns clockwise to the mechanical stop. Then set the L/G lever DOWN and check the gear down indications. Do not apply it if at least one green triangle shows on each gear. After a successful extension do not reset the free-fall system; if it fails, apply LDG WITH ABNORMAL L/G.

In FFS 6 Trainee B only: after HYD G+Y SYS LO PR, before the ILS.

Handcrank
3 turns clockwise, to the mechanical stop, even if resistance is felt
Do not apply if
At least one green triangle on each gear on the WHEEL SD page
After L/G GEAR NOT DOWNLOCKED, if time permits
Up to 4 recycles: wait at least 60 s after each; then wait at least 120 s
Fuel penalty, gear and doors open
145 %

QRH 24.02A · PDF 216

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. A QRH procedure, requested by L/G GRVTY PROC on an ECAM STATUS page or after L/G GEAR NOT DOWNLOCKED.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Lever DOWN after gravity extension extinguishes the UNLK lights on the LDG GEAR indicator panel, avoids the L/G CTL message on the WHEEL SD page, and minimizes the risk of gear retraction on the ground if the free-fall system is reset.
  • Do not reset the free-fall system: this avoids further fluid loss in a leak, or a possible gear unlock if a gear selector valve is jammed UP. It may be reset on training flights; if the green system is available the reset allows the doors to close. The crew should not reset it on the ground after the flight.
  • The display may show the gear doors in the amber transit position, depending on speed.
  • With both LGCIUs failed, the gear position indications on the ECAM are lost; the LDG GEAR lights remain if LGCIU 1 is electrically supplied.
  • With gear and doors extended, fuel consumption is increased (QRH factor 145 % for all HS-TX).
FCTM technique
  • Check for the green indications on the WHEEL SD page first: at least one green triangle on each gear, with the LDG GEAR DN memo, confirms the gear is downlocked.
Related procedures
  • L/G GEAR NOT DOWNLOCKED — The ECAM that leads to the recycle branch. See the GEAR NOT DOWNLOCKED brief.
  • HYD G+B SYS LO PR — L/G GRVTY PROC when SPD 200 KT. See the HYD G+B brief.
  • HYD G+Y SYS LO PR — L/G GRVTY PROC when CONF 3 and VAPP. See the HYD G+Y brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • FCOM calls the do-not-reset line DO NOT RESET LDG GEAR GRVTY EXTN; the QRH calls it DO NOT RESET GRAVITY GEAR EXTN handcrank. The QRH wording is used.
  • The manuals do not say who turns the handcrank; the PM is shown from instructor practice. In the dual hydraulic summaries the lines are in the APPROACH section.
  • The landing after an unsuccessful extension is [QRH] Landing with Abnormal L/G, which is not covered here.

Flaps/slats faults · FFS 6

3 procedures in this group — choose one

F/CTL FLAPS FAULT/LOCKED

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A

An amber caution: the flaps have stopped. First select the speed to stay below VFE. If the flaps are locked (wing tip brake on or alignment fault), hold the table MAX SPEED. If they are not locked, recycle the flaps lever once below VFE. If that fails, apply the QRH LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED, with approach speed from the table.

In FFS 6 Trainee A only: before the 3D RNP approach and the landing with partial/no flaps or slats.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. The FLAPS FAULT alert triggers when both flaps channels fail. The FLAPS LOCKED alert triggers when the flaps wing tip brakes activate.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 8.

  • Causes: dual flaps control unit (SFCC flaps channel) failure, dual hydraulic failure, a combination, a mechanical jam, or locking by wing tip brake activation.
  • Consequences: the control laws may change, the selected speed must be used, an early stabilized approach should be preferred, approach attitudes change, approach speeds and landing distances increase, and the go-around procedure may have to be modified.
  • For flight with SLATS or FLAPS extended, fuel consumption is increased. Refer to QRH/OPS Fuel Penalty Factors/ECAM Alert Table.
FCTM technique
  • The detection on approach comes with the flap lever selection. With A/THR operating, the managed target becomes the next characteristic speed, so pull the knob for selected speed to avoid further deceleration.
  • The AP may be used down to 500 ft AGL. It is not tuned for abnormal configurations: monitor it.
Related procedures
  • LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED — If unsuccessful, and on the STATUS page: S/F JAMMED PROC APPLY. See the QRH brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • F/CTL FLAPS FAULT/LOCKED is not in the QRH reset table.
  • The PDP has no slide for this failure: the turns come from the FCTM AOP-30-30 sequence and PR-AEP-F_CTL. The FCTM says "the crew" pulls the knob; it is shown for the PF, who flies.
  • The ECAM calls the alert F/CTL FLAPS FAULT or F/CTL FLAPS LOCKED: announce the title shown.

  2. WING TIP BRK ON

  4. If slats not locked:

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. The SLATS FAULT alert triggers when there is a failure of both slats channels. The SLATS LOCKED alert triggers when the slats wing tip brakes are activated.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 8.

  • Causes: dual slats control unit (SFCC slats channel) failure, dual hydraulic failure, a combination, a mechanical jam, or locking by wing tip brake activation.
  • Consequences: the control laws may change, the selected speed must be used, an early stabilized approach should be preferred, approach attitudes change, approach speeds and landing distances increase, and the go-around procedure may have to be modified.
  • With 2 SFCC slat channels failed, pitch is in alternate law with no protections, and roll is in direct law.
  • For flight with SLATS or FLAPS extended, fuel consumption is increased. Refer to QRH/OPS Fuel Penalty Factors/ECAM Alert Table.
FCTM technique
  • If a slats/flaps retraction failure occurs during takeoff, pull the SPD/MACH knob to select the speed and stop the acceleration, to avoid exceeding VFE. The overspeed warning follows the actual slats/flaps position.
  • The landing distance available at the departure airport and the aircraft gross weight determine the next course of action.
  • The AP may be used down to 500 ft AGL. It is not tuned for abnormal configurations: monitor it.
Related procedures
  • LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED — If unsuccessful, and on the STATUS page: S/F JAMMED PROC APPLY. See the QRH brief.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW — Associated procedure, if both slat channels fail. See the ALTN LAW brief.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — At landing gear extension, if both slat channels fail. See the DIRECT LAW brief.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXOHS-TXP..TXU
If slats not at zeroFUEL MODE SEL MAN; CTR TK PUMPS AS RQRD. APPR PROC: CTR TK PUMPS OFF. STATUS: CTR TK FEED: MAN ONLYNot displayed: no such lines in the procedure

Two FCOM units. Only HS-TXA..TXO has the FUEL MODE SEL / CTR TK PUMPS lines (see HS-TX differences).

Gaps and omissions
  • F/CTL SLATS FAULT/LOCKED is not in the QRH reset table.
  • The PDP has no slide for this failure: the turns come from the FCTM AOP-30-30 sequence and PR-AEP-F_CTL. The FCTM says "the crew" pulls the knob; it is shown for the PF, who flies.
  • The STATUS line on slats locked in clean configuration names other types (A318/A319, A319/A321); HS-TX aircraft are all A320-232, so only the both-channels case is shown.
  • The ECAM calls the alert F/CTL SLATS FAULT or F/CTL SLATS LOCKED: announce the title shown.
