LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

The approach configures in steps with selected speed: VFE NEXT - 5 kt, then one flaps lever step at VFE NEXT, repeated until the landing configuration. In landing configuration on final, decelerate to the calculated VAPP and keep selected speed; no AP below 500 ft AGL. Prepare the go-around speed from the MAX SPEED table before the approach.

In FFS 6 Trainee A: three times, after each hydraulic failure and after the flaps fault. Trainee B: once, after the slats fault.

Configure
SPD SEL VFE NEXT - 5 kt; AT VFE NEXT: flaps lever one step down
Final
Keep selected speed: calculated VAPP
AP
DO NOT USE BELOW 500 ft AGL
Go-around, circuit
Recommended speed: MAX SPEED - 10 kt
Diversion with slats/flaps extended
Cruise altitude limited to 20 000 ft
Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Order and prepare
  1. 1.1 PF
    • LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED PROCEDURE
  2. 1.2 PM
    • READ AND DO the QRH lines aloud
  3. 1.3 PM
    • LDG DIST PROCAPPLY
    • Determine flap lever position for landing
  4. 1.4 PF
    • Update the arrival briefing: tail strike awareness, go-around configuration, any deviation from standard callout, speeds after a missed approach, selected speed for acceleration at the acceleration altitude
2Configure · repeat until landing configuration
  1. 2.1 PF
    • SPD SELVFE NEXT - 5 kt
    • This may take you below the manoeuvring speed for the current configuration, which is acceptable above VLS. Preferably reduce speed and configure with wings level
  2. 2.2 PF + PM
    • AT VFE NEXT
      • SELECT FLAPS LEVER ONE STEP DOWN
    • OVERSPEED alert and VLS on the PFD are computed from the current flaps/slats position. VFE and VFE NEXT follow the FLAPS lever; if not displayed, use the placard speeds
  3. 2.3 PF
    • If VLS is greater than VFE NEXT (overweight landing case)
      • The FLAPS lever can be set in the required next position while the speed is reduced to follow VLS reduction as surfaces extend. The VFE warning threshold should not be triggered
      • Disconnect the A/THR; it can be re-engaged when the landing configuration is established
3Final approach and landing
  1. 3.1 PF
    • When in landing CONF and in final approach
      • DECELERATE TO CALCULATED VAPP
      • Use and keep the selected speed
      • DO NOT USE AP BELOW 500 ft AGL
    • VAPP should be close to VLS + wind correction. If VAPP is lower than VLS, disconnect the A/THR above VLS when reducing to VAPP
    • An early stabilized approach should be preferred; approach attitudes change, so stay aware of tail strike
  2. 3.2 PM
    • LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED PROCEDURE COMPLETED
4Go-around
  1. 4.1 PF
    • Use selected speed: at the acceleration altitude, control the acceleration to the speed required for the configuration
    • MAX SPEED from the table. In a go-around with CONF FULL selected, the L/G GEAR NOT DOWN warning triggers at landing gear retraction
  2. 4.2 PF + PM
    • If SLATS jammed
      • For circuit
        • MAINTAIN SLATS/FLAPS CONFIGURATION; recommended speed MAX SPEED - 10 kt
      • For diversion
        • SELECT FLAPS LEVER 0. Recommended speed for flaps retraction: between MAX SPEED - 10 kt and MAX SPEED. Recommended diversion speed: MAX SPEED - 10 kt. INCREASED FUEL CONSUMPTION
    • If FLAPS jammed
      • For circuit
        • MAINTAIN SLATS/FLAPS CONFIGURATION; recommended speed MAX SPEED - 10 kt. If HYD G+Y SYS LO PR: MAINTAIN SPEED CLOSE TO VAPP
      • For diversion, flaps jammed at 0
        • SELECT FLAPS LEVER 0. Recommended speed for slats retraction: between MAX SPEED - 10 kt and MAX SPEED. USE NORMAL OPERATING SPEEDS. If HYD G+Y SYS LO PR: MAINTAIN AT LEAST THE HIGHER OF VAPP OR VLS
      • For diversion, flaps jammed > 0
        • MAINTAIN SLAT/FLAP CONFIGURATION. Recommended speed for diversion: MAX SPEED - 10 kt. If HYD G+Y SYS LO PR: MAINTAIN SPEED CLOSE TO VAPP. INCREASED FUEL CONSUMPTION
From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

LANDING WITH SLATS OR FLAPS JAMMED
  1. LDG DIST PROCAPPLY
  2. Determine flap lever position for landing.
  3. Repeat the following until landing configuration is reached:
  4. SPD SELVFE NEXT - 5 kt
  5. AT VFE NEXT: SELECT FLAPS LEVER ONE STEP DOWN
  6. OVERSPEED alert, and VLS displayed on the PFD, are computed according to the current flaps/slats position.
  7. VFE and VFE NEXT are displayed on the PFD according to the FLAPS lever position. If not displayed, use the placard speeds.
  8. In some cases, the recommended speed for go-around requested by the procedure might be slightly above the VFE displayed on PFD as the VFE is linked to the S/F lever position. The OVERSPEED alert will not be triggered as it is taking into account the current slat/flap position.
  9. If VLS is greater than VFE NEXT (overweight landing case), the FLAPS lever can be set in the required next position, while the speed is reduced to follow VLS reduction as surfaces extend. The VFE warning threshold should not be triggered. In this case, disconnect the A/THR. A/THR can be re-engaged when the landing configuration is established.
  10. When in landing CONF and in final approach:
  11. DECELERATE TO CALCULATED VAPP
  12. The flight crew must use and keep the selected speed.
  13. DO NOT USE AP BELOW 500 ft AGL
  14. For Go-around: (MAX SPEED table)
  15. In the case of go-around with CONF FULL selected, the L/G GEAR NOT DOWN warning is triggered at landing gear retraction.
  16. If SLATS jammed:
  17. For circuit:
  18. MAINTAIN SLATS/FLAPS CONFIGURATION
  19. Recommended speed: MAX SPEED - 10 kt
  20. For diversion:
  21. SELECT FLAPS LEVER 0
  22. Recommended speed for flaps retraction: between MAX SPEED - 10 kt and MAX SPEED
  23. Recommended speed for diversion: MAX SPEED - 10 kt
  24. INCREASED FUEL CONSUMPTION
  25. If FLAPS jammed:
  26. For circuit:
  27. MAINTAIN SLATS/FLAPS CONFIGURATION
  28. Recommended speed: MAX SPEED - 10 kt
  29. If HYD G+Y SYS LO PR:
  30. MAINTAIN SPEED CLOSE TO VAPP
  31. For diversion:
  32. If FLAPS jammed at 0:
  33. SELECT FLAPS LEVER 0
  34. Recommended speed for slats retraction: between MAX SPEED - 10 kt and MAX SPEED
  35. USE NORMAL OPERATING SPEEDS
  36. If HYD G+Y SYS LO PR:
  37. MAINTAIN AT LEAST THE HIGHER OF VAPP OR VLS
  38. If FLAPS jammed > 0:
  39. MAINTAIN SLAT/FLAP CONFIGURATION
  40. Recommended speed for diversion: MAX SPEED - 10 kt
  41. If HYD G+Y SYS LO PR:
  42. MAINTAIN SPEED CLOSE TO VAPP
  43. INCREASED FUEL CONSUMPTION
  44. Caution For flight with SLATS or FLAPS extended, fuel consumption is increased. Refer to OPS Use of Fuel Penalty Factor Tables.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. A QRH procedure, requested by S/F JAMMED PROC APPLY on the STATUS page of a slats/flaps fault or a dual hydraulic failure.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The line SPD SEL VFE NEXT - 5 kt lets the crew configure for landing while controlling the speed safely.
  • FMS predictions do not take slat or flap failures into account. Fuel consumption is increased, so the predictions are not valid.
  • QRH fuel penalty factor for all HS-TX: flaps extended 80 %, slats extended 60 %, slats and flaps extended 100 %.
FCTM technique
  • This procedure may reduce speed below the manoeuvring speed for the current configuration, which is acceptable if the speed stays above VLS. Reduce speed and configure preferably with wings level.
  • Assuming VLS is displayed, VAPP should be close to VLS + wind correction, because this speed is computed from the current slat/flap position. VAPP can be lower than VLS: then disconnect the A/THR above VLS when reducing to VAPP.
  • The AP may be used down to 500 ft AGL. It is not tuned for abnormal configurations: monitor it.
  • In the arrival briefing, emphasize tail strike awareness, the go-around configuration, any deviation from standard callout, the speeds after a missed approach, and selected speed for acceleration at the acceleration altitude.
Related procedures
  • F/CTL FLAPS FAULT/LOCKED — Leads here. See the FLAPS brief.
  • F/CTL SLATS FAULT/LOCKED — Leads here. See the SLATS brief.
  • HYD G+B / G+Y SYS LO PR — Leads here; their QRH summaries include these lines and add the hydraulic-specific speeds. See the HYD briefs.
Gaps and omissions
  • The QRH and FCOM word two lines differently: "Recommended speed for diversion" / "Recommended diversion speed", and "L/G GEAR NOT DOWN" / "L/G L/G NOT DOWN". The QRH wording is used.
  • The procedure gives no PF/PM roles, and the PDP has no slide for it: the turns follow the task sharing for a QRH procedure, and the flap lever selection is shown as shared.
  • "Any deviation from standard call out" is to be briefed, but the manuals do not list the deviations.

F/CTL STABILIZER JAM · FFS 6

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

The stabilizer no longer moves electrically. Two versions: the amber ECAM with alternate law, or no ECAM with normal law, where the QRH procedure applies. Check the pitch trim wheel first. If it works, trim to keep the elevators at neutral on the F/CTL SD page. If not, the landing is FLAP LVR 3 and the gear goes down only in CONF 3 at VAPP, because direct law then removes the autotrim.

In FFS 6 Trainee A: stabilizer jam, visual circuits, then the out-of-trim landing. Trainee B: the same landing follows HYD G+Y SYS LO PR, which also loses the stabilizer (see the HYD G+Y brief).

MAX SPEED
320 KT
For landing
FLAP LVR 3 · GPWS LDG FLAP 3 ON · VREF + 10 KT
If MAN TRIM not available
L/G DN only when CONF 3 and VAPP
Go-around
MAX PITCH 15 DEG · TOGA THEN MCT
CONF FULL (QRH, no MAN PITCH TRIM)
Do not select, to keep the handling qualities

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when there is a loss of the electrical control of the stabilizer (with or without jamming of the stabilizer). The ELACs may not detect a jam when the pitch trim wheel is jammed: no ECAM warning, normal law remains, and the [QRH] STABILIZER JAM applies.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5.

  • The ECAM alert triggers on a loss of electrical control of the stabilizer. Pitch reverts to alternate law, and the autotrim remains available with the elevators commanded by the SEC.
  • Depending on the type of failure, the MAN PITCH TRIM may still be available.
  • With the THS jammed with the alert F/CTL STABILIZER JAM: pitch alternate law with reduced protections, roll direct, yaw alternate.
FCTM technique
  • Trimming for neutral elevator provides maximum authority to the elevators. Elevators in the UP position: move the wheel nose UP. Elevators in the DOWN position: move the wheel nose DOWN. Neutral is shown on the F/CTL SD page.
  • If manual trim is not available, extend the gear after CONF 3 and stabilization at VAPP. This ensures the aircraft is correctly trimmed for the final approach when control reverts to direct law, since the autotrim with the elevators is lost in direct law.
Related procedures
  • HYD G+Y SYS LO PR — The stabilizer is also lost in this failure: MAN TRIM is unusable and the same VAPP-before-gear rule applies. See the HYD G+Y brief.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW — Associated procedure (PROT LOST). See the ALTN LAW brief.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — At landing gear extension. See the DIRECT LAW brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals say "the flight crew" uses the pitch trim wheel; the PF is shown from instructor practice. The PDP has no slide for this failure.
  • The QRH procedure has no APPR SPD or gear extension line, so the VREF + 10 KT and the VAPP-before-gear rule are shown only for the ECAM case. The manuals do not state them for the no-ECAM case, where normal law remains.
  • The QRH says CAT 1 ONLY; the ECAM STATUS lists CAT 2 under INOP SYS. Each is quoted as written.
  • No fuel penalty entry exists for F/CTL STABILIZER JAM in the QRH table.
  • F/CTL STABILIZER JAM is not in the QRH reset table.
  • The syllabus says "stabilizer jam" and does not say which version the simulator presents; both are shown.

FCTM PR-AEP-MISC P 20/32 · PDF 465

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Fire detected by both loops, or by one loop with the other faulty, or both loops ruptured within 5 s.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • ECAM inhibits non-essential alerts from 80 kt to 1 500 ft (or 2 min after lift-off): any alert in this period is significant.
  • Above 100 kt and below V1 the Captain is go-minded; a fire alert or severe damage is one of the few reasons to reject.
FCTM technique
  • The Captain keeps a hand on the thrust levers until V1, whether PF or PM.
  • "STOP" both confirms the decision and states the Captain has control — the only handover without "I have control".
  • Rejected before 72 kt or autobrake inoperative: reduce thrust and apply full pedal braking until stopped.
  • After an A/BRK MAX stop, disarm ground spoilers before taxiing; do not vacate until it is clear no evacuation is needed.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] EMER EVAC — Fire not extinguishable. See the EMER EVAC brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • Company (THAI) phraseology is used instead of the generic Airbus wording: PA “CABIN CREW, AT YOUR STATIONS” (PDP: “ATTENTION! CREW AT STATIONS”) and ATC call sign “THA ___” (PDP: “AIRBUS ___”).

FCOM PRO-ABN-MISC P 16/30 · PDF 3811 · QRH C2 · PDF 294

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Applied when considering an emergency evacuation, or when required by the ECAM (e.g. ENG FIRE on ground: EMER EVAC PROC APPLY).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Typical causes: uncontrollable fire, smoke/fumes — during taxi, after a rejected takeoff or after landing.
  • With engines stopped only the right dome light works; on batteries the crew seats must be moved mechanically.
FCTM technique
  • "CABIN CREW (PA)…ALERT" tells the cabin the flight crew still controls the situation and prevents an unwanted cabin-initiated evacuation (done in the RTO flow).
  • ΔP check does not apply after an RTO: at least one automatic pressure system is required for departure.
  • "EVACUATION…INITIATE" = notify cabin crew, press EVAC COMMAND, advise ATC — preferably in this order.
  • Until the order is given the evacuation can be deferred or cancelled; once ordered it is irreversible.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FIRE (ON GROUND) · RTO — Engine fire on ground not extinguished. AGENT 1+2 DISCH → EMER EVAC PROC APPLY.
Gaps and omissions
  • Company (THAI) phraseology is used instead of the generic Airbus/FCOM wording: “CABIN CREW, AT YOUR STATIONS” (PDP/FCOM: “ATTENTION CREW AT STATIONS”) and “REMAIN SEATED, RESUME NORMAL DUTIES” (PDP/FCOM: “CABIN CREW and PASSENGERS REMAIN SEATED”).
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM PRO-ABN-MISC P 15/30).

Failure procedures

FLIGHT CREW INCAPACITATION · FFS 7

Technique Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

The fit pilot takes over with "I HAVE CONTROL" and secures the flight path. If the incapacitated pilot interferes with the controls, press the sidestick pb for 40 s. Declare the emergency to ATC, call the purser to help contain the incapacitated pilot, reduce the workload, and land at the nearest suitable airport with medical assistance arranged.

In FFS 7 During the rejected take-off for predictive windshear. The manuals have no procedure specific to this case (see Gaps).

Sidestick pb
40 s, if the controls are interfered with
Landing
Nearest suitable airport

Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Detect
  1. 1.1 PF + PM
    • Routine monitoring and aural crosschecks: absence of a standard callout may mean incapacitation
    • If you do not feel well, tell the other crewmember
    • Other clues: no appropriate response to a verbal communication, incoherent speech, strange behavior, irregular breathing, pale fixed facial expression, jerky motions
  2. 1.2 PF + PM
    • During takeoff the PM must be ready to take over
2Take over
  1. 2.1 PF
    • The fit pilot is the PF from here
    • I HAVE CONTROL
    • If the incapacitated pilot interferes with the handling of the aircraft
      • Press and keep pressed the sidestick pb for 40 s
      • The 40 s includes the time to deactivate the AP (if engaged) and the offside sidestick
    • Keep or engage the onside AP, as required
    • Perform callouts (challenge and response included) and checklists aloud
3Inform and contain
  1. 3.1 PF
    • MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY
    • On the radio, to inform ATC of the emergency
    • PURSER TO COCKPIT, PLEASE!
    • On the PA
    • Take any steps possible to contain the incapacitated pilot; these may involve the cabin crew
4Reduce workload and land
  1. 4.1 PF
    • Consider early approach preparation and checklists reading, automatic landing, and radar vectoring with a long approach
    • Land at the nearest suitable airport after consideration of all pertinent factors
    • Arrange medical assistance onboard and after landing, with as many details as possible about the condition
    • Request assistance from any medically qualified passenger (not on a flight with only two flight crewmembers onboard)

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. No ECAM alert. Absence of standard callouts at the appropriate time, a crewmember reporting feeling unwell, incoherent speech, a pale and(or) fixed facial expression, or irregular breathing.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Incapacitation is a real safety hazard that occurs more frequently than many other emergencies. It ranges from sudden death to partial loss of function, sometimes without any symptom beforehand.
  • Definition: any condition which affects the health of a crew member during the performance of duties which renders him incapable of performing the assigned duties.
  • Pressing the sidestick pb gives priority to that sidestick: the aural "PRIORITY LEFT" sounds on a captain takeover, and the other sidestick is inoperative.
FCTM technique
  • The decision to reject the takeoff and the stop action are the responsibility of the Captain. The "STOP" call both confirms the decision and states that the Captain now has control; it is the only hand-over of control not accompanied by "I have control".
Related procedures
  • Emergency evacuation — If an evacuation becomes necessary on the ground.. See the Emergency evacuation brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals have no specific procedure for incapacitation during a rejected takeoff, including who continues the stop if the Captain is the one incapacitated. The brief follows the general rule that the fit pilot takes over, confirmed by the user.
  • The PA wording differs: FCOM "PURSER TO COCKPIT, PLEASE!", PDP "ATTENTION, PURSER TO COCKPIT PLEASE". The brief uses the FCOM wording, confirmed by the user.
  • The FCTM says press the sidestick pb "for 40 seconds"; the PDP says "at least 40 seconds". The brief uses the FCTM wording, confirmed by the user.

FCU fault · FFS 7

2 procedures in this group — choose one

AUTO FLT FCU 1 + 2 FAULT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

Both FCU channels are lost, so every FCU control is inoperative. A/THR, both APs and both FDs are not available, except in LAND or GO AROUND mode where only A/THR is lost. The PFD barometric reference goes to 1 013 hPa, so set the actual setting on the standby altimeter and make the minimum callouts from it. The QRH reset table lists this alert, so consider the C/B reset at the STOP ECAM pause.

In FFS 7 Trainee A: followed by the raw data ILS to 200 ft DH/A and the go-around (both overweight), the ILS manually without FD and the overweight landing. Trainee B: followed by the ILS manually without FD and the overweight landing.

PFD BARO REF
STD ONLY
Standby altimeter
Set the actual barometer setting
MDA (MDH)
Do not insert on PERF APPR
In LAND or GA
CAT 2 ONLY
Reset in flight
Both C/Bs pulled, wait 5 s

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure, STATUS

AUTO FLT FCU 1 + 2 FAULT (ECAM)
  1. PFD BARO REF: STD ONLY
  2. With both FCU channels failed, the barometer reference automatically goes to 1 013 hPa. Use standby altimeter, and change this to the actual barometer setting.
  3. Do not insert the MDA (MDH) value on the PERF APPR page (because the PFD altitude is referenced to STD, and not to the correct barometric value).
  4. The PM must then perform the standard callouts ("HUNDRED ABOVE" and "MINIMUM"), using the STBY altimeter.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. The FCU is completely lost (both channels failed).

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • All FCU controls are inoperative. A/THR, AP 1 + 2 and FD 1 + 2 are not available (except in LAND or GO AROUND mode, where only A/THR is lost).
  • On the PFD: altitude alert inoperative; ILS/GLS/MLS deviation scales displayed; flight path vector displayed; Mach indication inoperative; FMA lost except in LAND or GA mode.
  • On the ND: ARC mode with map (20 NM range) is displayed. Needle 1 is related to VOR1 only; needle 2 to ADF 2 only. The weather radar image may be lost; if it remains displayed it must be disregarded. In all cases the WXR RNG message is displayed.
  • An A/THR disconnection caused by a failure is a non-standard disconnection: the engines hold the thrust set before it, THR LK flashes on the FMA and ENG THRUST LOCKED appears every 5 s. The lock ends as soon as the thrust levers are moved.
  • Alpha-floor protection is inhibited when both FCU channels are failed.
FCTM technique
  • STOP ECAM before reading STATUS to consider system resets, from the QRH reset table only. Baro setting is one of the actions that needs both pilots.
Related procedures
  • ENG THRUST LOCKED — Triggers if the thrust levers are not moved within 5 s after an involuntary A/THR disconnection.. THR LEVERS: MOVE.
  • AUTO FLT FCU 1(2) FAULT — One channel only remains operative. A separate alert with its own QRH reset (02.14).. BARO REF: X CHECK.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCTM has no technique for this failure (PR-AEP-AUTOFLT covers FMGC failure only), and the PDP has no module for it. Fly/thrust items come from the FCOM layer 2 text and the DSC thrust-lock description.
  • The FCOM names no pilot for changing the standby altimeter; the brief shows the PM, confirmed by the user. It names no pilot for not inserting the MDA (MDH), shown for both pilots. It names the PM only for the callouts.
  • The FCOM says the FMA is lost except in LAND or GA mode, and also that THR LK flashes on the FMA. The manuals do not reconcile the two. The brief only states the conflict, confirmed by the user.
  • HS-TO-only QRH version of the reset (02.15A) is excluded.

OVERWEIGHT LANDING

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

An in-flight turn back or diversion may need a landing above the maximum landing weight. This is permitted only with the QRH OVERWEIGHT LANDING procedure. Plan a long, early-stabilised approach and use flaps FULL unless performance limits it. Turn the packs OFF (or supply them from the APU) for go-around thrust. Cross the threshold at VLS and touch down below 360 ft/min, then use max reverse early.

In FFS 7 The landing after AUTO FLT FCU 1+2 FAULT. Trainee B combines it with the ILS manually without FD.

360 ft/min

be prepared for tire deflation above 800 °C

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Decide and order
  1. 1.1 PF
    • Exceptional case (turn back or diversion): immediate landing above MLW is permitted only with this procedure
    • OVERWEIGHT LANDING PROCEDURE
  2. 1.2 PM
    • READ AND DO the QRH lines aloud; read the notes before the action they relate to
    • FLAP LVR FULL FOR LANDINGUNLESS SPECIFIED BY ABN PROC OR LIMITED BY LANDING PERF
    • LDG DIST PROCAPPLY
  3. 1.3 PF + PM
    • Landing performance decides the configuration: below the max weight for go-around CONF 3 → land CONF FULL (go-around CONF 3); above it → land CONF 3 (go-around CONF 1+F)
2Approach preparation
  1. 2.1 PM
    • For approach
      • PACK 1OFF OR SUPPLIED BY APU
      • PACK 2OFF OR SUPPLIED BY APU
      • Increases maximum thrust available for a go-around

        • USE CONF 1+F FOR GO AROUND
      • SPEED AT RUNWAY THRESHOLD : VLS
      • MINIMIZE V/S AT TOUCHDOWN
  2. 2.2 PF
    • Brief: long straight-in or wide visual pattern; early stabilised approach with VAPP at the FAF
    • Go-around: transition from −3° to climb uses a lot of energy and some height; follow SRS up to the displayed VLS
3Approach
  1. 3.1 PF
    • At high weight VFE NEXT may be below green dot / S: select speed on the FCU to decelerate to VFE NEXT
    • If VFE CONF 1 is below VLS: disconnect A/THR to decelerate to VFE CONF 1; re-engage and use managed speed once in CONF 1 or 2
    • Reduce speed to reach VLS at the threshold (manual landing and autoland)
4Landing
  1. 4.1 PF
    • INCREASE FLARE HEIGHT
    • Touch down smoothly and symmetrically; V/S at most 360 ft/min
    • USE MAX REVERSE ASAP
    • After nosewheel touchdown
      • APPLY BRAKES AS NECESSARY — use the maximum available runway length to limit braking energy
  2. 4.2 PM
    • When landing completed
      • BRAKE FANSON
    • OVERWEIGHT LANDING PROCEDURE COMPLETED
  3. 4.3 PF + PM
    • V/S above 360 ft/min at touchdown requires a maintenance inspection

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Immediate landing above maximum landing weight (in-flight turn back or diversion).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • In exceptional cases (in-flight turn back or diversion), an immediate landing above maximum landing weight is permitted, provided the pilot follows the overweight landing procedure.
  • Above MLW, structural considerations require the ability to touch down at 360 ft/min without damage.
FCTM technique
  • Fly a long straight-in approach or a wide visual pattern to configure early; VAPP at the FAF, VLS at the threshold.
  • VLS CONF 1+F may be higher than VLS CONF 3 + 5 kt in a CONF 1+F go-around: follow SRS, which accelerates to the displayed VLS.
  • Modulate braking with the runway available to avoid very hot brakes and tire deflation.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXPHS-TXQ..TXU
Maximum landing weight64 500 kg66 000 kg

QRH/FCOM procedure and FCTM technique apply to all HS-TX; only the maximum landing weight differs.

Gaps and omissions
  • The landing distance procedure (LDG DIST PROC) and the max weight for go-around CONF 3 come from performance tools not included in the supplied books (EFB).
  • No PDP slide covers this procedure; the QRH order and completion calls follow the general PDP QRH-procedure slide.

FUEL IMBALANCE · FFS 7

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A

A fuel imbalance may be a fuel leak, so check the fuel first: compare FOB + FU with the FOB at departure, and do not apply this procedure if a leak is suspected. Otherwise open the crossfeed, stop the center tank feed and switch OFF the pumps on the lighter side. When balanced, restore the pumps and close the crossfeed.

No requirement

Do not apply; apply FUEL LEAK

1 500 kg in flight and at landing

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. QRH procedure with no ECAM alert. There is no requirement to correct an imbalance until the ECAM fuel advisory is displayed (difference between wing fuel quantities greater than 1 500 kg).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • In exceptional conditions (i.e. fuel system failure), the maximum imbalance values may be exceeded without significant effect to the aircraft handling qualities. The aircraft remains fully controllable in all flight phases.
  • The fuel check (FOB + FU against the FOB at departure) must also be performed each time a FUEL IMBALANCE procedure is necessary, before applying it. An abnormally negative value suggests a leak; an abnormally positive value, a fuel quantity overread.
FCTM technique
  • For any message or alert related to the fuel leak, fuel quantity or fuel imbalance, the flight crew should consider a fuel leak as a possible cause.
Related procedures
  • FUEL LEAK — A fuel imbalance may indicate a fuel leak. If a wing leak is suspected, the FUEL LEAK procedure says not to apply FUEL IMBALANCE.. See the FUEL LEAK brief.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXOHS-TXP..TXU
Center tank linesCTR TK PUMP 1 and 2 OFF; ALL FUEL PUMPS ON when balancedCTR TK L and R XFR OFF; FUEL PUMPS ON and CTR TK L and R XFR ON when balanced

The center tank lines differ: CTR TK PUMP 1 and 2 on HS-TXA..TXO, CTR TK L and R XFR on HS-TXP..TXU.

Gaps and omissions
  • The FCTM has no technique for this procedure beyond considering a fuel leak; the PDP has no module for it. The flow is the standard advisory and QRH sequence.
  • The outer tank limit (690 kg in flight and at landing) has conditions on the inner tank quantities; see FCOM LIM-FUEL.
  • The manuals print a separate version for each HS-TX group. "From the manuals" merges them into one procedure, with a chip on the lines that differ, confirmed by the user.

RNP APPROACH · DEGRADED NAVIGATION · FFS 7

Technique Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

There is no single procedure: the FCOM SOP lists what to do under Management of Degraded Navigation, and the crew reviews it in the arrival briefing. This brief leads with RNAV(GNSS) approaches with LNAV/VNAV minima; RNAV(RNP) rules are kept for reference under From the manuals. A loss on one side only: continue on the remaining AP/FD. A loss on both sides, XTK above 0.3 NM or 75 ft below the path: discontinue unless visual references are enough to proceed visually. Hand-flying needs the FD: in approach, AP and FD both off is not authorized without F-LOC deviation.

In FFS 7 3D RNP approach with AP and LNAV/VNAV minima. Trainee A: the degradation leads to a go-around. Trainee B: "RNP degradation or system malfunction", then the one-engine-inoperative go-around at minima.

"CROSS TRACK" XTK > 0.1 NM · "VDEV" V/DEV > ½ dot (50 ft)

Discontinue, vertical
75 ft below the path (V/DEV > ¾ dot)

0.3 NM with AP ON, or AP OFF with FD ON

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

Management of degraded navigation — RNAV(GNSS)
  1. Use the appropriate remaining AP/FD in the following cases:
  2. GPS PRIMARY LOST on one ND
  3. NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on one ND
  4. Discontinue the approach in the following cases, if external visual references are not sufficient to proceed visually:
  5. GPS PRIMARY LOST on both NDs
  6. XTK > 0.3 NM
  7. NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE
  8. NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD on both NDs
  9. LNAV minima: be prepared to continue the approach by reverting to NAV-FPA, if the vertical guidance is not satisfactory.
  10. LNAV/VNAV minima: discontinue the approach in the case of deviation of 75 ft below the vertical path (V/DEV > ¾ dot).

FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-18-C P 16/36 · PDF 4251

For reference — RNAV(RNP) differs
  1. GPS PRIMARY must be available on both FMS, with both GPS in NAV or SBAS. If one FMS is inoperative or one GPS is not in NAV or SBAS before the IAF, RNAV(RNP) is not permitted.
  2. The approach may be continued in the case of single failure of:
  3. GPS (MMR) · FMGC · EFIS DU · MCDU · AP
  4. Discontinue the approach in the following cases:
  5. FINAL APP does not engage
  6. GPS PRIMARY LOST on both NDs
  7. Dual NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD
  8. FM/GPS POSITION DISAGREE
  9. FMS1/FMS2 POS DIFF
  10. Dual loss of FMGC or dual loss of FINAL APP mode
  11. Loss of GPWS TERRAIN function in case of inconsistencies affecting obstacles or terrain computation
  12. NAV ALT DISCREPANCY
  13. Go-around must be initiated if XTK reaches 1 RNP or V/DEV reaches ¾ dot below the vertical profile.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. During an RNAV(GNSS) or RNAV(RNP) approach: GPS PRIMARY LOST, NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD, NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE, excessive XTK or V/DEV, FINAL APP not engaging, or a failure of a guidance system.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • "RNP APCH" corresponds to RNAV(GNSS) approaches and "RNP AR" to RNAV(RNP). Both use FINAL APP with V/DEV and XTK deviations.
  • Minimum equipment to start RNP APCH: one FMGC, one GPS, two IRS, one MCDU, one FD, one PFD on the PF side, two NDs, two FCU channels.
  • If GPS PRIMARY LOST is displayed, navigation accuracy stays sufficient for RNP operations provided the RNP value is checked or entered and HIGH accuracy is displayed. An RNAV(GNSS) approach, however, requires GPS PRIMARY.
  • GPS jamming or spoofing can cause NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD, GPS PRIMARY LOST and NAV FM/GPS POS DISAGREE.
FCTM technique
  • If NAV accuracy is LOW before the approach, use TRK FPA, and establish on the final course against navaid raw data.
  • Monitor the final approach with the blue start-of-descent symbol, FMA, V/DEV, XTK and F-PLN, confirmed by needles and distance/altitude.
  • With one engine inoperative, the bank limit can be below 30° when IAS is below manoeuvring speed; retracting flaps at the usual speeds may affect the turn radius.
Related procedures
  • FMGC faults — FMGC failure as the system failure. See the FMGC faults brief.
  • GPS interference (FCOM supplementary) — Expected spoofing during approach. GLS, RNAV(GNSS) or RNAV(RNP) approaches should not be considered; GPS DESELECT.
  • Go-around, one engine inoperative — Engine failure during the go-around. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals have no ECAM or QRH procedure for "RNP degradation": this brief is built from the FCOM SOP lists. The PF/PM turns are arranged from the SOP role labels, not from a PDP slide.
  • The SOP does not list NAV ALT DISCREPANCY as a reason to discontinue an RNAV(GNSS) approach; it does for RNAV(RNP).
  • The manuals do not say how to continue by hand when the PF-side FD is the one lost; they say only to use the appropriate remaining AP/FD.
  • RNP AR contingency detail is in the Airbus ACD and airline procedures, which are not in the supplied books.

APU shutdown/fire · FFS 7

2 procedures in this group — choose one

APU AUTO (EMER) SHUT DOWN

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

The APU has shut down, either by itself after a failure (AUTO) or by the APU FIRE pb, the APU SHUT OFF sw or a detected fire on ground (EMER). The only ECAM line is MASTER SW OFF. After an automatic shutdown a restart can be considered, within the limit on start attempts.

  1. MASTER SWOFF

FCOM PRO-ABN-APU P 1/4 · PDF 2972

STATUS

INOP SYS

  • APU
More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. APU AUTO SHUT DOWN: automatic APU shutdown for a reason other than a fire. APU EMER SHUT DOWN: APU SHUT OFF sw on the External Power Panel pushed, APU FIRE pb pushed, or APU fire on ground detected.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • In the case of an APU failure or misbehavior, the APU may automatically shut down, without a cooling period, in order to avoid subsequent damage.
  • An immediate emergency shutdown, without a cooling period, occurs when the APU FIRE pb on the overhead panel or the APU SHUT OFF sw on the external power panel is pressed.
  • Some shutdown conditions apply only on ground with the engines not running: ECB failure, N overspeed and no speed. An APU fire shuts the APU down automatically on ground only. The full list is in FCOM DSC-49-30.
  • The FAULT light on the APU MASTER SW pb comes on when the APU has failed, an automatic shutdown is in progress, or an emergency shutdown has occurred.
Related procedures
  • APU FIRE — Pushing the APU FIRE pb triggers APU EMER SHUT DOWN.. See the APU FIRE brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The procedure limits a restart "after three consecutive" start attempts; the system description says "after more than three consecutive" attempts, and "should" rather than "must". The brief uses the procedure wording, confirmed by the user.
  • The FCTM and the PDP have no technique specific to this alert; the flow is the standard ECAM sequence.
  • The QRH reset table does not list this alert.

FCOM PRO-ABN-APUF P 1/2 · PDF 2976

STATUS

INOP SYS

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Fire detected by both loops, or by one loop when the other loop is faulty, or a rupture in both loops within 5 s.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The APU has one fire extinguisher bottle with two electrically-operated squibs. The flight crew controls the discharge from the FIRE panel in the cockpit.
  • The APU AGENT pb becomes active when the flight crew releases the APU FIRE pb-sw.
  • When an APU fire is detected on the ground, the APU automatically shuts down and the bottle discharges automatically, 3 s after the fire warning appears. The red APU FIRE light on the external power panel and an external horn also come on.
Related procedures
  • APU AUTO (EMER) SHUT DOWN — Triggers when the APU FIRE pb is pushed or an APU fire on ground is detected.. MASTER SW: OFF; Do not attempt a restart after a fire.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCOM gives no further action if the APU FIRE pb-sw stays on after the agent is discharged.
  • The FCTM and the PDP have no technique specific to this warning; the flow is the standard ECAM sequence with the crosscheck for guarded controls.

LOSS OF BRAKING · FFS 7

Memory items Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

Memory items for no braking on the ground. Set maximum reverse, release the pedals, then have the PM switch A/SKID & N/W STRG OFF so the ABCU gives alternate braking. Only then press the pedals again, with brake pressure limited to 1 000 PSI. If there is still no braking, use short successive parking brake applications. Nosewheel steering and antiskid are lost, so steer with the rudder and differential braking.

In FFS 7 Trainee A: after the one-engine-inoperative crosswind landing. Trainee B: after the overweight landing.

1 000 PSI
REV
MAX; may be kept to full stop if needed
Below 70 kt
Idle reverse once the aircraft can stop on the runway
Accumulator
At least 7 full brake applications

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

[MEM] LOSS OF BRAKING
  1. If no braking:
  2. REVMAX
  3. If needed, the flight crew may keep maximum reverse thrust until full aircraft stop.
  4. BRAKE PEDALSRELEASE
  5. When the flight crew sets the A/SKID & N/W STRG sw to OFF, the control of the braking system is transferred from the BSCU to the ABCU, and the alternate braking mode is activated. Consequently the PF should release the brake pedals before the PM selects the A/SKID off. This action avoids brutal braking application.
  6. A/SKID OFFORDER
  7. The PF orders the PM to set the A/SKID & N/W STRG sw to OFF.
  8. A/SKID & N/W STRGOFF
  9. BRAKE PEDALSPRESS
  10. MAX BRK PR1000 PSI
  11. The ABCU automatically limits the brake pressure to 1 000 PSI. Monitor brake pressure on the BRAKES PRESS indicator.
  12. If still no braking:
  13. PARK BRAKEUSE
  14. Use short successive parking brake applications to stop the aircraft.

FCOM PRO-ABN-BRAKES P 1/22 · PDF 3024

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. No perceived effect on the deceleration when applying manual braking, after the PF took over the autobrake (if used), during a RTO, the landing roll or taxi.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The procedure lets the crew manually activate alternate braking without antiskid when the normal braking mode has failed and the automatic switch to alternate braking has also failed. If that fails too, it asks for the parking brake.
  • It results in the loss of nosewheel steering and of the antiskid function.
  • In alternate braking without antiskid, autobrake and antiskid are inoperative. Brake pressure is limited to 1 000 PSI automatically, to limit the risk of wheel locking and tire burst.
FCTM technique
  • Sequence the switch to alternate braking in three steps. The PF should: 1. Release the brake pedals. 2. Request the PM to set the A/SKID & N/W STRG sw to OFF. 3. Press the brake pedals, only after the PM has set the sw to OFF.
  • Full reverse may be used to a complete stop if needed. Below 70 kt, when the crew considers that the aircraft can stop on the runway, set idle reverse. Unless required by an emergency, avoid high reverse thrust at low speed, to avoid engine stall and excessive EGT.
  • When reverse is reduced from REV MAX to REV IDLE, be prepared to perceive a change in the felt deceleration.
  • During a RTO: if normal braking is inoperative, immediately apply the LOSS OF BRAKING memory items.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCOM gives the callout "LOSS OF BRAKING" and PARK BRAKE USE without naming a pilot. The brief shows the PF for both, confirmed by the user.
  • The PDP has no module for this procedure.

FUEL LEAK · FFS 7

QRH procedureLAND ASAP (amber) Practised by Trainee B

When a leak is confirmed: amber LAND ASAP. If the leak is confirmed from an engine or pylon, shut that engine down and do not restart it. If not, keep the crossfeed closed, stop the center tank feed and watch the inner tanks. One tank depleting faster by at least 300 kg in less than 30 min: shut down that engine to tell an engine leak from a wing leak. Both depleting alike: suspect the center tank or APU feed line. Do not use the reversers for landing.

Landing
LAND ASAP (amber)
Asymmetric depletion
≥ 300 kg in less than 30 min
Center tank feed restored
Inner tank below 3 000 kg
Reversers
Do not use for landing; not available for landing performance
Fuel checks
Each waypoint or at least every 30 min

Reference tables

Values copied from the QRH

Indications and probable source

FCTM table of indications and observations.

Indications and observationsSymmetryProbable source
Fuel spray from an engine/pylon. For one engine side only: excessive fuel flow or significant N1 decrease. One wing tank decreases abnormally fast.AsymmetricEngine
Fuel spray from the wing. One wing decreases abnormally fast.Asymmetric & symmetricHole in a tank
Sudden overflow in one of the tanks.Asymmetric & symmetricHole in a pipe
Developing imbalance. Burnt fuel smell in the cabin. Abnormal decrease of total fuel. [FOB + FU] < BLOCK. FOB differs from the flight plan at a waypoint. Destination EFOB decreasing or amber.Asymmetric & symmetricEngine, hole in a tank, hole in a pipe, APU

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. FOB + FU significantly less than FOB at engine start or decreasing; fuel spray seen from an engine, pylon or wingtip/sharklet; total fuel decreasing abnormally; a developing imbalance; a tank decreasing too fast; excessive fuel flow with low N1; fuel smell in the cabin; destination EFOB amber or "DEST EFOB BELOW MIN"; depending on the FWC standard, the FUEL F.USED/FOB DISAGREE alert.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • A fuel leak may be detected if the FOB + FU is significantly less than the FOB at engine start or decreasing, a passenger observes fuel spray, the total fuel decreases at an abnormal rate, an imbalance develops, a tank decreases too fast, fuel flow is excessive with low N1, fuel is smelt in the cabin, or the destination EFOB turns amber or "DEST EFOB BELOW MIN" appears.
  • HS-TXP..TXUOn HS-TXP..TXU a tank overflowing (pipe rupture in a tank) is also listed as a way to detect a leak.
  • APU OFF for a fuel smell in the cabin prevents additional fuel loss through the APU feeding line.
FCTM technique
  • If the leak is confirmed from the engine or pylon, the engine is shut down to stop the leak and to prevent a fire hazard from fuel leaking onto hot engine surfaces.
  • If it is not confirmed, each tank is isolated so each wing tank feeds its own engine. If one wing tank decreases faster, its engine is shut down to confirm whether the leak is from the wing tank or the engine.
  • The 300 kg threshold allows for fuel system accuracy. A leak rate that is constant or increasing below it indicates a permanent asymmetric leak developing over time, and should be considered a leak from a wing or an engine.
  • If both wing tanks decrease symmetrically and the center tank quantity decreases, the leak comes from the center tank or the APU feed line.
  • Do not use the reversers at landing even if available: their airflow blows leaking fuel toward the engine air inlet or the brakes, which may overheat the engine or start a fire, or reduce brake performance or start a fire on hot brakes.
  • If the crew detects a fuel leak before the ECAM alert is triggered, the crew can activate the QRH FUEL LEAK procedure.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN — The QRH does not name it here. Apply it after the engine shutdown in this procedure, as confirmed by the user.. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief, which holds this procedure.
  • FUEL IMBALANCE — A fuel imbalance may indicate a leak; do not apply FUEL IMBALANCE if a leak is suspected.. See the FUEL IMBALANCE brief.
  • ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT — ENGINE RESTART: CONSIDER if the leak continues after the engine shutdown (wing leak suspected).. See the ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT brief.
  • FUEL OVERREAD — The opposite indication: FOB + FU significantly more than the FOB at engine start, or increasing.. Apply the QRH FUEL OVERREAD procedure.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXOHS-TXP..TXU
Center tank linesCTR TK PUMP 1 and 2CTR TK L and R XFR
After shutdown of the engine on the leaking sideCTR TK PUMP 1 and 2 ON immediatelyCTR TK L and R XFR ON if the leak stops; CTR TK XFR (non-leaking side) ON if it continues

The center tank lines differ: CTR TK PUMP 1 and 2 on HS-TXA..TXO, CTR TK L and R XFR on HS-TXP..TXU.

Gaps and omissions
  • The QRH does not say which ECAM procedure follows the engine shutdown. The brief points to ENG 1(2) SHUT DOWN under Related procedures, confirmed by the user. HS-TO-only versions (QRH 21.06B, FCOM ENG 1(2) FUEL LEAK P 103/226) are excluded.
  • The FCTM mentions a FUEL F.USED/FOB DISAGREE alert "depending on the FWC standard". The HS-TX FCOM procedures do not list it. The brief shows it as a possible trigger, confirmed by the user.
  • "ENGINE MASTER 1 OFF" is the PDP example of the crosscheck wording: apply it to the engine concerned. The PDP has no fuel module; the flow is the standard QRH sequence.
  • The manuals print a separate version for each HS-TX group. "From the manuals" merges them into one procedure, with a chip on the lines that differ, confirmed by the user.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. The protection trip is initiated by the associated GCU, or the line contactor is open with APU GEN pb-sw set to ON.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • APU GEN pb-sw OFF de-energizes the generator field, opens the line contactor and resets the fault circuit.
  • The APU GEN FAULT light is inhibited when APU speed is too low, or when the APU GEN line contactor opens after EXT PWR or an engine generator takes over.
Related procedures
  • APU AUTO (EMER) SHUT DOWN — A different alert: the APU itself has stopped, not only its generator.. See the APU AUTO (EMER) SHUT DOWN brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • HS-TO-only version of this procedure is excluded.
  • The FCTM and the PDP have no technique specific to this alert, and the QRH reset table does not list it; the OFF THEN ON line is the procedure's own. The flow is the standard ECAM sequence.

Cabin smoke · FFS 7

2 procedures in this group — choose one

SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE

QRH procedureLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee B

Time is critical: red LAND ASAP, and be prepared to divert immediately. Immediate actions protect the crew, stop further contamination and open communication with the cabin. If the source is not immediately isolated, start the diversion and the descent to FL 100 / MEA-MORA. Then identify the source: air conditioning, cabin equipment, or avionics/electrical. At any time after the immediate actions, consider REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, ELEC EMER CONFIG or an immediate landing.

In FFS 7 Smoke in the AFT cabin, then the removal of smoke/fumes (see Removal).

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Order
  1. 1.1 PF + PM
    • Smoke or fumes perceptible: confirmed visually or by smell

  2. 1.2 PF

    • READ AND DO the QRH lines aloud
2Immediate actions
  1. 2.1 PF + PM
    • CREW OXY MASKS (if required)USE/100%/EMERG

  2. 2.2 PM
    • VENTILATION BLOWEROVRD
    • VENTILATION EXTRACTOVRD
    • Avionics ventilation air is extracted overboard
    • CAB FANSOFF

    • GALY & CABOFF
    • SIGNSON
  3. 2.3 PF
    • CKPT / CAB COMESTABLISH
    • The cabin crew estimate and report the density of the smoke/fumes and the severity of the situation

  1. 3.1 PM
    • If smoke/fumes source immediately obvious, accessible, and extinguishable
      • FAULTY EQPTISOLATE
  2. 3.2 PF
    • If smoke/fumes source not immediately isolated

      • Initiate the diversion before entering the identification part of the procedure
4At any time after the immediate actions
  1. 4.1 PF + PM
    • If smoke/fumes become the GREATEST THREAT
      • REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMESCONSIDER
      • ELEC EMER CONFIGCONSIDER
      • See the REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES brief, and TO SET ELEC EMER CONFIG below
    • If situation becomes UNMANAGEABLE
      • IMMEDIATE LANDINGCONSIDER
      • The Captain can consider an overweight landing, a tailwind landing, a ditching, a forced landing, etc.
5Identify and fight the source
  1. 5.1 PM
    • If AIR COND smoke/fumes suspected
      • APU BLEEDOFF
      • VENTILATION BLOWERAUTO
      • VENTILATION EXTRACTAUTO
      • CARGO AFT ISOL VALVEOFF
      • PACK 1OFF
      • If smoke/fumes continue
        • PACK 1ON
        • PACK 2OFF
        • If smoke/fumes persist
          • PACK 2ON
          • VENTILATION BLOWEROVRD
          • VENTILATION EXTRACTOVRD
      • REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMESCONSIDER
    • If CABIN EQPT smoke/fumes suspected
      • If smoke/fumes continue
        • EMER EXIT LIGHTON
        • COMMERCIALOFF
        • SMOKE / FUMES DISSIPATIONCHECK
        • FAULTY EQPTSEARCH / ISOLATE
        • If smoke/fumes persist or when faulty equipment confirmed isolated
          • COMMERCIALNORM
        • REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMESCONSIDER
    • If smoke/fumes source cannot be determined and persist or AVNCS / ELECTRICAL smoke/fumes suspected
      • ELEC EMER CONFIGCONSIDER
      • Also enter this paragraph if the source is not identified, or if the air conditioning or cabin equipment paragraphs were unsuccessful
    • If smoke/fumes disappear within 5 minutes
      • NORMAL VENTILATIONRESTORE
6To set ELEC EMER CONFIG
  1. 6.1 PF
    • Decide to set it: shed as much equipment as possible to try to isolate the source
  2. 6.2 PM
    • Read the QRH line and point to the guarded control
    • CONFIRM?
  3. 6.3 PF
    • CONFIRMED
    • After verifying the control the PM points to
  4. 6.4 PM
    • EMER ELEC GEN 1 LINEOFF
    • EMER ELEC PWRMAN ON
    • When EMER GEN AVAIL
      • APU GENOFF
      • GEN 2OFF
      • APPLY ELEC EMER CONFIG PROCEDURE, BUT DO NOT RESET GEN, EVEN IF REQUESTED BY ECAM
    • If AVIONICS SMOKE was triggered first, the ECAM shows its specific ELEC EMER CONFIG procedure instead. See the ELEC EMER CONFIG brief for handling the ECAM and its STATUS
7Before landing
  1. 7.1 PM
    • At 3 min or 2 000 ft AAL before landing
      • GEN 2ON
      • EMER ELEC GEN 1 LINEON
      • Restored this late to recover normal braking while minimizing possible reactivation of a smoke source
    • When aircraft stopped
      • ALL GENsOFF
    • SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE PROCEDURE COMPLETED

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Flight or cabin crew suspect smoke/fumes from the avionics, the air conditioning or the cabin equipment; the AVIONICS SMOKE alert triggers; or there is a smell of smoke/fumes in the cockpit. For another ECAM SMOKE alert (cargo, lavatory), apply the ECAM first.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • This procedure includes all the steps of the AVIONICS SMOKE procedure.
  • The immediate actions are common to all cases of smoke or fumes, whatever the source. Their objectives are flight crew protection, avoiding further contamination of the cockpit/cabin, and communication with the cabin crew.
  • A diversion may be avoided if the source is obvious, accessible and extinguishable, or confirmed isolated after the immediate actions.
  • Guidelines for the source: smoke/fumes first from the ventilation outlets, or detected in the cabin, suggest air conditioning, and several SMOKE alerts will follow shortly (apply the ECAM procedures). After an ENG or APU failure they may come through the bleed system and recirculate until they disappear. Only the AVIONICS SMOKE alert suggests avionics. Smoke while an equipment is declared faulty suggests that equipment.
  • A smell of smoke/fumes similar to orange peels: suspect a toxic leak of rain repellent fluid. Similar to pine needles: suspect a non-toxic leak.
  • With VENTILATION BLOWER and EXTRACT both in OVRD, a single pack may not be able to maintain the cabin pressure. Restore normal configuration if PACK 2 is not suspected to cause smoke/fumes.
  • CARGO AFT ISOL VALVE OFF prevents a cargo smoke warning from being triggered by cabin smoke.
  • Partial shedding was removed from the procedure: shedding one side and then the other with a battery charging leaves DC 1, DC 2 and the BAT bus bars inoperative for the rest of the flight. Full ELEC EMER CONFIG lets the crew recover the normal electrical configuration for landing, particularly normal braking.
  • EMER ELEC GEN 1 LINE OFF opens the GEN 1 line contactor: GEN 1 keeps running and supplies one fuel pump in each wing tank, and AC BUS 1 is supplied by GEN 2 through the bus tie contactor.
FCTM technique
  • An immediate diversion should be considered as soon as smoke/fumes are detected. If the source is not immediately obvious, accessible and extinguishable, initiate it without delay.
  • The boxed items may be applied at any time in the procedure, but not before the immediate actions. After the first steps of REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, come back here for the suspected source while descending to FL 100; reaching FL 100, complete REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES.
  • Remain in ELEC EMER CONFIG until a late stage, and restore some generation a few minutes before landing.
  • Coordination with the cabin crew is a key element.
Related procedures
  • REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES — Boxed item: when smoke/fumes become the greatest threat.. See the REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES brief.
  • ELEC EMER CONFIG — Boxed item, and the AVNCS / ELECTRICAL or unknown-source paragraph.. See the ELEC EMER CONFIG brief; Do not reset the generators, even if requested by ECAM.
  • SMOKE AFT CARGO SMOKE — Other ECAM SMOKE alerts: apply the ECAM procedure first.. See the SMOKE AFT CARGO SMOKE brief.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXOHS-TXP..TXU
FCOM STATUS after a smoke ELEC EMER CONFIGLists CTR TK FUEL UNUSABLE; ENG 1+2 N1 DEGRADED MODE marked "IAE-powered aircraft"No CTR TK FUEL UNUSABLE line; no IAE marking

The QRH lines are the same for all HS-TX. Only the FCOM STATUS after a smoke ELEC EMER CONFIG differs slightly.

Gaps and omissions
  • The QRH line "CKPT / CAB COM" names no pilot; the PF is shown because the PF communicates, confirmed by the user. The PM is shown for the panel lines as read & do.
  • The HS-TO-only version (QRH 27.01A, FCOM P 19–27/50) is excluded, including its PACK (AFFECTED SIDE) line.
  • The manuals have no paragraph specific to smoke in the aft cabin. Cabin smoke is treated by the suspected source, confirmed by the user: FCTM says smoke/fumes detected in the cabin may suggest AIR COND, otherwise CABIN EQPT.
  • FCOM and QRH line wording differs slightly (OXY MASK / GOGGLE, CKPT / CABIN COM, "within 5 min"). The brief quotes the QRH.

REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee B

Used when dense smoke or fumes become the greatest threat. Keep the air flowing (CAB FANS OFF and PACK FLOW HI, unless there are fuel vapours), raise the landing elevation to 10 000 ft / MEA-MORA and start a descent to FL 100 / MEA-MORA. Then go back to the SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure during the descent. At FL 100 the cabin is depressurised and RAM AIR is used. If smoke persists: max 200 kt, cockpit door open, and open the PM sliding window.

In FFS 7 Listed in the syllabus as "Removal of smoke/fumes, due to smoke in AFT cabin".

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. QRH procedure. Apply it if smoke/fumes become the greatest threat when applying the [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure — a boxed item that may be applied at any time of that procedure, but not before its immediate actions.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The most effective means of smoke/fumes removal is ram air: descend to FL 100 or MEA-MORA while the cabin altitude is raised to 10 000 ft or MEA-MORA. The higher cabin altitude also reduces, at least temporarily, the smoke/fumes concentration.
  • With fuel vapours, CAB FANS ON: recirculated air ventilates the air mixer bay and other fuselage areas, preventing fuel vapour accumulation and the risk of explosion; passenger health is not affected.
  • Without fuel vapours, CAB FANS OFF prevents smoke/fumes from entering the cockpit and cabin; PACK FLOW HI gives maximum airflow. Do not shut down the packs or reduce ventilation to smother the fire. Do not deploy oxygen masks if fire is suspected in the cabin.
  • In ELEC EMER CONFIG, APU MASTER ON closes the battery contactors for a maximum of 3 min, so the crew can manually control the outflow valve powered by the DC BAT BUS.
  • If there is smoke/fumes in the cockpit, open the cockpit window to evacuate it. Due to the increased noise level, pay particular attention to visual warnings.
FCTM technique
  • The [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure: diversion anticipated (LAND ASAP), immediate actions, then — if the source is not immediately isolated — diversion and descent, origin identification and fighting. Boxed items (REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, ELEC EMER CONFIG, immediate landing) may be applied at any time, but not before the immediate actions.
  • Once the first steps of REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES are applied, return to the SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure for the steps for the suspected source while descending to FL 100; reaching FL 100, complete REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES.
  • QRH procedures: read the notes before performing the action they relate to.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE — Parent procedure: REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES is one of its boxed items.. LAND ASAP; immediate actions (crew protection, avoid further contamination, cabin crew communication); If source not immediately isolated: DIVERSION and DESCENT TO FL 100 / MEA-MORA INITIATE; Identify and fight: AIR COND, CAB EQPT, or AVNCS/ELECTRICAL (or source unknown and persisting).
  • ELEC EMER CONFIG (as a smoke boxed item) — Dense smoke still the greatest threat, or all specific actions unsuccessful.. Shed as much electrical equipment as possible to isolate the source; Remain in ELEC EMER CONFIG until a late stage; restore generation a few minutes before landing.
Gaps and omissions
  • The parent [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure (two HS-TX FCOM variants, HS-TXA..TXO and HS-TXP..TXU) is summarised only, not reproduced.
  • The PDP gives only the order callout ("REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES PROCEDURE"); the split of the QRH lines between PF and PM is not given beyond read & do by the PM. The PF descent, ATC and speed items follow the FCTM task sharing.

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Applied when considering an emergency evacuation, or when required by the ECAM (e.g. ENG FIRE on ground: EMER EVAC PROC APPLY).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Typical causes: uncontrollable fire, smoke/fumes — during taxi, after a rejected takeoff or after landing.
  • With engines stopped only the right dome light works; on batteries the crew seats must be moved mechanically.
FCTM technique
  • "CABIN CREW (PA)…ALERT" tells the cabin the flight crew still controls the situation and prevents an unwanted cabin-initiated evacuation (done in the RTO flow).
  • ΔP check does not apply after an RTO: at least one automatic pressure system is required for departure.
  • "EVACUATION…INITIATE" = notify cabin crew, press EVAC COMMAND, advise ATC — preferably in this order.
  • Until the order is given the evacuation can be deferred or cancelled; once ordered it is irreversible.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FIRE (ON GROUND) · RTO — Engine fire on ground not extinguished. AGENT 1+2 DISCH → EMER EVAC PROC APPLY.
Gaps and omissions
  • Company (THAI) phraseology is used instead of the generic Airbus/FCOM wording: “CABIN CREW, AT YOUR STATIONS” (PDP/FCOM: “ATTENTION CREW AT STATIONS”) and “REMAIN SEATED, RESUME NORMAL DUTIES” (PDP/FCOM: “CABIN CREW and PASSENGERS REMAIN SEATED”).
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM PRO-ABN-MISC P 15/30).

Engine failure · FFS 7

3 procedures in this group — choose one

ENG 1(2) FAIL

Amber cautionLAND ASAP (amber) Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

An engine fails after V1 (or at go-around). Below 400 ft the PF only flies: rudder to centre the beta target, 12.5° then SRS, gear up. At 400 ft the PF orders ECAM ACTIONS until the engine is secured, then calls STOP ECAM to level off at EO acceleration altitude, clean up and set MCT at green dot. CONTINUE ECAM takes the PM to the STATUS page, where the PF stops the ECAM again for the after-takeoff flow and a relight decision.

In FFS 7 Trainee A: engine severe damage/separation between V1 and V2, at night. The manuals have no separate procedure for an engine separation, so use the damage branch here (see Severe damage). Trainee B: engine failure between V1 and V2, at night.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Engine core speed below idle with the ENG MASTER lever ON and the ENG FIRE pb not pushed.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Flameout causes include fuel starvation, volcanic ash/sand, heavy rain/hail/icing, bird strike, engine stall, control malfunction.
  • Suspect damage with two or more of: EGT above red line, rotor speed mismatch or no rotation, vibration/buffet, abnormal oil pressure/temperature, hydraulic loss, repeated stalls.
  • Takeoff with an engine failure: the blue beta target replaces the sideslip index; lateral normal law gives some rudder, the pilot completes it to centre the target.
  • When an engine failure is detected the FMGS gives engine-out predictions and deletes pre-selected speeds.
FCTM technique
  • Aircraft handling first: stabilise pitch, speed and path before the ECAM.
  • Failure above V2: keep the SRS attitude; minimum speed V2.
  • "Secure the engine" = ENG MASTER OFF (no damage), AGENT 1 DISCH (damage), fire out or AGENT 2 DISCH (fire).
  • With AP engaged the rudder trim is managed by the AP; release rudder pedal pressure.
  • Do not exceed the EO maximum acceleration altitude if acceleration is delayed.
  • In cruise: MCT, A/THR off, set heading, standard strategy M.78/300 kt, descend to EO recovery altitude, never below green dot.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT — No damage, relight considered. See the ENG RELIGHT brief.
  • ONE ENGINE INOPERATIVE — GO-AROUND — Engine failure at go-around. TOGA + prompt rudder; SRS or 12.5°; GA TRK — terrain.
Gaps and omissions
  • Thrust-malfunction and on-ground branches of ENG FAIL are not shown in the flow; this brief covers the in-flight case.
  • Callout wording differs slightly between sources: FCOM "ECAM ACTION" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETE" vs PDP and FCTM "ECAM ACTIONS" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETED". The PDP is a generic Airbus tutorial; FCOM wording is shown where both exist.
  • HS-TO-only versions omitted (FCOM P 87–89 and P 174–183/226).

HANDLING THE AIRCRAFT IN THE CASE OF SEVERE DAMAGE

Technique Practised by Trainee A

Fly the aircraft first. Bank, pitch and thrust are the primary parameters, controlled manually, while navigation and communication continue. Assess the handling qualities as soon as possible with smooth sidestick inputs and no more than 15° of bank, and avoid the speedbrakes unless necessary.

In FFS 7 Trainee A only: engine severe damage/separation between V1 and V2, at night.

Bank during assessment
Limit to 15°
Speedbrakes
Avoid before the end of the flight, unless necessary
Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Fly
  1. 1.1 PF
    • Fly the aircraft
    • Revert to "back to basics" flying if necessary: bank, pitch and thrust are the primary parameters to control manually
  2. 1.2 PF + PM
    • Continue all navigation and communication tasks
2Assess handling qualities
  1. 2.1 PF
    • As soon as possible, identify how pitch, roll and yaw are controllable
    • Apply smooth sidestick inputs and limit the bank angle to 15°
    • This prevents possible destabilization of the aircraft

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Severe damage to the aircraft, in particular if it significantly affects aerodynamics, flight controls or engines.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • If the damage significantly affects aircraft aerodynamics, flight controls, or engines, then aircraft handling qualities may be affected.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FAIL — Engine damage: the ECAM procedure has its own damage branch.. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals have no separate procedure or alert for an engine separation. Applying the ENG 1(2) FAIL damage branch and this FCTM paragraph to one is a reading of the manuals, confirmed by the user. This FCTM paragraph is the only general guidance on severe damage.
  • The FCTM does not split these items between PF and PM. The flying items are shown for the PF; the assessment is the "flight crew" in the source. This split is confirmed by the user.

ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee B

A QRH (paper) procedure for restarting an engine that failed without damage. Check the relight envelope, set the failed engine to IDLE/IGN with crossbleed open, then ENG MASTER ON and watch N2/EGT — there is no automatic start abort in flight.

In FFS 7 Trainee B only.

within 30 s of fuel flow
Failed attempt
N2 < 50 % within 70 s
Before retry
wait 30 s (drain)

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

ENG RELIGHT — IN FLIGHT
  1. No attempt if engine damage, if shut down for fire, or if a relight may cause fire.
  2. ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFF
  3. THR LEVER (affected engine)Check IDLE
  4. ENG MODE selIGN
  5. X BLEEDOPENOutside the windmilling envelope the FADEC opens the starter valve.
  6. WING ANTI ICE (for starter assist)OFF
  7. ENG MASTER (affected engine)ON
  8. ENG PARAMETERS (N2, EGT)MONITOR
  9. AUTOMATIC START ABORT NOT AVAIL
  10. When idle reached (ENG AVAIL):
  11. ENG MODE selNORM
  12. TCAS MODE selTA/RA
  13. X BLEEDAUTO
  14. Affected SYSRESTORE
  15. If no relight:
  16. ENG MASTER (affected engine)OFFWait 30 s before attempting a new start.
  17. If N2 does not increase above 50 % within 70 s, consider the relight unsuccessful; consider a windmill relight at minimum 270 kt.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. QRH procedure, considered from ENG 1(2) FAIL (no damage) or STATUS "CONSIDER ENG RELIGHT".

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The relight can be a windmilling start or a starter-assisted relight using bleed from the other engine.
  • Unlike a ground auto start, the crew must act on an abnormal start.
FCTM technique
  • The crew may stop the relight procedure at any time if the situation requires (time, distance to fly).
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FAIL — Calls for ENG RELIGHT CONSIDER if no damage. See the ENG 1(2) FAIL brief.
Gaps and omissions
  • Envelope boundaries are graphical — use the QRH chart; values are not transcribed.
  • HS-TO version omitted (FCOM P 1–3/226, QRH 19.06A).

Failure procedures

STALL RECOVERY · FFS 8

Memory items Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

Memory item for any stall indication. Reduce the angle of attack first: nose down pitch control and wings level. Only when the stall indications have stopped, increase thrust smoothly, check the speedbrakes retracted and recover the flight path smoothly. Minimizing the loss of altitude is secondary to regaining lift.

First action
Nose down pitch control
Bank
Wings level
Thrust
Only when out of stall: increase smoothly as needed
FLAPS 1
Clean, below FL 200 and below VFE Next

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

[MEM] STALL RECOVERY
  1. As soon as any stall indication (could be aural warning, "STALL STALL" red message on PFD, buffet, etc.) is recognized, apply the immediate actions:
  2. NOSE DOWN PITCH CONTROLAPPLY
  3. This will reduce angle of attack
  4. In the case of lack of pitch down authority, reducing thrust may be necessary.
  5. BANKWINGS LEVEL
  6. When out of stall (no longer stall indications) :
  7. THRUSTINCREASE SMOOTHLY AS NEEDED
  8. In the case of one engine inoperative, progressively compensate the thrust asymmetry with rudder.
  9. SPEEDBRAKESCHECK RETRACTED
  10. FLIGHT PATHRECOVER SMOOTHLY
  11. If in clean configuration and below 20 000 ft :
  12. FLAPS 1SELECT
  13. If a risk of ground contact exists, once clearly out of stall (no longer stall indications), establish smoothly a positive climb gradient.

FCOM PRO-ABN-MISC P 2/30 · PDF 3797

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Any stall indication: aural warning, "STALL STALL" red message on the PFD, buffet, etc.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • The stall is a condition where the angle of attack increases beyond a point such that the lift begins to decrease. Above AOAstall the airflow separates from the wing surface and the lift coefficient decreases.
  • The stall always occurs at the same angle of attack for a given configuration, Mach number and altitude. AOAstall depends on the aircraft configuration (slats, flaps, speed brakes), Mach and altitude, and wing contamination.
  • When the threshold is reached, permanent aural and visual alerts ("STALL, STALL" synthetic voice then cricket, "STALL STALL" red message on PFD) are triggered until a correct angle of attack is recovered.
  • Stall warnings give sufficient margin to alert the crew in advance of the actual stall, even with contaminated wings. Stall buffet is airframe vibration from the airflow separating when approaching AOAstall.
  • High altitude: buffeting increases due to the high Mach number, and both AOAstall and CL MAX decrease as Mach increases. For some Mach numbers the buffet may appear just before the stall warnings.
  • Near the maximum altitude, margins reach their required minimum. Icing conditions or turbulence could rapidly lead to a slowdown, a buffet onset, a stall condition and, subsequently, a high altitude upset.
  • In alternate law the stall warnings are activated at an appropriate margin from the stall condition, the PFD speed scale shows a black/red barber pole below the stall warning, and the α floor protection is inoperative. In direct law, stall warnings are available as for alternate law.
FCTM technique
  • The immediate key action is to reduce the angle of attack with a nose down pitch order on the sidestick: this ensures an immediate aircraft response.
  • Minimizing the loss of altitude is secondary to reducing the angle of attack, as the first priority is to regain lift.
  • Immediate maximum thrust on stall recognition is not appropriate. Engine spool up makes the speed increase slow, so it does not reduce the angle of attack instantaneously, and the thrust increase from under wing mounted engines generates a pitch up that may prevent the reduction.
  • When stall indications have stopped and the aircraft has recovered sufficient energy, smoothly recover the initial flight path.
  • A stalled condition can exist in any attitude. Recover from the stall first, then apply the appropriate upset recovery technique.
Related procedures
  • [MEM] STALL WARNING AT LIFTOFF — A separate memory item with different actions, for stall warnings triggered at liftoff.. THRUST: TOGA; At the same time: PITCH ATTITUDE 15°, BANK WINGS LEVEL; Callout: "STALL, TOGA 15°"; When a safe flight path and speed are achieved, consider warnings that are still active as spurious.
  • UPSET PREVENTION AND RECOVERY — All upset recovery techniques assume the aircraft is not stalled. Once out of stall, apply the appropriate technique.. Nose high or nose low actions, as needed.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FLAPS 1 condition differs between the sources: the FCOM says "If in clean configuration and below 20 000 ft", the FCTM says "below FL 200", and a PDP example says "if speed is still lower than VFE Next". The flow combines them as clean, below FL 200 and below VFE Next. Confirmed by the user. The verbatim FCOM procedure above is unchanged.
  • The manuals describe no stick shaker. Their stall indications are the aural warning, the PFD message and buffet. Any training wording that mentions a stick shaker is left out of this brief. Confirmed by the user.
  • The manuals do not describe an "accelerated stall" by name. The nearest text is that a stalled condition can exist in any attitude. Linking such an exercise to this brief without further wording is confirmed by the user.
  • The FCOM gives the callout "STALL, I have control" without naming a pilot, and the manuals do not cover the PM noticing the stall first. The PDP slide shows the callout in the PF column, and this brief shows the PF. Confirmed by the user. The PF/PM split for FLAPS 1 also comes from the PDP slide.
  • This brief describes stall warnings in alternate and direct law only. Normal law, with its high angle-of-attack protection, is not covered. Confirmed by the user.
  • The manuals have no stall guidance specific to the landing configuration beyond the ground contact note, and FLAPS 1 applies only in clean configuration. Linking such an exercise to this brief is confirmed by the user.
  • The QRH has no stall recovery procedure, and the manuals give no other PM action for this procedure.

UPSET PREVENTION AND RECOVERY · FFS 8

Technique Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

A technique, with no ECAM or QRH procedure. The first pilot to see the divergence calls "NOSE HIGH" or "NOSE LOW". Assess the energy, confirm the attitude on the PFD and recover from any stall first. Then use the nose high or nose low actions as needed and recover the level flight at a sufficient airspeed.

Callout
NOSE HIGH or NOSE LOW
Primary reference
PFD
Nose high: bank
Must not exceed 60°
Nose low: roll
Shortest direction to wings level

Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Recognise and confirm
  1. 1.1 PF + PM
    • First pilot to observe the divergence
      • NOSE HIGH
      • NOSE LOW
    • Assess the energy: airspeed, altitude, attitude, load factor, thrust setting, position of drag and high-lift devices, and the rate of change of those conditions
    • Determine the pitch and bank angle on the PFD, and communicate with the other crew member
    • Confirm the attitude: nose low, normally airspeed increasing, altitude decreasing, VSI descent; nose high, normally airspeed decreasing, altitude increasing, VSI climb
    • Check other attitude sources: standby attitude indications, the PM instruments, references outside the cockpit when possible
    • If stalled (stall buffet and/or stall aural alert)
      • Apply the stall recovery procedure first
    • To avoid dual inputs, know at all times who has control. If the PM wants to act on the sidestick: announce "I have control", then press and maintain the sidestick pushbutton
2Nose high
  1. 2.1 PF
    • Takeover and disconnect AP and A/THR
    • If the AP and A/THR responses enable to stop the flight path divergence, the flight crew may keep them engaged
    • Apply nose down pitch order: as much as required to obtain a nose down pitch rate
    • In the case of lack of pitch down authority
      • Use incremental inputs on the trim (nose down) to improve the effectiveness of the elevator control
      • Excessive use of pitch trim may make the upset situation worse or may result in high structural loads
    • Adjust the thrust: select up to maximum thrust available while ensuring adequate pitch control
    • Increasing thrust may reduce the effectiveness of nose-down pitch control. It may be necessary to limit or reduce thrust to the point where control of the pitch is achieved
    • Adjust the roll not to exceed 60 degrees
    • If all normal pitch control techniques are unsuccessful
      • Keep the current bank angle or bank the aircraft to enable the nose to drop toward the horizon
      • The least bank possible to start the nose down, never exceeding approximately 60°. If already greater than 60°, reduce it to less than 60°
    • Recover the level flight
    • At a sufficient airspeed while avoiding a stall due to premature recovery at low speed, or excessive g-loading at high speed
  2. 2.2 PM
    • Monitor the airspeed and the attitude throughout the recovery
    • Announce the flight path divergence if the recovery maneuver is not efficient
3Nose low
  1. 3.1 PF
    • Takeover and disconnect AP and A/THR
    • If the AP and A/THR responses enable to stop the flight path divergence, the flight crew may keep them engaged
    • If required
      • Recover from stall
      • Even in a nose low situation, the aircraft may be stalled and it would be necessary to recover from a stall first
    • Excessive use of pitch trim may make the upset situation worse or may result in high structural loads
    • Adjust the roll in the shortest direction to wings level
    • A nose low with high angle of bank requires prompt action, because the decreasing altitude is rapidly being exchanged for an increasing airspeed. It may be necessary to reduce the g-loading to improve roll effectiveness. The bank angle indicator shows the shortest direction
    • Adjust the thrust and the drag: reduce the thrust and/or use the speedbrakes to control the speed
    • Recover the level flight
    • At a sufficient airspeed while avoiding a stall due to premature recovery at low speed, or excessive g-loading at high speed
  2. 3.2 PM
    • Monitor the airspeed and the attitude throughout the recovery
    • Announce the flight path divergence if the recovery maneuver is not efficient

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

Nose High Actions
  1. Recognize and confirm the situation
  2. Takeover and disconnect AP and A/THR
  3. Apply nose down pitch order
  4. Excessive use of pitch trim may make the upset situation worse or may result in high structural loads.
  5. Adjust the thrust
  6. Adjust the roll not to exceed 60 degrees
  7. Recover the level flight

  2. Takeover and disconnect AP and A/THR
  3. Recover from stall if required
  4. Excessive use of pitch trim may make the upset situation worse or may result in high structural loads.
  5. Adjust the roll in the shortest direction to wings level
  6. Adjust the thrust and the drag
  7. Recover the level flight
