Reference tables

Values copied from the QRH

Abnormal attitude law

The law engages when one of these values is reached.

ParameterValue
Bank angleAbove 125°
Pitch attitude, if at least 2 ADC are valid and consistentAbove 50° nose up or below 30° nose down
Pitch attitude, in all other casesAbove 40° nose up or below 20° nose down
SpeedBelow 70 to 90 kt (depending on the aircraft pitch attitude), or above 440 kt
MachAbove 0.91
Angle of attackAbove 40°

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. An upset condition exists any time an aircraft diverges from what the flight crew is intending to do.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • An upset is an undesired aircraft state characterized by unintentional divergences from parameters normally experienced during operations. It may involve pitch and/or bank angle divergences and may lead to inappropriate airspeeds for the conditions.
  • Prevention relies on effective monitoring of the environment, the aircraft energy state, the flight path and the technical state (flight control laws, system failures). All flight crew members are responsible for it.
  • When the abnormal attitude law engages: pitch alternate law with no protection (no load factor limitation), roll direct law, yaw mechanical law. Autotrim is not available, so USE MAN PITCH TRIM is displayed on the PFDs, and F/CTL DIRECT LAW is displayed on the ECAM.
  • Back within the normal flight envelope, these conditions remain for the remainder of the flight: pitch alternate law without reduced protection, roll direct law, yaw alternate law, and F/CTL ALTN LAW on the ECAM.
FCTM technique
  • The nose high and nose low techniques are a logical progression and are not necessarily procedural. The sequence is guidance only: a series of options to consider depending on the situation. The crew may apply these actions or part of them, mainly if the recovery is effective.
  • Troubleshooting the cause of the upset is secondary to initiating the recovery, but the pilot must still recognize and confirm the situation first.
  • All upset recovery techniques assume the aircraft is not stalled. When needed, recover from the stall first.
  • The PFD is a primary reference for recovery. Even in extreme attitudes, some portion of the sky or ground indications is present on the pitch scale, and the bank indicator gives the aircraft bank.
  • Avoid exaggerated control inputs through reflex responses. Inputs must be smooth, positive and proportional to the amount and rate of pitch, roll or yaw experienced.
  • Aggressive and opposite flight control inputs must not be applied: they can lead to loads higher than the limit and result in structural damage or failure. If you sense an over control, set the sidestick to the neutral position.
  • The rudder should not be used to induce roll, or to counter roll induced by any type of turbulence.
Related procedures
  • [MEM] STALL RECOVERY — A stalled condition can exist in any attitude and takes priority over the upset actions.. NOSE DOWN PITCH CONTROL: APPLY; BANK: WINGS LEVEL; When out of stall: thrust, speedbrakes, flight path.
  • LOW ENERGY — The "SPEED, SPEED, SPEED" aural alert (if installed) announces a low energy situation. See Gaps.. Increase the thrust and/or adjust the pitch depending on the situation, until the aural alert stops; Available in CONF 2, 3 and FULL; Inhibited when TOGA is selected, below 100 ft RA, above 2 000 ft RA, at alpha floor or a ground proximity warning system alert, in alternate or direct law, or if both radio altimeters fail.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals have no ECAM or QRH procedure for an upset. This brief uses the FCTM technique and the PDP slides. Including it as a brief is confirmed by the user.
  • The manuals do not describe inverted flight by name. The nearest text is the nose low technique and the abnormal attitude law above 125° of bank. Linking such an exercise to this brief without further wording is confirmed by the user.
  • The FCTM says the PF applies the required actions but says "flight crew" for the pitch trim. The PF on the pitch trim wheel is instructor practice, not from the manuals.
  • The FCOM system description applies the low energy aural alert to ALL, but another FCOM page heads it "IF INSTALLED", the FCTM says "if available", and the IF INSTALLED table in FCOM GEN has no row for it. Whether HS-TX aircraft have it is unconfirmed. Keeping the Related entry on that basis is confirmed by the user.
  • The manuals do not describe a nose high, low energy exercise by name. Linking such an exercise to this brief, which says to recover from any stall first, is confirmed by the user.
  • The manuals give no callout wording for the PM announcing an inefficient recovery, beyond "NOSE HIGH" and "NOSE LOW".
  • The PDP lists the takeover step as "(if required)" where the FCTM figure relies on its note (1); the meaning is the same. The FCTM figure also places the pitch trim note in the nose low actions, and the PDP nose low slides do not show it. This brief follows the FCTM.
  • After recovery, the PDP slide shows yaw mechanical control, and the FCOM says the yaw alternate law is active. This brief follows the FCOM.

Failure procedures

ELEC IDG 1(2) OIL LO PR/OVHT · FFS 9

Amber caution Practised by Trainee A

An amber caution: the IDG oil pressure is low or its oil is above 180 °C. Disconnect the IDG with its guarded pushbutton after a crosscheck, pressing until the GEN FAULT light comes on and for no more than 3 s. Only maintenance can reconnect it. If available, the APU may be started and the APU GEN used; on an ETOPS flight, start the APU and use its electrical channel. Landing capability drops to CAT 3 SINGLE.

In FFS 9 IDG 2 overheat at 15 min to EEP, then use of the APU (see the APU phase).

Verbatim procedure, STATUS

ELEC IDG 1(2) OIL LO PR/OVHT
  1. IDG (AFFECTED)OFF
  2. If the associated engine is running, the IDG must be disconnected from the engine at or above idle to prevent damage to the disconnect mechanism.
  3. The IDG disconnection is inhibited, when the engine is stopped or below idle. Press the IDG pb-sw until the GEN FAULT light comes on. However, do not press for more than 3 s, to avoid damage to the disconnect solenoid. The IDG FAULT light goes off, when the IDG is disconnected.
  4. When the IDG is disconnected before takeoff, the oil temperature of the affected IDG may reach a higher value than during normal operations, but without exceeding 150 °C.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. ELEC IDG 1(2) OIL LO PR: the IDG oil pressure is low. ELEC IDG 1(2) OIL OVHT: the IDG outlet oil temperature rises above 180 °C.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10.

  • The IDG FAULT light comes on if the oil outlet overheats above 180 °C or the oil pressure is low; it goes off when the IDG is disconnected.
  • Pressing the IDG pb-sw disconnects the IDG from its driveshaft, and only maintenance personnel can reconnect it. Disconnect only with the engine running or windmilling. An automatic thermal disconnection occurs at 200 °C.
  • GEN 1 and 2 have priority over the APU generator. The APU generator can supply the entire network.
  • In flight, the APU backs up the electrical system. APU starting is permitted throughout the normal flight envelope.
FCTM technique
  • ETOPS flights, engine or IDG failure: start the APU and use the APU electrical channel.
  • ETOPS flights, one IDG failed: a diversion is required in the case of blue hydraulic circuit low level, low pressure or overheat, APU no start, APU or APU generator inoperative, or a second IDG failure.
Related procedures
  • ELEC IDG 1(2) DISCONNECTED — Triggers when the IDG is disconnected.. Crew awareness; Same STATUS: APU may be started and APU GEN used; CAT 3 SINGLE ONLY.
  • IDG OIL TEMP advisory — ECAM advisory at IDG OIL TEMP ≥ 147 °C, before the overheat alert.. Reduce IDG load, if possible (GALLEY or GEN OFF); If required, restore when the temperature has dropped; Restrict generator use to a short time, if the temperature rises again excessively.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCTM ELEC chapter covers only the emergency electrical configuration, and no PDP module covers this alert; the flow is the standard ECAM sequence.
  • The QRH reset table has no entry for this alert, and the FCOM says only maintenance personnel can reconnect the IDG.
  • The manuals name no role for the APU start. Confirmed by the user: the PM. The APU switch lines come from the normal cockpit preparation SOP.
  • The HS-TO version of this procedure (FCOM P 118–119/122) is not used.

FMGC 1(2) FAULT · FMGC 1+2 FAULT · FFS 9

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A

One FMGC failing leaves the other running everything (single mode): recover the AP on the other side, put both NDs on the same range and mode, and reset the failed FMGC from the QRH. Both FMGCs failing drops AP/FD and A/THR: try to re-engage them, otherwise fly manual thrust with FDs off and TRK/FPA, tune navaids on the RMPs, reset per QRH, and use MCDU BACK UP NAV.

In FFS 9 Listed in the syllabus as "navigation failure, both FMGS fault", on entering the ETOPS area. Use the dual FMGC part of the flow.

C/B pull
10 s, then push
Re-engage AP/FD
1 min after PLEASE WAIT clears
Resets
only per QRH table

Handling flow

Who does what, phase by phase

PhasePF · flies, navigates, communicatesPM · reads and does
1Single FMGC failure (demo FMGC 1 / FMGC 2)
  1. 1.1 PF
    • Golden rules: fly, navigate, communicate; appropriate level of automation
    • AP1 and FD1 lost (affected side) → engage AP2; A/THR stays
    • Do not use the MCDU until PLEASE WAIT clears
  2. 1.2 PM
    • Select the same range and mode on both NDs (SET OFFSIDE RNG/MODE → OFFSIDE FM CONTROL)
    • Failed-side MCDU reverts to MCDU MENU; exit by selecting any MCDU page (healthy FM in force)
    • Both FDs now driven by the operative FMGC; any MCDU entry goes to it
2Reset the failed FMGC (QRH 02.12)
  1. 2.1 PM
    • CONFIRM?
    • Before each C/B action: PM points to the C/B, PF answers “CONFIRMED”
  2. 2.2 PF
    • CONFIRMED
  3. 2.3 PM
    • If FMGC 1 is affected
      • AP 2 pbON
      • FD 1 pbOFF
      • C/B B02 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 1) on 49VUPULL — wait 10 s — PUSH
    • If FMGC 2 is affected
      • AP 1 pbON
      • FD 2 pbOFF
      • C/B M17 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 2) on 121VUPULL — wait 10 s — PUSH
  4. 2.4 PF
    • Wait 1 min after PLEASE WAIT disappears before re-engaging FD/AP of the reset FMGC
3Dual FMGC failure
  1. 3.1 PF
    • FMGC auto-reset may occur; when the ECAM is confirmed apply ECAM/OEB actions and the abnormal task sharing
    • AP/FD and A/THR disconnect — try to re-engage both
    • Not recovered: move thrust levers for manual thrust; FDs OFF; TRK/FPA (bird)
  2. 3.2 PM
    • Tune navaids on the RMPs
    • Check the QRH system reset table, then reset per QRH 02.12
    • Not recovered: MCDU MENU → BACK UP NAV (simplified IRS/GPS navigation)

AUTO FLT — BOTH MCDU LOCKED OR BLANK OR FMGC MALFUNCTION (in flight)
  1. If FMGC 1 is affected:
  2. AP 2 pbON
  3. FD 1 pbOFF
  4. C/B B02 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 1) — on 49VUPULL
  5. Wait 10 s
  6. C/B B02 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 1)PUSH
  7. Caution Wait 1 min after the PLEASE WAIT message disappears from the MCDU, before engaging or re-engaging the FD and the AP of reset FMGC.
  8. If FMGC 2 is affected:
  9. AP 1 pbON
  10. FD 2 pbOFF
  11. C/B M17 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 2) — on 121VUPULL
  12. Wait 10 s
  13. C/B M17 (AUTO FLT / FMGC / 2)PUSH
  14. Caution Wait 1 min after the PLEASE WAIT message disappears from the MCDU, before engaging or re-engaging the FD and the AP of reset FMGC.
  15. If the FMGC reset is not successful, consider FMGC reset with engines not running.

System reset — general
In flight
  • Reset authorized only if an ECAM/OEB/FCOM/QRH procedure requests it, or the alert/malfunction is listed and authorized in the system reset table.
  • Only one reset at a time unless the procedure says otherwise.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Single or dual FMGC failure. Handled from the FCTM technique, the FMGS degraded modes and the QRH system reset table (AUTO FLT — BOTH MCDU LOCKED OR BLANK OR FMGC MALFUNCTION).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Single mode: the failed FMGC shows OPP FMGC IN PROCESS; its ND shows MAP NOT AVAIL / SET OFFSIDE RNG/MODE, or OFFSIDE FM CONTROL when ranges match.
  • If one FMGC fails, the remaining FMGC controls the radio receivers on both sides; if both fail, use the RMPs.
  • BACK UP NAV gives flight planning, position from IRS/GPIRS, F-PLN on ND and sequencing — no AP/FD NAV mode.
FCTM technique
  • Single failure: recover flight-plan display on the affected ND by using the same range as the opposite ND; consider a reset per QRH.
  • Dual failure: if the FG part is still available, the AP may remain engaged and revert to HDG-V/S or TRK-FPA (FG standard dependent).
Gaps and omissions
  • No ECAM procedure titled FMGC 1(2) FAULT exists in the supplied FCOM; the brief uses FCTM, FCOM DSC and QRH reset content.
  • FCOM DSC-22_20-40-10 manual FMGC reset / resynchronisation not expanded here.

Engine failure · FFS 9

2 procedures in this group — choose one

ENG 1(2) FAIL

Amber cautionLAND ASAP (amber) Practised by Trainee A

An engine fails after V1 (or at go-around). Below 400 ft the PF only flies: rudder to centre the beta target, 12.5° then SRS, gear up. At 400 ft the PF orders ECAM ACTIONS until the engine is secured, then calls STOP ECAM to level off at EO acceleration altitude, clean up and set MCT at green dot. CONTINUE ECAM takes the PM to the STATUS page, where the PF stops the ECAM again for the after-takeoff flow and a relight decision.

In FFS 9 Engine 1 or 2 at ETP. The syllabus then says "strategies" (see Drift down, and Diversion for the fixed speed strategy).

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Engine core speed below idle with the ENG MASTER lever ON and the ENG FIRE pb not pushed.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Flameout causes include fuel starvation, volcanic ash/sand, heavy rain/hail/icing, bird strike, engine stall, control malfunction.
  • Suspect damage with two or more of: EGT above red line, rotor speed mismatch or no rotation, vibration/buffet, abnormal oil pressure/temperature, hydraulic loss, repeated stalls.
  • Takeoff with an engine failure: the blue beta target replaces the sideslip index; lateral normal law gives some rudder, the pilot completes it to centre the target.
  • When an engine failure is detected the FMGS gives engine-out predictions and deletes pre-selected speeds.
FCTM technique
  • Aircraft handling first: stabilise pitch, speed and path before the ECAM.
  • Failure above V2: keep the SRS attitude; minimum speed V2.
  • "Secure the engine" = ENG MASTER OFF (no damage), AGENT 1 DISCH (damage), fire out or AGENT 2 DISCH (fire).
  • With AP engaged the rudder trim is managed by the AP; release rudder pedal pressure.
  • Do not exceed the EO maximum acceleration altitude if acceleration is delayed.
  • In cruise: MCT, A/THR off, set heading, standard strategy M.78/300 kt, descend to EO recovery altitude, never below green dot.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] ENG RELIGHT IN FLIGHT — No damage, relight considered. See the ENG RELIGHT brief.
  • ONE ENGINE INOPERATIVE — GO-AROUND — Engine failure at go-around. TOGA + prompt rudder; SRS or 12.5°; GA TRK — terrain.
Gaps and omissions
  • Thrust-malfunction and on-ground branches of ENG FAIL are not shown in the flow; this brief covers the in-flight case.
  • Callout wording differs slightly between sources: FCOM "ECAM ACTION" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETE" vs PDP and FCTM "ECAM ACTIONS" / "ECAM ACTIONS COMPLETED". The PDP is a generic Airbus tutorial; FCOM wording is shown where both exist.
  • HS-TO-only versions omitted (FCOM P 87–89 and P 174–183/226).

ENGINE FAILURE IN CRUISE · drift-down strategy

Technique Practised by Trainee A

After an engine failure at cruise level the aircraft cannot hold its altitude. The PF sets MCT with A/THR off, sets a heading and determines the engine-out recovery altitude, then drifts down at M.78/300 kt (standard strategy) to the EO LRC ceiling, never below green dot. After an engine fire, the fire drill is done first and without delay.

Thrust
MCT · A/THR off
Standard strategy
M.78 / 300 kt
Minimum speed
Green dot

  2. 1.2 PF
    • ALL THRUST LEVERSMCT

    • A/THR off so thrust is not reduced when selecting speed or OPEN DES; MCT is frozen

      • Keep A/THR on
  3. 1.3 PF + PM

  4. 1.4 PM

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Engine failure or engine shutdown (including after an engine fire) at cruise level.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • Three strategies exist: standard, obstacle and fixed speed. Unless a specific procedure was set at dispatch (ETOPS, mountainous areas), the standard strategy is used.
FCTM technique
  • Engine failure in cruise: unless a dispatch procedure exists, use the standard strategy, M 0.78/300 kt to the REC MAX EO (LRC engine-out ceiling). Obstacle strategy: green dot to the drift-down ceiling, then standard when clear.
  • Do not hurry the ECAM actions in cruise — complete the drill correctly.
Related procedures
  • ENG 1(2) FIRE (IN FLIGHT) — When the engine failure is a fire. Fire drill first, without delay.
Gaps and omissions
  • No source puts the fire drill and the cruise strategy in one sequence. The fire procedure is applied without delay (FCTM), while the cruise flow sets MCT and A/THR off first and starts ECAM “when appropriate” (PDP). The brief keeps the fire drill first.

ETOPS · diversion and abnormal procedures · FFS 9

Technique Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

On an ETOPS flight, four technical criteria govern a re-routing or diversion: loss of NAT-HLA capability, diversion airports going below minima or becoming unsuitable, LAND ASAP failures, and failures whose increased fuel consumption exceeds the reserves. After an engine or IDG failure, start the APU and use its electrical channel. After an engine failure, the fixed speed strategy is the one recommended for ETOPS, with the speed established before dispatch.

Engine or IDG failure
Start the APU · use the APU electrical channel
Blue hydraulic low level, low pressure or overheat
Start the APU to ensure the APU generator
Fixed speed strategy
Speed value as established before dispatch
Loss of air conditioning
At FL 100 with RAM AIR opened: CAB FANS off

From the manuals

Verbatim procedure

Diversion decision making
  1. The technical criteria governing a re-routing or diversion decision can be classified into four categories:
  2. Loss of NAT-HLA capability, before entering the NAT-HLA area (as applicable)
  3. Weather minima at diversion airport(s) going below the company/crew en-route minima, before reaching the ETOPS Entry Point, or diversion airport(s) becoming unsuitable for any reason
  4. Failure cases requiring a diversion to the nearest airport (cases leading to a LAND ASAP message on the ECAM and/or in the QRH)
  5. Failure cases resulting in increased fuel consumption, exceeding the available fuel reserves
  6. Electrical generation. If one IDG fails, a diversion is required in the case of:
  7. Blue hydraulic circuit low level, low pressure or overheat
  8. APU no start
  9. APU or APU generator inoperative
  10. Second IDG failure
  11. Fuel system. Some failure cases may lead to fuel gravity feeding which implies flight at lower altitude or to some fuel being unusable. The flight crew's evaluation of the actual situation and the fuel remaining may lead to the decision that a diversion is required.
  12. Hydraulic system. If there is low level, low pressure or overheat on blue hydraulic circuit, a diversion is required in the case of:
  13. One IDG failure
  14. APU no start
  15. APU/APU GEN failure
  16. APU. If APU/APU GEN fails, a diversion is required in the case of:
  17. Blue hydraulic circuit low level, low pressure or overheat
  18. One IDG failure

FCOM PRO-SPO-40-40 P 1/2 · PDF 4586

ETOPS abnormal and emergency procedures
  1. ELECTRICAL EMERGENCY CONFIGURATION. Complete the ECAM procedure using the following:
  2. AIR CONDITIONING: As cockpit and cabin temperature control is lost, it is recommended to open the cockpit door.
  3. FUEL: As all fuel pumps are lost, the engines are fed by gravity. Refer to GRVTY FUEL FEEDING Procedure.
  4. ENGINE ANTI-ICE: Engine anti-ice valves are permanently open, although the ECAM memo ENG A. ICE is not displayed on the ECAM (except if the ENG A. ICE pb is at ON).
  5. WING ANTI-ICE: If only one ENG BLEED is available, PACK 1 must be switched OFF, to avoid having both packs and wing anti-ice supplied by a single bleed source.
  6. ENGINE: As the engines are in degraded N1 mode, the power setting has to be done using tables.
  7. BLUE HYDRAULIC CIRCUIT LOW LEVEL OR LOW PRESSURE OR OVERHEAT: Start the APU to ensure availability of the APU generator.
  8. ENGINE OR IDG FAILURE: Start the APU and use the APU electrical channel.
  9. LOSS OF AIR CONDITIONING: In the case of loss of the air conditioning capability (loss of both packs, loss of both bleeds without APU bleed etc.), when at FL 100 with the RAM AIR opened, the CAB FANS must be switched off.

FCOM PRO-SPO-40-50 P 1/4 · PDF 4588 · FCOM PRO-SPO-40-50 P 2/4 · PDF 4589

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. A failure, or a diversion airport becoming unsuitable, on an ETOPS flight. These procedures apply in addition to the SOP and the ABNORMAL and EMERGENCY procedures.

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • When an engine failure occurs during cruise, three strategies apply: standard, obstacle and fixed speed. Unless a specific procedure has been established before dispatch (considering ETOPS or mountainous areas), the standard strategy is used.
  • The FCTM says the fixed speed strategy is recommended for ETOPS operation and refers to the FCOM diversion decision making section. The PDP gives "ETOPS constraint" and "Speed value as established before dispatch".
  • The FCOM maximum diversion distance tables are computed for ISA, no wind, the optimum diversion level after an engine failure and a single engine diversion speed schedule, with the schedules MCT/VMO and MCT/320 kt. Obstacles are not considered to determine if a route is an ETOPS route.
FCTM technique
  • The fixed speed section of the FCTM gives no speed, thrust or descent lines of its own.
Related procedures
  • Engine failure in cruise · drift-down strategy — The thrust, heading and descent lines for the standard and obstacle strategies.. All thrust levers MCT, A/THR OFF; Do not decelerate below green dot.
  • Maximum diversion distance — Dispatch performance table; it differs between HS-TXA..TXF and HS-TXG..TXU.. See the FCOM table.
Gaps and omissions
  • The manuals give no value for the fixed speed strategy; the speed comes from the operator's dispatch procedure, which is not in the supplied manuals. The MCT/VMO and MCT/320 kt schedules are from the maximum diversion distance tables, and no source calls them the fixed speed. Confirmed by the user: no number is shown.
  • This brief goes beyond the ECAM/QRH scope of the other briefs. Confirmed by the user: add it as a brief for the diversion row.
  • No source names roles for these ETOPS lines. Confirmed by the user: the PM performs the APU start and the CAB FANS line.
  • The HS-TO versions (FCOM PRO-SPO-40-50 P 2–4/4, PRO-SPO-40-60 P 3–4/4) are not used.

FUEL IMBALANCE · FFS 9

QRH procedure Practised by Trainee A Trainee B

A fuel imbalance may be a fuel leak, so check the fuel first: compare FOB + FU with the FOB at departure, and do not apply this procedure if a leak is suspected. Otherwise open the crossfeed, stop the center tank feed and switch OFF the pumps on the lighter side. When balanced, restore the pumps and close the crossfeed.

In FFS 9 Listed in the syllabus as "Fuel monitoring and imbalance".

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. QRH procedure with no ECAM alert. There is no requirement to correct an imbalance until the ECAM fuel advisory is displayed (difference between wing fuel quantities greater than 1 500 kg).

Flight phase inhibition. Not inhibited in any phase.

  • In exceptional conditions (i.e. fuel system failure), the maximum imbalance values may be exceeded without significant effect to the aircraft handling qualities. The aircraft remains fully controllable in all flight phases.
  • The fuel check (FOB + FU against the FOB at departure) must also be performed each time a FUEL IMBALANCE procedure is necessary, before applying it. An abnormally negative value suggests a leak; an abnormally positive value, a fuel quantity overread.
FCTM technique
  • For any message or alert related to the fuel leak, fuel quantity or fuel imbalance, the flight crew should consider a fuel leak as a possible cause.
Related procedures
  • FUEL LEAK — A fuel imbalance may indicate a fuel leak. If a wing leak is suspected, the FUEL LEAK procedure says not to apply FUEL IMBALANCE.. See the FUEL LEAK brief.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXOHS-TXP..TXU
Center tank linesCTR TK PUMP 1 and 2 OFF; ALL FUEL PUMPS ON when balancedCTR TK L and R XFR OFF; FUEL PUMPS ON and CTR TK L and R XFR ON when balanced

The center tank lines differ: CTR TK PUMP 1 and 2 on HS-TXA..TXO, CTR TK L and R XFR on HS-TXP..TXU.

Gaps and omissions
  • The FCTM has no technique for this procedure beyond considering a fuel leak; the PDP has no module for it. The flow is the standard advisory and QRH sequence.
  • The outer tank limit (690 kg in flight and at landing) has conditions on the inner tank quantities; see FCOM LIM-FUEL.
  • The manuals print a separate version for each HS-TX group. "From the manuals" merges them into one procedure, with a chip on the lines that differ, confirmed by the user.

HYD G RSVR LO LVL · FFS 9

Amber caution Practised by Trainee B

An amber caution: the green reservoir is low. Switch the PTU OFF without delay, because a PTU overheat may occur two minutes later and may lead to the loss of the second hydraulic circuit, then switch the green engine 1 pump OFF. The green system is lost. Plan a gravity gear extension, alternate braking and slow slats and flaps, apply the landing distance procedure and use the fuel penalty factor instead of the FMS predictions.

In FFS 9 At 15 min to EEP. The syllabus says "restore". The manuals give no in-flight restoration for this alert, so the instructor removes the failure after the procedure.

Landing capability
CAT 3 SINGLE ONLY

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. The fluid quantity is below 3.5 l (0.92 US Gal). Inhibited for the first 15 s of flight phase 5.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • A pump driven by engine 1 pressurizes the green system.
  • The bidirectional PTU comes into action automatically when the differential pressure between the green and yellow systems is greater than 500 PSI. Hydraulic fluid cannot be transferred from one system to another.
  • Single hydraulic failures have very little effect on the handling of the aircraft but degrade the landing capability to CAT 3 SINGLE.
FCTM technique
  • In case of reservoir low level, the PTU must be switched OFF as required by ECAM to avoid a PTU overheat which may occur two minutes later. A PTU overheat may lead to the loss of the second hydraulic circuit.
Related procedures
  • L/G GRAVITY EXTENSION — STATUS: L/G GRVTY PROC APPLY.. See the L/G gravity extension brief.
  • Fuel Penalty Factors/ECAM Alert Table — FMS PRED UNRELIABLE and FUEL CONSUMPT INCRSD. The G SYS LO PR row depends on whether spoilers 1 and 5 are indicated extended.. Find the factor in the QRH table for the registration.
Gaps and omissions
  • No PDP module covers this alert; the flow is the standard ECAM sequence with the FCTM PTU recommendation.
  • The QRH reset table has no entry for this alert.
  • The manuals name no PF/PM split for the approach items here; the split follows the task sharing and the L/G gravity extension brief.

NAV ADR 1+2+3 FAULT · BUSS · FFS 9

Red warning Practised by Trainee B

Below FL 250, if the speed stays unreliable, the crew turns off all three ADRs. Both PFDs then show the Backup Speed Scale (BUSS) based on angle of attack and the backup altitude scale, GPS altitude. Fly the green band with pitch and thrust. The BUSS cannot be switched back. Do not use speed brakes, and control the cabin pressure manually.

In FFS 9 On entering the ETOPS area. The alert triggers by itself here, so start at the ECAM actions (phase 2); the "Below FL 250" limit belongs to the unreliable-speed route, not to this ECAM procedure. The syllabus says "restore". The BUSS is not reversible, so the instructor removes the failure after the procedure.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. The three ADRs are failed. Also triggers when the crew turns off all ADRs below FL 250 because speed stays unreliable.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 1, 4, 8, 10.

  • When activated, the BUSS replaces the normal speed and GPS altitude replaces the barometric altitude scale, on both PFDs, once the crew turns off all ADRs.
  • The BUSS comes from the angle of attack and depends on the slat/flap configuration.
  • Backup altitude scale: current GPS altitude with two amber dashes over the last two digits, a GPS ALT flag, and no vertical speed indication.
  • Speed brakes change the speed-to-AOA relationship, so the BUSS may then give erroneous data.
FCTM technique
  • Before retracting the next flap setting fly the upper part of the green band; before extending it, the lower part. This limits excursions into the amber zones.
  • Any longitudinal stick input changes the AOA, so the BUSS must move. If it does not, disregard it.
  • While the BUSS is active: cabin pressure controlled manually, HUD not used if installed, FPV available on one or both PFDs depending on the ADIRS standard.
Related procedures
  • UNRELIABLE SPEED INDICATION — Leads here below FL 250 when speed stays unreliable. See the Unreliable speed brief.
  • F/CTL ALTN LAW (PROT LOST) — Associated procedure. See the F/CTL ALTN LAW brief.
  • F/CTL DIRECT LAW — Control reverts to direct law at gear extension. See the F/CTL DIRECT LAW brief.
HS-TX differences
TopicHS-TXA..TXOHS-TXP..TXU
FMS after all ADRs offWHEN ALL ADR OFF BOTH FMS LOST · BACK UP NAV USE · USE RMP FOR NAVAID TUNINGNo such lines in the QRH ALL ADR OFF

ECAM procedure and STATUS: one version for all HS-TX. QRH ALL ADR OFF differs: HS-TXA..TXO also lose both FMS.

Gaps and omissions
  • "BAS" is not an abbreviation in the supplied manuals: the FCOM says Backup Altitude Scale and the PDP says Back-Up Altitude Scale.
  • PDP mentions a "reversible BUSS (if installed)". The FCOM states activation is not reversible for all HS-TX; the reversible modification is listed for HS-TO only. This brief follows the FCOM.
  • The flow order and PF/PM split of the QRH part are arranged from the QRH lines and AOP-30-30; no PDP slide gives the turns.
  • HS-TO versions omitted (FCOM P 41–42/124, QRH 26.01C).

Duct leak / pack overheat · FFS 9

3 procedures in this group — choose one

AIR L(R) WING LEAK

Amber caution Practised by Trainee B

An amber caution: an overheat is detected near the hot air ducts in one wing. Switch the affected engine bleed OFF, shut the crossbleed and switch wing anti-ice OFF, so the crew must avoid icing conditions. For a left wing leak, also switch the APU bleed OFF if it has not closed. The STATUS lists the engine bleed, the pack on that side and wing anti-ice as inoperative.

In FFS 9 Listed in the syllabus as "LEFT WING DUCT LEAK", at ETP, followed by PACK 2 OVHT.

Above 124 °C for the L(R) wing

SHUT
If severe ice accretion

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Both BMCs are operative and detect a temperature above 124 °C for the L(R) wing, or one BMC is failed and the other detects a temperature above 124 °C for the L(R) wing.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • Leak detection loops detect overheating near the hot air ducts. A wing has a double loop: a wing leak signal needs both loops, or one loop with the other inoperative.
  • A wing leak signal closes the bleed valve on the related side, turns on the FAULT light on the AIR COND panel and closes the x-bleed valve (except during an engine start). For a left wing leak, it also closes the APU bleed valve if open (except during an engine start).
  • If one BMC fails, the other still issues the wing leak warning, but the associated FAULT light is lost and the associated bleed valve does not close automatically.
Related procedures
  • AIR ENG 1+2 BLEED FAULT (LEFT LEAK) — A separate procedure when both engine bleed supply systems are lost with a left wing leak or a pylon leak on side 1.. If unsuccessful: DES TO FL 100/MEA-MORA; See the FCOM procedure.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCTM has no chapter for this alert and no PDP module covers it; the flow is the standard ECAM sequence.
  • The FCTM example of the overhead announcement is "AIR, XBLEED, CLOSE"; the ECAM line for this alert reads X BLEED SHUT. The flow does not quote an announcement for it.
  • The HS-TO version of this procedure (FCOM P 66–67/82) is not used.

AIR PACK 1(2) OVHT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee B

An amber caution: the pack compressor outlet is above 260 °C. Switch the affected pack OFF; high flow is automatically selected on the remaining pack. When the overheat clears, the FAULT light goes off and the pack can be switched back ON.

In FFS 9 After the left wing leak, pack 1 is already lost, so PACK 2 OFF leaves no pack until the overheat clears.

AIR PACK 1+2 FAULT

Amber caution Practised by Trainee B

An amber caution: neither pack is available. Switch both packs OFF and descend to FL 100 or MEA-MORA, whichever is higher. Below FL 100 with differential pressure under 1 PSI, switch RAM AIR ON (guarded, crosscheck first) and stay at or below FL 100/MEA-MORA. If the fault was due to an overheat, switch the affected pack back ON when the overheat clears.

In FFS 9 The last step after the left wing leak and PACK 2 OVHT. The manuals give no procedure for those two failures together, and this alert's trigger names both ACSCs failed (see Gaps).

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. Both ACSCs are failed.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • Each controller has two lanes. If both lanes fail, the related pack is lost and the hot air pressure-regulating valve closes.
  • RAM AIR pb (guarded): the emergency ram air inlet opens. If Δp ≥ 1 PSI, the outflow valve control remains normal and no emergency ram air flows in. If Δp < 1 PSI, the outflow valve opens to about 50 % under automatic control, and ram air goes directly to the mixer unit.
FCTM technique
  • ETOPS flights: in the case of loss of the air conditioning capability (loss of both packs, loss of both bleeds without APU bleed, etc.), when at FL 100 with the RAM AIR opened, the CAB FANS must be switched off.
Related procedures
  • AIR PACK 1(2) OVHT — Associated procedure if the fault was due to an overheat.. WHEN PACK OVHT OUT: PACK (AFFECTED) ON.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCOM trigger names only both ACSCs failed, but the procedure also has the branch "If FAULT was due to an overheat". The manuals do not state that this alert follows an AIR L(R) WING LEAK with an AIR PACK 1(2) OVHT. Confirmed by the user: show it as the third step of that sequence.
  • The FCOM note on closing the FWD CARGO ISOL VALVE is left out of the flow: the If Installed table lists the FWD ISOL Valve as not installed, and likewise FWD Cargo Heating, although STATUS prints FWD CRG HEAT.
  • The FCTM has no chapter for this alert and no PDP module covers it. Confirmed by the user: the PF flies the descent and the ECAM continues, with no STOP ECAM before STATUS.
  • The manuals name no role for the ETOPS CAB FANS line. Confirmed by the user: the PM.
  • The HS-TO version of this procedure (FCOM P 72–74/82) is not used.

Cargo smoke · FFS 9

2 procedures in this group — choose one

SMOKE AFT CARGO SMOKE

Red warningLAND ASAP (red) Practised by Trainee B

A red warning with red LAND ASAP. Smoke is detected in the aft cargo hold, which is built to contain a fire, so the smoke is not felt in the cockpit; only the SMOKE light on the CARGO SMOKE panel confirms it. Close the aft isolation valve if it did not close by itself, cabin fans OFF, discharge AGENT 1 (guarded pb, crosscheck first) and AGENT 2 after 60 min, and divert. Expect the warning to stay after discharge. On the ground, the passengers disembark before any cargo door is opened.

In FFS 9 The syllabus says only "Cargo smoke" and does not name the hold.

LAND ASAP
Red — nearest airport with a safe landing
AGENT 1
DISCH (bottle 1 empties in about 60 s)
AGENT 2
DISCH after 60 min
Cargo doors
Not opened before PAX DISEMBARK

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when smoke in the AFT cargo compartment is detected. Inhibited in flight phases 4, 5, 7 and 8.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • The cargo compartments are designed to be air-tight and fireproof to contain a fire, and the cargo ventilation prevents cargo smoke from reaching the cockpit/cabin. The crew can only confirm the alert with the SMOKE light on the CARGO SMOKE panel.
  • The aft compartment has four smoke detectors on two loops. The warning needs both detectors of a cavity (or one, if the other is inoperative). The isolation valves close and the extraction fan stops automatically.
  • The DISCH pb fires the squibs of the fire bottles: bottle 1 discharges in about 60 s; a flow metering system controls bottle 2 for at least 135 min. BTL 1(2) light amber when empty.
  • The DISCH sw is guarded. The DISCH AGENT 2 light comes on amber 60 min after AGENT 1 and goes off when the AGENT 2 squib is ignited.
FCTM technique
  • An immediate diversion should be considered as soon as smoke/fumes are detected. If the source is not immediately obvious, accessible and extinguishable, divert without delay.
  • Guarded controls are crosschecked by both pilots before acting in flight.
  • If smoke/fumes become perceptible in the cockpit or cabin, or any doubt exists about the smoke origin, apply the [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE — If any doubt exists about the smoke origin, or smoke/fumes are perceptible.. LAND ASAP; immediate actions; Diversion and descent to FL 100 / MEA-MORA if the source is not isolated; Boxed items at any time: REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, ELEC EMER CONFIG, immediate landing.
  • SMOKE DISCH AGENT 2 — Reminder 60 min after AGENT 1 when the cargo smoke alert has stopped.. AGENT 2 DISCH.
Gaps and omissions
  • "AFT/BULK CRG SMOKE" is not an HS-TX alert title; the THA FCOM gives SMOKE AFT CARGO SMOKE for all HS-TX.
  • The procedure does not call for an evacuation; it requires PAX DISEMBARK before opening the cargo doors.
  • FCOM note 1 (recovering aft cargo ventilation for livestock) applies only to aircraft with the AFT cargo ventilation option and is not used here.
  • No PDP module covers cargo smoke; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling.
  • The HS-TO version (FCOM P 34–36/50) is not used.

  19. WHEN ON GROUND BEFORE OPEN CRG DOORS:
  20. PAXDISEMBARK
  21. On ground, the warning may be triggered due to a high level of humidity or insecticide spraying. If the smoke is not visually confirmed and the warning is no more displayed: deactivate the smoke detection system (SDCU C/Bs), reset the cargo ventilation system (AIR COND/AFT CARGO/VENT/CTL & MONG C/B), and at cargo doors closure reactivate SDCU 1 and 2.

More detail

Background, technique and sources

What it is

Trigger. This alert triggers when smoke in the FWD cargo compartment is detected. Inhibited in flight phases 4, 5, 7 and 8.

Flight phase inhibition. Inhibited in phases 4, 5, 7, 8.

  • The cargo compartments are designed to be air-tight and fireproof to contain a fire, and the cargo ventilation prevents cargo smoke from reaching the cockpit/cabin. The crew can only confirm the alert with the SMOKE light on the CARGO SMOKE panel.
  • The forward compartment has two smoke detectors on two loops. The warning needs both detectors of a cavity (or one, if the other is inoperative).
  • The DISCH pb fires the squibs of the fire bottles: bottle 1 discharges in about 60 s; a flow metering system controls bottle 2 for at least 135 min. BTL 1(2) light amber when empty.
  • The DISCH sw is guarded. The DISCH AGENT 2 light comes on amber 60 min after AGENT 1 and goes off when the AGENT 2 squib is ignited.
FCTM technique
  • An immediate diversion should be considered as soon as smoke/fumes are detected. If the source is not immediately obvious, accessible and extinguishable, divert without delay.
  • Guarded controls are crosschecked by both pilots before acting in flight.
  • If smoke/fumes become perceptible in the cockpit or cabin, or any doubt exists about the smoke origin, apply the [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE procedure.
Related procedures
  • [QRH] SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE — If any doubt exists about the smoke origin, or smoke/fumes are perceptible.. LAND ASAP; immediate actions; Diversion and descent to FL 100 / MEA-MORA if the source is not isolated; Boxed items at any time: REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, ELEC EMER CONFIG, immediate landing.
  • SMOKE DISCH AGENT 2 — Reminder 60 min after AGENT 1 when the cargo smoke alert has stopped.. AGENT 2 DISCH.
Gaps and omissions
  • The FCOM procedure prints the line FWD ISOL VALVE OFF, marked "if installed". The If Installed table (GEN P 26/78) lists FWD Cargo Ventilation and the FWD ISOL Valve as not installed, while GEN P 14/78 lists the general "Cargo ventilation system / Cargo isolation valves" as installed. Confirmed by the user: the flow leaves the line out; the procedure section keeps it verbatim.
  • STATUS prints FWD CRG VENT and FWD CRG HEAT, also "if installed"; the same table lists them as not installed. They are kept verbatim.
  • The FCOM notes on recovering FWD cargo ventilation for livestock apply only to aircraft with FWD Cargo Ventilation and are not used here.
  • No PDP module covers cargo smoke; the flow uses the generic ECAM handling.
  • The HS-TO version (FCOM P 42–43/50) is not used.
